Off the heat, stir in lemon zest, juice, and parsley. Season.
Plate over pasta or rice. Spoon sauce.

notes: Lemon zest in both the meatballs and the sauce, double citrus.
Chicken thigh mince > chicken breast mince. The fat makes them stay juicy.

title: Chicken Milanese
summary: A thin parmesan and lemon-crumbed cutlet fried in butter, heaped with dressed rocket.

items.raw: 4 chicken breasts, butterflied and pounded to 5mm

steps.text: Pound the chicken to even 5mm thickness. Season heavily.
Set up three plates: flour, egg-milk, and breadcrumbs mixed with parmesan, oregano, and lemon zest.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then press hard into breadcrumbs.
Heat butter and oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat until foaming.
Swim the cutlets, fat should bubble around them. Cook 2 minutes a side, basting with the hot fat for that rippled golden crust. Drain on a rack.
Toss the rocket, tomatoes, shallot, and shaved parmesan with the olive oil, lemon, salt, and pepper.
Plate each cutlet with a heaped pile of dressed rocket on top. Lemon wedge on the side.

notes: Milanese = breaded escalope. The salad on top is non-negotiable in Italy.
Lemon zest in the crumb is the secret, perfumes the crust without overpowering.

title: Chicken Noodle Soup
summary: A whole-chicken broth with egg noodles and vegetables, brightened with lemon and dill.

items.raw: 1.2kg whole chicken (or 1kg bone-in thighs and drumsticks)
3 carrots, in chunks (use the trimmings for broth, save 2 carrots diced for the soup)
items.note: use the trimmings for broth, save 2 carrots diced for the soup

items.raw: 3 celery sticks, in chunks (reserve 2 sticks diced for soup)

steps.text: Put the chicken in a stockpot with the broth aromatics, salt, and water. Bring to a bare simmer (never a hard boil, it cloudies the broth). Skim any scum off the top for the first 20 minutes.
Simmer gently for 60 minutes. The chicken should be tender, the broth deeply yellow.
Lift the chicken out. When cool enough, shred the meat off the bones. Discard skin and bones.
Strain the broth through a fine sieve into a clean pot. Discard the vegetables.
Bring the broth to a simmer. Add the diced carrots, celery, and leek. Cook 8 minutes.
Add the noodles. Cook per packet, usually 5–7 minutes.
Fold in the shredded chicken. Finish with lemon juice, parsley, dill, salt, and pepper.
Ladle into bowls. Best with a slice of buttered toast on the side.

notes: Whole chicken makes the broth. Boneless breasts make sad soup.
Lemon at the end lifts everything. A pinch of dill is the secret.

title: Chicken Pad See Ew
summary: Wide rice noodles charred in the wok with chicken, egg, gai lan and dark soy.

items.raw: 300g fresh wide rice noodles (sen yai, Asian grocer)

items.item: baby gai lan or 200g Chinese broccoli
items.raw: 4 baby gai lan or 200g Chinese broccoli, in 6cm lengths

steps.text: Whisk all the sauce ingredients.
If the noodles are refrigerated and stuck together, gently separate them by hand, don't microwave or rinse.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat. Cook the chicken in a single layer 2 minutes a side. Lift out.
Heat 2 more tbsp oil. Add the garlic. Toss 20 seconds.
Push to the side. Pour in the eggs. Let them set 5 seconds, then scramble.
Add the gai lan stems first. Toss 90 seconds. Add the leaves; 30 seconds.
Add the noodles. Press them flat against the wok with the spatula to develop charred spots. Don't toss too much, pad see ew is about smoky char from the wok hei.
After 90 seconds, return the chicken. Pour the sauce around the edges. Toss for 60 seconds, every noodle glossy and brown.
Plate immediately.

notes: Char on the noodles. Press, don't toss. That smoky flavour is wok hei, the breath of the wok.
Fresh wide rice noodles only. Dried noodles cannot replicate the texture.

title: Chicken Parmesan
summary: Crumbed chicken breast baked under marinara and mozzarella, the crisp edges left showing.

items.raw: 500ml good marinara (or homemade simple tomato sauce)

steps.text: Pound the chicken breasts to even thickness. Season heavily.
Set up three dishes: flour, egg, and panko mixed with the parmesan, oregano, and garlic powder.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then press hard into the panko mix.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Fry the cutlets 3 minutes a side until deep golden. Lift onto a rack.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Spread a thin layer of marinara in a baking dish. Lay the cutlets in.
Spoon more sauce on top of each cutlet (leaving the edges of the breadcrumb crust showing, crucial for texture). Top with mozzarella slices and a scatter of parmesan.
Bake 12 minutes until the cheese is melted, blistered, and the sauce is bubbling.
Tear basil over the top. Serve with spaghetti (with the rest of the sauce) and salad.

notes: Don't drown the cutlet in sauce, the breadcrumb edges sticking out is what stops it going soggy.
Fresh basil at the end, never baked in.

title: Chicken Pesto Pasta
summary: Fresh basil pesto tossed off the heat with pasta, sliced chicken and cherry tomatoes.

steps.text: Pulse garlic, pine nuts, and salt in a food processor. Add basil; pulse to chop without pureeing. Tip into a bowl. Stir in parmesan, then olive oil.
Season chicken with oregano, salt, pepper. Sear in olive oil 4 minutes a side until golden. Rest 5 minutes; slice.
Cook pasta in well-salted water until al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water before draining.
In a wide bowl, toss hot pasta with pesto and 2 tbsp pasta water. Off the heat, never cook pesto, it kills the basil.
Fold in cherry tomatoes and sliced chicken. Add more pasta water if needed for glossy coat.
Plate. Scatter extra parmesan and a few basil leaves.

notes: Pesto over hot pasta, off the heat. Heated pesto goes dull green and bitter.
Reserved pasta water gives the sauce body.

title: Chicken Piccata
summary: Floured chicken escalopes in a lemon, caper and white wine pan sauce mounted with butter.

steps.text: Pat chicken dry. Season heavily. Dredge in flour and shake off excess.
Heat the oil and butter in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken 3 minutes a side until deeply golden. Lift onto a plate.
Pour the wine into the same pan. Scrape the base. Reduce by half.
Add the stock, lemon juice, and capers. Simmer 4 minutes until reduced to a glossy sauce.
Off the heat, swirl in the cold butter a cube at a time. Each cube emulsifies and silkens the sauce.
Return the chicken with any juices. Fold in parsley.
Plate with lemon slices on top. Spoon sauce generously. Serve with pasta or mash.

notes: Cold butter at the end is what makes the sauce restaurant-glossy.
Capers, lemon, butter, that's the trinity. Don't add cream or it stops being piccata.

title: Chicken Pot Pie
summary: Chicken, leek and mushroom in a creamy mustard sauce beneath a puff pastry lid.

steps.text: Season the chicken and brown in olive oil over high heat for 4 minutes. Lift out.
Reduce heat to medium. Melt the butter in the same pan. Add the leek, carrot, and celery. Cook 8 minutes until soft.
Add the mushrooms and garlic. Cook 5 minutes until the mushrooms release and reabsorb their liquid.
Stir in the flour. Cook 2 minutes, coats the vegetables in roux.
Whisk in the stock gradually so no lumps form. Stir in the cream, mustard, and thyme. Simmer 5 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Return the chicken with its juices. Add the peas. Simmer 5 more minutes. Season well, the filling should taste rich and slightly over-seasoned because the pastry is plain.
Tip into a pie dish. Cool 10 minutes, hot filling melts the pastry.
Lay the puff pastry over the dish, trim the edges, and crimp with a fork. Cut a small steam hole in the centre.
Brush with beaten egg. Bake at 200°C for 25–30 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the filling is bubbling around the edges.
Rest 5 minutes before serving.

notes: Cool the filling before laying the pastry on top, or it goes soggy underneath.
A single sheet of good butter puff is far better than scratch shortcrust here.

title: Chicken Quesadilla
summary: Chipotle chicken and melted cheese folded into crisp, golden flour tortillas.

items.raw: 1 chipotle in adobo, chopped (or 1 tsp smoked paprika + 1/2 tsp chilli powder)
items.note: or 1 tsp smoked paprika + 1/2 tsp chilli powder

steps.text: Cook the chicken with onion and capsicum in oil over high heat for 8 minutes. Stir in garlic, chipotle, cumin, and oregano. Cook 2 minutes. Finish with lime juice. Cool slightly.
On a tortilla, sprinkle cheese on half, then chicken, more cheese, jalapeño, coriander. Fold the other half over to make a half-moon.
Heat a dry pan over medium heat. Place the quesadilla in. Press lightly with a spatula. Cook 3 minutes a side until deeply golden and cheese is melted.
Rest 1 minute (lets cheese set so it doesn't spill). Cut into 3 wedges.
Repeat with the rest. Serve with sour cream, salsa, avocado, and lime.

notes: Dry pan, not oiled. Quesadilla skin should be papery and blistered.
Rest before cutting or molten cheese erupts.

title: Chicken Ramen Bowl
summary: Crisp-skinned chicken thigh over ramen in a shiitake broth seasoned with miso tare.

steps.text: Simmer broth ingredients gently for 25 minutes. Strain.
Score chicken skin shallowly. Season. Pan-sear skin-side-down in a dry pan for 7 minutes, then flip 4 minutes more. Skin should be crackling. Slice.
Whisk tare ingredients in each bowl.
Cook noodles per packet (2–4 minutes).
Pour 400ml hot strained broth into each bowl. Whisk to dissolve the tare.
Add noodles. Top with sliced chicken, egg halves, blanched greens, nori, spring onion, sesame, and chilli oil.

notes: Tare in the bowl, broth poured over. Same trick all ramen shops use.
Crackling chicken skin > soft chicken on top. Make sure the skin is crisp.

title: Chicken Satay
summary: Lemongrass and turmeric chicken skewers charred hot and served with peanut sauce.

items.raw: 2 stalks lemongrass, white only, finely chopped

steps.text: Blitz all marinade ingredients (except chicken) to a paste. Toss with the chicken. Rest 2+ hours.
Soak bamboo skewers. Thread 4 pieces of chicken per skewer, packed tight.
For the sauce: heat all ingredients in a small pan and simmer 5 minutes until thickened to a coating consistency. Loosen with water if needed.
Heat a grill plate to screaming hot. Cook the skewers 2 minutes per side for 8 minutes total, basting once with leftover marinade. The edges should char.
Plate with peanut sauce, cucumber, and rice. Lime on the side.

notes: Char is half the dish. Don't cook over moderate heat, you need flame.
Cucumber on the side isn't just garnish, it cools the spice.

title: Chicken Satay Bowl
summary: Charred lemongrass and turmeric chicken over rice with fresh vegetables and peanut sauce.

items.raw: 2 stalks lemongrass, white only, finely chopped

steps.text: Blitz all chicken marinade ingredients into a paste. Toss with chicken. Rest 1 hour.
Heat a grill plate to high. Cook chicken in single layer batches 3 minutes a side until charred.
For sauce: simmer all ingredients in a small pan 5 minutes until thick. Loosen with water if needed.
Build bowls: rice on the bottom. Arrange chicken in the centre, then cucumber, carrot, sprouts, onion around.
Drizzle peanut sauce generously. Scatter coriander, peanuts, lime.

notes: Skewer-less satay. All the marinade flavour without the skewering effort.
Peanut sauce is also great on tomorrow's tofu.

title: Chicken Schnitzel
summary: Thin parmesan-crumbed chicken fried in foaming butter until the crust puffs.

items.raw: 4 chicken breasts, butterflied and pounded to 5mm

steps.text: Pound the chicken between cling film to even 5mm thickness. Season heavily.
Set up flour, egg-milk, and breadcrumbs mixed with parmesan and oregano.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then press lightly into breadcrumb mix. Don't pack the crumbs hard.
Heat butter and oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat until the butter foams.
Swim the schnitzel, fat should bubble around it. Cook 2 minutes per side, basting with the hot fat using a spoon for the puffed crust.
Drain on a rack briefly. Serve immediately with lemon, potatoes, and salad.

notes: Pound thin and even. Cooks in 4 minutes total.
Basting with hot fat creates the signature wavy puffed breadcrumb crust.

title: Chicken Shawarma Bowl
summary: Warm-spiced roast chicken over turmeric rice with hummus, pickles and tahini.

items.raw: 2 cups basmati rice, cooked with a pinch of turmeric
items.prep: cooked with a pinch of turmeric

items.item: shredded red cabbage tossed with 1 tbsp red wine vinegar
items.raw: 1 cup shredded red cabbage tossed with 1 tbsp red wine vinegar
Tahini sauce (4 tbsp tahini + 4 tbsp water + 2 tbsp lemon + salt)
items.note: 4 tbsp tahini + 4 tbsp water + 2 tbsp lemon + salt

steps.text: Marinate the chicken with all listed spices, oil, lemon, and garlic. Rest 2+ hours.
Heat the oven to 220°C. Lay the chicken on a foil-lined tray. Roast 22 minutes until charred at the edges.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice into strips.
Build each bowl: turmeric rice on one side, chicken on top, then a smear of hummus on the other side. Arrange piles of cabbage, cucumber, tomato, onion, and pickles around the edges.
Drizzle tahini sauce in a zigzag. Dust with sumac. Scatter parsley. Lemon wedge on the side.

notes: Same flavour profile as a shawarma wrap, but in a bowl format, easier to make, eats well as meal prep.
Reheat the rice and chicken; serve everything else cold for that hot-cold contrast.

title: Chicken Shawarma Plate
summary: Warm-spiced roast chicken on saffron rice with hummus, salad, pickles and garlic sauce.

items.raw: Large pinch saffron in 2 tbsp hot water

steps.text: Marinate chicken 2+ hours.
For the rice: cook onion in ghee 5 minutes. Add rice; toast 1 minute. Add stock, saffron water, salt. Bring to boil, cover, reduce to lowest heat 15 minutes. Rest 10 minutes off heat.
Heat oven to 220°C. Roast chicken on a foil-lined tray 22 minutes until charred. Slice into strips.
Plate: a mound of saffron rice on one side, sliced chicken on top. Surround with tomato salad, pickles, hummus.
Drizzle tahini and garlic sauce. Stuff with pita pieces.

notes: Same chicken as shawarma wraps, different format, bigger meal.
Saffron rice is the bed. Buttery and fragrant.

title: Chicken Souvlaki
summary: Lemon and oregano chicken skewers charred and wrapped with tzatziki, salad and chips.

steps.text: Marinate the chicken with all listed ingredients. Rest 1 hour minimum.
Soak bamboo skewers (or use metal). Thread the chicken pieces tightly.
Whisk the tzatziki.
Heat a grill plate to high. Cook the skewers 3 minutes per side for 12 minutes total. The edges should char.
Warm the pita.
Build wraps: pita, tzatziki, salad pile, hot chips, chicken straight off the skewer, more tzatziki, feta crumble, lemon squeeze. Roll tight.

notes: Thighs over breast for souvlaki, they take the char without drying.
Chips in the wrap is the Greek way. Don't skip.

title: Chicken Stir Fry
summary: Velveted chicken thigh with crisp vegetables in a glossy soy and oyster sauce.

items.raw: 1 tbsp cornflour mixed with 3 tbsp water

steps.text: Marinate chicken 15 minutes.
Mix sauce ingredients.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in wok over high heat. Cook chicken in a single layer 3 minutes. Lift out.
Add 1 tbsp oil. Stir-fry broccoli 90 seconds with a splash of water to steam through.
Add capsicum, carrot, sugar snaps. Toss 2 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger; 30 seconds.
Return chicken. Pour sauce around edges. Toss 60 seconds until glossy.
Off the heat, fold in spring onions.
Plate over rice. Sesame on top.

notes: Hardest veg first, softest last. Order matters in a stir-fry.
Get the wok screaming hot. Wok hei is the difference between great and meh.

title: Chicken Tagine
summary: Chicken simmered with saffron and warm spices, sharpened by preserved lemon and olives.

items.raw: Pinch saffron in 2 tbsp hot water
1 preserved lemon, pulp scraped, rind sliced

steps.text: Brown the chicken in 2 tbsp oil over medium-high in batches. Set aside.
Reduce heat. Add remaining oil. Cook onions 10 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, and ground spices. Stir 1 minute.
Pour in saffron water and stock. Return chicken. Tuck in the preserved lemon rind and most olives.
Cover and simmer on lowest heat 60 minutes, fall-off-the-bone tender.
Lid off for the last 10 minutes if the sauce needs body.
Off the heat, scatter remaining olives, coriander, parsley.
Serve over couscous with flatbread.

notes: Preserved lemon, find at any Middle Eastern grocer. It's what makes this dish.
No sweet element here (unlike lamb tagine), preserved lemon and olive carry it.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
summary: Crisp-skinned thighs glazed in the pan with soy, mirin and sake until sticky.

steps.text: Combine the sauce ingredients in a small bowl and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Pat the chicken dry. Season lightly with salt.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Place the chicken skin-side down and press it flat with a spatula. Cook 7–8 minutes without moving, the skin should be deeply golden and crisp.
Flip and cook another 4 minutes until almost cooked through.

Drain any excess fat. Pour in the sauce. It will bubble up immediately. Tilt the pan and baste the chicken constantly with a spoon for 2–3 minutes until the sauce thickens to a syrup and clings to the chicken.
Rest on a board for 2 minutes, then slice across the grain. Fan over rice, spoon the pan sauce on top, scatter spring onion and sesame seeds.

notes: Thighs only, breast goes dry before the glaze sets.
Real teriyaki is glaze-pan, not marinade-in-a-bag. The sticky surface comes from reducing in the pan at the end.

title: Chicken Tikka
summary: Yoghurt-marinated thigh pieces roasted on skewers and charred under the grill.

items.item: Sliced onion with lemon and chaat masala
items.raw: Sliced onion with lemon and chaat masala

steps.text: Combine all marinade ingredients with the chicken. Massage thoroughly. Rest at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Soak bamboo skewers (or use metal). Thread the chicken pieces leaving small gaps for char.
Heat the oven to 240°C with a rack in the top third. Line a tray with foil and set a rack inside.
Arrange the skewers on the rack. Roast 12 minutes, turning once, until the edges char.
Finish under a hot grill (broiler) for 2 minutes per side for proper tandoor-style char.
Rest 3 minutes. Serve with mint chutney, sliced onions, and naan.

notes: Bone-out thighs only. Breast goes dry; bone-in is too slow on skewers.
Overnight marinade, yogurt enzymes tenderise and the spices penetrate properly.

title: Chicken Wings
summary: Oven wings dried with baking powder until crackling, tossed in a honey soy glaze.

items.raw: 1.2kg chicken wings, split into drumettes and flats
1 tbsp baking powder (not baking soda, this is the crispness secret)
items.note: not baking soda, this is the crispness secret

steps.text: Pat the wings completely dry, bone dry is critical. The baking powder trick only works on dry skin.

Toss the wings with baking powder, salt, garlic powder, and pepper until evenly coated. Lay on a rack over a tray. Refrigerate uncovered for at least 1 hour, ideally overnight, this dries the skin further.
Heat the oven to 220°C. Roast on the rack for 40–45 minutes, flipping once, until deep mahogany and crackling.
While they cook, combine the glaze ingredients (except sesame and spring onion) in a small pan. Simmer 4 minutes until syrupy.
When the wings are done, tip into a wide bowl. Pour the glaze over and toss to coat every piece.
Pile on a platter. Top with sesame seeds and spring onion.

notes: Baking powder + dry skin + overnight rest = oven wings that out-crisp deep-fried.
Toss in glaze AFTER cooking. Glazing before burns the sugar.

title: Chicken Wrap
summary: Charred spiced chicken rolled with a yoghurt dill sauce, salad, feta and herbs.

steps.text: Marinate chicken with all listed ingredients. Rest 15 minutes.
Whisk the yogurt sauce.
Heat a heavy pan over high heat. Cook the chicken in batches in a single layer for 3 minutes a side until charred at the edges.
Warm tortillas briefly.
Smear sauce on each. Layer lettuce, chicken, tomato, cucumber, onion, feta, herbs, pickled chilli.
Fold bottom up, sides in, roll tight. Cut in half if you like.
Optional: toast each wrap seam-down in a dry pan for 90 seconds to seal.

notes: High heat for the chicken or it steams. Char is the point.
Sauce on the tortilla first, then build. Wet stuff in the middle, drier on the edges.

title: Chicken Yakitori
summary: Chicken and spring onion skewers grilled and brushed with layer upon layer of tare.

items.raw: 8 spring onions, white parts in 3cm lengths

steps.text: Combine tare ingredients in a small pan. Simmer 5 minutes until reduced by a third and syrupy. Discard garlic and ginger.
Soak bamboo skewers (or use metal). Thread chicken alternating with spring onion whites, packed tight.
Heat a grill plate or BBQ to high. Cook skewers 2 minutes a side without glaze, get a base of colour.
Brush heavily with tare. Cook another minute a side. Brush again. Repeat 2–3 times, building layers of sticky glaze.
Final brush as they come off the grill. Scatter sesame.
Serve with shichimi for those who want spice, over rice.

notes: Layer the glaze in coats. Brushing once gives one coat of flavour; brushing four times gives depth.
Spring onions are essential, they char and soften and balance the rich chicken.

title: Chili Cheese Fries
summary: Crisp fries under a quick beef and bean chilli and melted cheese.

items.raw: 1.2kg frozen straight-cut fries (or homemade, peeled, cut, oil-tossed)

steps.text: Cook fries per packet at 220°C until deep golden and crisp (toss with oil and salt if not pre-coated). Or homemade: 220°C for 30 minutes, tossing halfway.

For the chili: brown the mince in oil for 6 minutes. Add onion; cook 5 minutes. Add garlic and spices; cook 1 minute. Add tomato paste; cook 2 minutes. Add tomatoes, beans, stock. Simmer 15 minutes until thick. Season.
On an oven-safe platter, pile the hot fries. Spoon chili over generously (leave some fries showing).
Scatter cheese over the chili and fries. Pop under a grill for 2 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Top with spring onion, jalapeños, sour cream zigzag, coriander, hot sauce.
Eat with your hands and lots of napkins.

notes: Two fry layers if you really want to commit, fries, chili, cheese, more fries on top, more chili and cheese, melt.
Don't drown the fries. Some bare crispy fries are part of the joy.

title: Chili Con Carne
summary: Cubed chuck simmered for hours with dried chillies, beer and a square of chocolate.

items.raw: 2 × 400g tins kidney or pinto beans, drained

steps.text: Toast the dried chillies in a dry pan for 30 seconds, then soak in boiling water 15 minutes. Drain and blend with a splash of soaking water until smooth.
Pat the beef dry, season heavily, and brown in oil over high heat in batches, don't crowd. Set aside.
In the same pot, soften the onions for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, paprika, oregano, and cinnamon. Cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes. Add the chilli puree and cook 2 minutes more.
Return the beef. Add the tomatoes, stock, beer, and the chocolate.
Simmer on the lowest heat, partially covered, for 2 hours. Stir every 30 minutes. The beef should be falling apart and the sauce thick and glossy.
In the last 15 minutes, stir in the beans. Finish with lime juice. Season, chili needs more salt than you'd expect.
Rest 15 minutes before serving. Top each bowl with sour cream, cheese, spring onion, coriander.

notes: Cubed chuck beats mince for a reason, those tender pieces of beef in a thick sauce is the dish.
Texas purists no beans. I'm not Texan. Beans stay.

title: Chili Garlic Noodles
summary: Thick wheat noodles tossed in sizzled garlic oil, black vinegar and Sichuan chilli oil.

items.raw: 2 tbsp Chinkiang black vinegar (or rice vinegar)
1 tbsp Sichuan chilli oil (with crispy bits)
1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
300g fresh thick wheat noodles (or 200g dried udon-style)
1/2 cup blanched bok choy or spinach

steps.text: Whisk all sauce ingredients in a wide serving bowl. Set aside.
Cook the noodles in unsalted boiling water per packet. Drain (don't rinse).
Heat the oil in a small pan until shimmering. Off the heat, add the minced garlic, it will sizzle and turn golden in the residual heat (this is way more flavour than raw or burned garlic).
Tip the warm garlic oil straight into the sauce bowl. Whisk.
Add the hot noodles to the bowl. Toss vigorously to coat every strand.
Top with spring onions, blanched greens, sesame, and coriander.
Eat immediately while warm. Toss again at the table to redistribute the sauce.

notes: Sizzling oil over raw garlic is the technique. Cooks it without burning, gives the sauce its body.
No protein needed, these stand on their own. Add a soft-boiled egg if you want.

title: Chow Mein
summary: Egg noodles left to crisp in a hot wok, tossed with chicken, vegetables and soy.

items.raw: 300g chicken thigh, sliced (or beef or prawns)

steps.text: Whisk all sauce ingredients.
Cook the noodles per packet. Drain, rinse under cold water briefly, and toss with 1 tbsp oil to stop them sticking.
Heat a wok over high heat until smoking. Add 1 tbsp oil. Cook the chicken in a single layer for 3 minutes until just done. Lift out.
Add the remaining oil. Stir-fry the garlic and ginger 20 seconds.
Add the carrot and capsicum. Toss 90 seconds.
Add the noodles. Spread them across the wok and let them sit for 30 seconds to develop crispy edges. Then toss for another 90 seconds.
Return the chicken. Add the sauce around the edges. Toss vigorously for 60 seconds, every strand should be glossy brown.
Off the heat, fold in the bean sprouts and spring onions. Toss 20 seconds, keep them crisp.
Tip onto plates immediately.

notes: Crispy edges on the noodles come from letting them sit in a hot wok. Don't toss constantly.
Sprouts at the end, they should still crunch.

title: Chowder
summary: A creamy corn and potato chowder with bacon, half-blended for body.

items.raw: 500g corn kernels (frozen or fresh from 4 cobs)

steps.text: Render the bacon in a heavy pot over medium heat until crisp. Lift out.
Add the butter, then the onion, celery, and carrot. Cook 8 minutes until soft. Add garlic; cook 1 minute.
Sprinkle in the flour. Cook 2 minutes.
Whisk in the milk gradually. Add the stock, potatoes, bay, and thyme. Simmer 12 minutes until potatoes are just tender.
Add the corn. Simmer 5 minutes.
Take out 2 cups of soup, blend smooth, return to the pot, this thickens without losing texture.
Stir in the cream. Warm through gently, never boil after the cream goes in.
Season. Top with crispy bacon, spring onion, and hot sauce.

notes: Half-blend the soup. Full blend = baby food. No blend = thin. Half = perfect.
Sweet summer corn makes the dish. Frozen works year-round.

title: Clam Chowder
summary: A creamy New England chowder of clams, potato and bacon, gently warmed through.

items.raw: 1kg fresh clams (or 2 × 400g tins clams in juice)
250ml water (for steaming fresh clams; skip if using tinned)
items.note: for steaming fresh clams; skip if using tinned

items.item: Oyster crackers or warm crusty bread
items.raw: Oyster crackers or warm crusty bread

steps.text: If using fresh clams: scrub under cold water. Discard any with cracked shells or ones that won't close when tapped. Steam in a covered pot with 250ml water until they open, 3–5 minutes. Strain the liquor through a coffee filter or fine cloth, reserve. Pull the meat from most shells; chop coarsely. Keep a few in shell for garnish. If tinned: drain and reserve juice; chop the clams.
In a heavy pot, render the bacon over medium heat until crisp. Lift out, leaving the fat.
Add the butter, then the onion and celery. Cook 8 minutes until soft, not coloured.
Sprinkle in the flour. Cook 2 minutes, make a blonde roux.
Whisk in the clam liquor (about 400ml total, top up with fish stock if needed). Cook 2 minutes until smooth.
Add the potatoes, bay leaves, thyme, and milk. Simmer 12 minutes until potatoes are tender but holding shape.
Stir in the cream and the chopped clams. Warm through gently, never boil after the clams go in or they go rubbery. 4 minutes.
Add the sherry, half the bacon, salt, and white pepper. Taste.
Ladle into deep bowls. Top with reserved bacon, parsley, and a few clams in shell for show. Crackers or bread on the side.

notes: Never boil after the clams are in. Gentle warmth only.
New England style is creamy. Manhattan style is tomato-based and a completely different dish, pick a side.

title: Club Sandwich
summary: A three-tier toasted sandwich of chicken, bacon, lettuce and tomato, cut into quarters.

items.raw: 2 chicken breasts, poached and sliced (or rotisserie chicken)
4 leaves crisp iceberg or butter lettuce

steps.text: Toast all 6 slices of bread to a deep gold.
Mix the mayo and mustard.
Build the first layer: bottom slice → mayo → lettuce → tomato (salt and pepper) → bacon → middle slice (both sides spread with mayo).
Build the second layer on top: mayo → lettuce → chicken → cheese → egg if using → top slice (mayo-side-down).
Press gently. Insert 4 cocktail picks evenly spaced through the entire sandwich.
Cut diagonally twice to make 4 triangles, with one pick through each triangle holding everything in place.
Serve with pickles and crisps.

notes: Three-layer is non-negotiable. Two layers makes it a BLT, not a club.
The cocktail picks aren't for show, they hold the tower together for the cut.

title: Cobb Salad
summary: Chicken, bacon, egg, avocado and blue cheese laid out in stripes with a sharp dressing.

items.raw: 2 chicken breasts, poached and shredded (or 2 cups rotisserie chicken)
6 rashers bacon, fried crisp and crumbled

steps.text: For perfect hard-boiled eggs: lower fridge-cold eggs into boiling water. Cook 9 minutes. Plunge into iced water for 5 minutes. Peel.
Poach the chicken: cover the breasts in cold seasoned water, bring to a bare simmer, then turn off the heat and cover. Rest 15 minutes. Shred.
Whisk the dressing ingredients. Taste, should be sharp.
On a wide flat platter, lay down the shredded lettuce as a bed.
Arrange everything else in distinct stripes across the top: a row of chicken, a row of bacon, a row of egg, a row of avocado, a row of tomatoes, a row of blue cheese.
Scatter chives over the top.
Bring to the table looking beautiful. Drizzle dressing across just before serving, then toss at the table.

notes: The stripes are the dish. Toss it up at the start and you just have salad.
Blue cheese is non-negotiable in a Cobb. Substitute with feta only if you must.

title: Coq au Vin
summary: Chicken marinated overnight in red wine and braised with bacon, mushrooms and onions.

items.raw: 1.5kg chicken pieces (legs and thighs, bone-in skin-on)

items.item: dry red burgundy or pinot noir
items.raw: 750ml dry red burgundy or pinot noir

steps.text: A day ahead: combine the chicken with the marinade ingredients. Refrigerate overnight.
Drain the chicken (strain and reserve the wine; discard the veg). Pat the chicken bone-dry.
In a Dutch oven, render the bacon in the olive oil until crisp. Lift out.
Brown the chicken in the bacon fat, skin-side first, for 5 minutes a side. Lift out.
Add the pearl onions and mushrooms. Brown for 5 minutes. Lift out.
Sprinkle the flour into the pot. Whisk for 1 minute. Pour in the reserved wine and the stock, whisking. Add the tomato paste.
Return the chicken (skin-side-up) and bacon. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and bake at 160°C for 60 minutes. Add the onions and mushrooms; cook another 30 minutes uncovered. The chicken should be falling-tender, the sauce reduced by a third.
Lift the chicken and vegetables onto a plate. Bring the sauce to a hard boil for 5 minutes if it needs more body. Whisk in the cold butter to mount.
Return everything to the pot. Scatter with parsley. Serve with mashed potato or crusty bread.

notes: A bottle of decent wine. Cooking wine = cooking sadness. Drink what's left.
Overnight marinade is traditional and worth the planning, the wine penetrates the meat.

title: Cottage Pie
summary: Beef mince in a rich red wine gravy under a forked, golden potato crust.

steps.text: Boil potatoes in salted water until very tender, 18 minutes.
Brown the mince in oil over high heat for 6 minutes. Drain excess fat. Add onion, carrot, celery; cook 8 minutes. Add garlic; cook 1 minute.
Stir in tomato paste and flour; cook 2 minutes. Add wine; reduce by half. Add stock, Worcestershire, thyme. Simmer 15 minutes until thick.
Stir in peas. Season. Tip into a baking dish.
Drain potatoes. Mash with butter and milk until smooth. Season.
Spread mash over the filling. Drag a fork across the surface to rough it up (those peaks crisp in the oven).
Scatter cheese if using.
Bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until deeply golden on top and bubbling at the edges.
Rest 5 minutes before serving.

notes: Cottage pie = beef. Shepherd's pie = lamb. Don't mix them up.
Fork-rough the mash. Smooth top = pale top. Peaks = crispy peaks.

title: Couscous
summary: Buttery couscous tossed with herbs, nuts, apricot, feta and lemon.

items.raw: Small handful pistachios or toasted almonds, chopped

steps.text: Place the couscous in a wide bowl with the olive oil, salt, and butter cubes.
Pour over the hot stock. Stir once, cover with cling film or a plate, and rest 8 minutes.
Fluff with a fork, break up every lump. The grains should be light and separate.
Tip into a wide serving bowl. Add the onion, cucumber, tomatoes, nuts, apricots, herbs, lemon zest and juice, and extra olive oil. Toss gently.
Crumble feta over the top. Crack pepper. Taste, adjust salt or lemon.
Serve warm or at room temperature, alongside tagine, grilled meats, or as a standalone lunch.

notes: The butter cubes melt into the steaming couscous, that's how to get rich, glossy grains without any frying.
Plenty of fresh herbs is what makes couscous interesting. Don't skimp.

title: Crispy Duck Pancakes
summary: Five-spice duck legs roasted until crackling, shredded and rolled in pancakes with hoisin.

items.raw: 6 spring onions, white parts in thin strips

steps.text: Pat the duck legs very dry. Score the skin in a crosshatch, 5mm deep, without cutting the meat.
Mix salt, five-spice, sugar, and Sichuan pepper. Rub all over the duck. Sit on a rack over a tray and refrigerate uncovered overnight, this dries the skin, the key to crackling.
The next day: rinse the duck briefly and pat dry. Heat the oven to 180°C.
Place the duck skin-side-up on a rack over a foil-lined tray. Roast 2 hours.
Crank the oven to 220°C for the final 15–20 minutes, the skin should turn deep mahogany and crackling crisp. Listen for it singing.
Rest 10 minutes. Shred the meat with two forks, keeping pieces of crispy skin distributed through.
Steam the pancakes per packet.
Serve on a platter: shredded duck (with crispy skin), pancakes, hoisin, cucumber, and spring onion. Each diner builds their own, smear of hoisin, duck, veg, roll up.

notes: Overnight dry-rub-in-the-fridge is non-negotiable. Wet duck doesn't crisp.
Two cooks: low to render the fat, high to crisp the skin.

title: Croque Monsieur
summary: Ham and Gruyère toasted, blanketed in béchamel and grilled until blistered.

items.item: thick slices of good white sourdough or pain de mie
items.raw: 4 thick slices of good white sourdough or pain de mie
4 thick slices Paris ham (or any good cooked ham)

steps.text: Melt the butter for the bechamel. Whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes, keep it pale.
Whisk in the warm milk gradually. Cook 5 minutes until thick. Off the heat, stir in the mustard, nutmeg, salt, pepper, and Gruyère. The sauce should be very thick.
Lightly butter the slices of bread on one side.
Lay 2 slices butter-side-down. Smear a thin layer of bechamel, then a sprinkle of Gruyère, then 2 slices of ham, more cheese, and top with the second slice of bread (butter-side-up).
Toast in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes a side until golden and the cheese is starting to melt.
Transfer to a tray. Spoon the rest of the bechamel over the top of each sandwich. Scatter the remaining Gruyère heavily over the bechamel.
Grill (broil) on high until the top is blistered, deeply golden, and bubbling, about 3 minutes. Watch it.
Rest 1 minute before eating. For a Croque Madame, top with a fried egg.

notes: A thick bechamel is non-negotiable, runny sauce makes soggy bread.
Don't skip the buttered toast step before the broiler. That gives you the layered crunch.

title: Dhal
summary: Soft red lentils finished at the table with a sizzling tadka of spices and curry leaves.

items.raw: Pinch of curry leaves (10–12 if you can find them)

steps.text: In a pot, combine the lentils, water, turmeric, and salt. Bring to a boil and skim any foam.
Add the diced onion, tomato, and ginger. Reduce to a simmer and cook 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils have broken down into a soft porridge. Add water if it gets too thick.
Whisk the dhal smooth with a wooden spoon or stick blender. Season.
For the tadka: heat the ghee in a small pan. Add cumin and mustard seeds. When they pop, add the dried chilli and asafoetida.
Add the sliced onion. Fry 6 minutes until deep golden.
Add the garlic and curry leaves. Cook 30 seconds, careful, they spit.
Off the heat, stir in the Kashmiri chilli powder and garam masala, the residual heat blooms them without burning.
Pour the entire sizzling tadka into the cooked dhal. Squeeze in the lemon. Stir once.
Top with coriander and fresh chilli. Serve with rice or naan.

notes: The tadka is the whole personality of the dhal. Pour it in at the table for theatre, it sizzles.
Curry leaves transform dhal. If you can find them fresh, get a bunch and freeze for next time.

title: Dim Sum
summary: Steamed pork and prawn siu mai with a black vinegar and ginger dipping sauce.

items.raw: 400g pork mince (not too lean, fat is good)
items.note: not too lean, fat is good

items.raw: 200g raw prawns, peeled and chopped fine
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and finely chopped

items.item: round wonton or siu mai wrappers
items.raw: 30 round wonton or siu mai wrappers

items.item: finely diced carrot for the tops
items.raw: 1 tbsp finely diced carrot for the tops

steps.text: In a bowl, combine the pork, prawn, mushroom, water chestnut, spring onion, ginger, soy, wine, oyster sauce, sesame oil, sugar, cornflour, and white pepper. Mix in one direction for 3 minutes, this is critical, it develops the springy texture.
Hold a wrapper in your palm. Spoon a heaped tablespoon of filling into the centre.
Cup the wrapper around the filling, letting it pleat naturally around the sides. Flatten the top slightly. Sit it on the bench so it stands like a barrel.
Dot the top of each siu mai with a few specks of diced carrot.
Line a steamer with baking paper (poked with holes) or cabbage leaves. Arrange the dumplings with 1cm between each.
Steam over rapidly boiling water for 10–12 minutes until firm to the touch.
Whisk the dipping sauce. Serve hot from the steamer.

notes: Mix the filling in ONE direction for several minutes, that's how dumpling houses get that springy, bouncy texture.
A real dim sum spread has many items. Siu mai is the gateway dim sum to make at home, once you can do these, you can do har gow, char siu bao, the lot.

title: Eggplant Parmesan
summary: Crumbed, fried eggplant layered with tomato sauce, mozzarella and parmesan, then baked.

steps.text: Salt the eggplant slices and rest in a colander 30 minutes. Pat dry, this is the difference between meaty and oily eggplant.
For the sauce: warm the olive oil with garlic and chilli for 2 minutes. Add tomato paste; cook 1 minute. Add passata, sugar, and basil. Simmer 15 minutes. Season.
Set up three dishes: flour, egg, panko mixed with parmesan and oregano.
Dredge each eggplant slice in flour, dip in egg, then press into panko mix.
Heat 5mm of oil in a wide pan. Fry the slices in batches for 2 minutes a side until deep golden. Drain on a rack.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Spread a thin layer of sauce in a baking dish.
Layer: eggplant in a single layer, scatter mozzarella and parmesan, drizzle sauce. Repeat 3 layers, finishing with cheese and sauce.
Bake 25–30 minutes until bubbling and the top is deep golden in spots.
Rest 10 minutes, essential. The layers need to set.
Tear basil over the top.

notes: Salt and rest the eggplant. Skipping makes a wet, bitter dish.
Rest before cutting. A piping-hot eggplant parm collapses.

title: Empanadas
summary: Flaky baked pastries filled Argentine-style with spiced beef, egg, olives and raisins.

items.raw: 1 egg yolk, beaten with 1 tsp water

steps.text: Rub the cold butter into the flour and salt until it looks like coarse breadcrumbs. Mix the egg, water, and vinegar; pour in and bring together into a soft dough. Wrap and rest 1 hour in the fridge.
Brown the beef in olive oil over high heat. Add the onion and capsicum; cook 8 minutes. Add the garlic and spices; cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the stock. Simmer 5 minutes until almost dry, wet filling tears the pastry.
Off the heat, fold in the chopped egg, olives, and raisins. Season. Cool completely.
Roll the dough to 3mm. Cut 12cm circles.
Spoon a heaped tablespoon of filling onto each circle. Brush the rim with egg wash. Fold in half and seal by pressing with a fork or by making a rope crimp (repulgue) along the edge.
Brush each empanada with egg wash and sprinkle with flaky salt.
Bake at 200°C for 22–25 minutes until deep golden.
Rest 5 minutes, the filling is molten. Serve hot.

notes: Cool filling is the secret. Hot filling melts the butter in the pastry and ruins the texture.
Egg + olive + raisin in the filling is classic Argentine. Once you try it, you'll understand why.

title: Enchiladas
summary: Chicken-filled corn tortillas dipped in a dried chilli sauce and baked with cheese.

items.raw: 4 dried guajillo chillies, stems and seeds removed
2 dried ancho chillies, stems and seeds removed

steps.text: Toast the dried chillies in a dry pan over medium heat for 30 seconds a side until pliable and aromatic. Soak in just-boiled water for 15 minutes to soften.
Drain the chillies. Blend with the oil, onion, garlic, cumin, oregano, and 250ml stock until smooth.
Tip the puree into a pan and simmer 8 minutes until darkened. Loosen with the remaining stock to a pourable sauce. Season.
Combine chicken, onion, coriander, salt, and the 150g cheese.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Spread a ladle of sauce in the base of a baking dish.
Warm each tortilla briefly in a dry pan or microwave (15 seconds), cold tortillas crack. Dip each tortilla into the warm sauce, then place on a board.
Spoon filling along the centre and roll up. Lay seam-down in the dish, tight together. Repeat with all tortillas.
Pour the rest of the sauce over the top. Scatter with the 200g cheese.
Bake 22 minutes until bubbling and the cheese is golden in spots.
Top with crumbled feta, red onion, coriander, and a drizzle of sour cream.

notes: Dried chillies do the heavy lifting. Tinned enchilada sauce is fine but not the same dish.
Sauce the tortillas, not just the top of the dish, that's the difference between enchiladas and a casserole.

title: Fajitas
summary: Charred skirt steak and capsicum brought sizzling to the table with warm tortillas.

items.raw: 700g skirt or flank steak (or chicken thigh)

steps.text: Mix the marinade. Coat the steak in half and the vegetables (separately) in the other half. Rest 30 minutes.
Heat a cast iron pan over high heat until it's smoking.
Drop the steak in. Cook 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare on skirt steak (it should char heavily). Rest on a board.
In the same pan, sear the vegetables in batches. You want char on the edges and crunch left in the middle, keep moving, 4 minutes max.
Slice the steak against the grain in thin strips.
Bring everything to the table on the hot pan, sizzling. Let people build their own with tortilla, steak, veg, avocado, salsa, sour cream, lime, coriander.

notes: Skirt or flank, cuts that need a hot, fast cook and cross-grain slicing.
The sizzle when the pan hits the table is half the point. Heat the pan until you can't hold a hand above it.

title: Falafel Salad
summary: Halved falafel over a crisp salad with feta and olives, finished with tahini and sumac.

steps.text: Heat the falafel: oven at 200°C for 10 minutes, or shallow-fry in oil for 2 minutes per side.
Whisk the tahini dressing, start thick, add water gradually. Should be pourable but creamy.
On a wide platter, layer the lettuce, then tomato, cucumber, onion, cherry tomatoes, olives, feta, and herbs.
Cut each falafel in half and scatter over the top, exposed centres soak up the dressing.
Drizzle with tahini dressing. Dust with sumac. Crack black pepper.
Serve with warm pita on the side for scooping.

notes: Halve the falafel, the crumbly inside catches the dressing.
Make-ahead salad bowl: dress at the table or it goes soggy.

title: Falafel Wrap
summary: Crisp herb falafel from soaked dried chickpeas, wrapped with tahini and pickles.

items.raw: 250g dried chickpeas (not tinned), soaked overnight in cold water
Small bunch of parsley, leaves and stems
Small bunch of coriander, leaves and stems

steps.text: Drain the soaked chickpeas thoroughly. They should be plump but still raw, do not boil them.

Tip the chickpeas into a food processor with the onion, garlic, herbs, cumin, coriander, salt, baking powder, and flour. Pulse to a coarse meal, like wet sand, not a paste. Scrape the sides as you go.
Squeeze a handful, it should just hold together. If it crumbles, pulse a touch more. Rest the mix 20 minutes.
Whisk the tahini sauce ingredients. It will seize, then loosen as you add more water. Aim for thick pouring consistency.
Roll the mix into walnut-sized balls and flatten slightly into patties.
Heat 2cm of oil in a deep pan to 170°C (a small piece of falafel mix should sizzle steadily). Fry in batches for 3–4 minutes, turning, until deep brown and crisp. Drain on paper.
Warm the flatbreads briefly in a dry pan. Spread with tahini, layer in lettuce, tomato, cucumber, onion, pickles, then 3 falafels per wrap. Drizzle more tahini, add hot sauce, and roll tight.

notes: Tinned chickpeas hold too much water, they'll fall apart in oil. Dried only.
Make a double batch and freeze the uncooked patties on a tray; fry straight from frozen.

title: Feijoada
summary: Black beans slow-cooked with pork belly, sausage and beef, served with rice and farofa.

items.raw: 300g salt pork or pancetta, in pieces
Sautéed kale or collard greens (couve à mineira)

steps.text: Drain the beans. Cover with fresh water in a large pot. Bring to a boil and simmer 30 minutes (don't fully cook).
In a separate Dutch oven, brown the pork belly in batches. Lift out.
Brown the beef in the same pot. Lift out.
Brown the sausage. Lift out.
Cook the onion in the rendered fat for 8 minutes. Add garlic and cumin; cook 1 minute.
Return all the meats. Add the partially cooked beans with their water, plus enough fresh water to cover by 2cm. Add the bay leaves and salt pork.
Simmer on low, partially covered, for 2.5 hours. Stir every 30 minutes. The beans should be very soft and the broth should thicken to a deep mahogany.
Pull out a cup of beans, mash, and stir back in, this is how you get the silky, near-black sauce.
Finish with orange juice and zest, salt, and pepper.
Serve over rice with farofa scattered on top, kale on the side, orange slices to cut the richness, and hot sauce.

notes: The condiment plate is half the dish: farofa for crunch, kale for green, orange for brightness.
Pork belly + sausage + salt pork is the holy trinity of meats. Use at least three different cuts.

title: Fish and Chips
summary: Cold beer-battered fish and twice-fried chips, crisp and light.

items.item: large fillets of firm white fish
items.raw: 2 large fillets of firm white fish (flathead, snapper, barramundi, or cod)
150g plain flour, plus extra for dusting

steps.text: Cut the potatoes into chunky chips, 1.5cm thick. Soak in cold water 20 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry.
Heat the oil to 150°C. First fry the chips for 6–7 minutes until soft but pale. Drain on a rack and rest.
Whisk the flours, baking powder, and salt. Pour in the cold beer just before frying, whisk only until just combined, lumps are fine. Cold + barely mixed = light, crisp batter.
Bring the oil up to 190°C. Pat the fish dry, dust lightly in plain flour, then drop into the batter.
Lift each fillet by the tail and lower halfway into the oil for 3 seconds before releasing, this sets the shape. Fry 5–7 minutes until deep golden and crisp. Drain on a rack.
While the fish drains, give the chips a second fry at 190°C for 3–4 minutes until properly golden and crackling. Salt immediately.
Serve fish on top of the chips with lemon and tartar. Vinegar on the chips if you're a purist.

notes: Two fries make the chips. Skip the first and you'll have soggy potato sticks.
Beer batter must be cold and barely mixed. Whisking it smooth makes it tough.

title: Fish Curry
summary: Firm white fish poached gently in a South Indian coconut, tamarind and curry leaf sauce.

items.raw: 700g firm white fish (snapper, barramundi), in 3cm pieces
10 fresh curry leaves (or 1 tsp curry powder)

steps.text: Pat fish dry. Season with salt and a pinch of turmeric. Rest while you make the sauce.
Heat the oil. Add mustard seeds. When they pop, add curry leaves.
Add onion. Cook 8 minutes until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, green chilli. Cook 1 minute.
Add turmeric, coriander, chilli powder. Toast 30 seconds.
Add the blitzed tomato. Cook 5 minutes until the oil splits.
Pour in the coconut milk and tamarind. Simmer 8 minutes, the sauce should darken and thicken.
Slide the fish in gently. Don't stir, just spoon sauce over. Simmer 5 minutes until the fish flakes.
Off the heat, top with coriander. Serve over rice with lime and naan.

notes: Don't stir vigorously after the fish goes in, it falls apart. Gentle spooning of sauce instead.
South Indian style. Tamarind for sour, coconut for richness, mustard seeds for the pop.

title: Fish Tacos
summary: Spiced white fish in charred corn tortillas with lime slaw and chipotle crema.

items.raw: 600g firm white fish fillets (snapper, barramundi, or cod)
1 chipotle in adobo, chopped + 1 tsp adobo sauce
8–12 small corn tortillas, warmed and charred

steps.text: Mix the slaw, let it sit while you cook the fish (the cabbage softens slightly).
Whisk the crema.
Rub the fish with the oil, lime, and spices.
Heat a heavy pan over medium-high heat. Cook the fish 3 minutes a side until just opaque and flaking. Break into large chunks.
Char the tortillas directly over a gas flame or in a dry pan for 20 seconds a side.
Build each taco: tortilla, slaw, fish, avocado, jalapeño, pickled onion, crema, lime squeeze.

notes: Quick-pickled red onion (sliced onion + lime juice + salt + 10 min rest) takes these from good to great.
Double-stack the tortillas if they're thin. Wet fillings tear corn tortillas fast.

title: Four Cheese Pizza
summary: A white pizza of mozzarella, Gorgonzola, Gruyère and parmesan, finished with honey.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 240°C with a stone or tray inside.
Mix the olive oil with garlic. Brush over the bases (no tomato, this is a white pizza).
Distribute mozzarella, Gorgonzola, Gruyère, and most of the parmesan over the bases.
Scatter thyme leaves.
Slide onto the hot stone. Bake 8 minutes until the cheeses are melted and bubbling, edges deep golden.
Drizzle with honey while still hot, the sweetness cuts the rich cheese beautifully.
Top with the rest of the parmesan and cracked pepper.

notes: No red sauce. A four-cheese is a white pizza or it loses the point.
Honey + Gorgonzola is the surprise. If you've never tried it, do.

title: French Onion Soup
summary: Onions cooked slowly to mahogany in beef stock, under a grilled Gruyère crouton.

steps.text: Melt the butter with oil in a wide heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onions, salt, and sugar.
Cook for 45–60 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes. This is patience work, you're looking for deep, even mahogany. Brown bits stuck to the pot are flavour gold; scrape and incorporate them.
When the onions are deep, jammy, and reduced to a quarter of their original volume, sprinkle in the flour and cook 1 minute.
Add the garlic, thyme, and bay. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and brandy, scraping up everything. Reduce by half, 3 minutes.
Add the stock. Simmer 20 minutes. Season heavily.
Meanwhile, toast the bread until deeply golden.
Heat the grill (broiler) to high. Ladle soup into oven-safe bowls. Float a slice of toast on top. Pile with Gruyère and a scatter of parmesan.
Grill until the cheese is blistered, deep gold, and bubbling, about 3 minutes. Watch it.
Serve immediately, careful, the bowls are nuclear.

notes: Onions take an hour. There's no shortcut. Anyone selling you 15-minute caramelised onions is selling you onions, not caramelised onions.
Real Gruyère, not "Swiss-style". The nuttiness is half the dish.

title: Fried Chicken
summary: Buttermilk-marinated chicken in a craggy spiced coating, fried steadily until deep golden.

image.credit: Photo: 素材王国 Footage Kingdom / Pexels

steps.text: Whisk buttermilk, hot sauce, salt, and pepper. Submerge chicken pieces. Marinate overnight (or at least 4 hours).
Combine all coating ingredients in a wide dish.
Lift each piece of chicken out of buttermilk (let excess drip off). Press deeply into the coating. Rest on a rack for 15 minutes, this is critical, sets the breading.
Heat oil to 165°C in a deep heavy pan or Dutch oven (a thermometer is the difference between perfect and burnt).
Fry chicken in batches of 3–4 pieces for 12–15 minutes, turn occasionally. Internal temperature should hit 75°C.
Drain on a rack. Salt while still hot.
Rest 5 minutes before eating. The crust sets, the steam settles back into the meat.

notes: Buttermilk overnight is the entire secret to juicy interior.
165°C oil, not hotter. Higher heat browns the outside before the inside cooks.

title: Gazpacho
summary: A chilled blended soup of ripe tomato, cucumber and capsicum, thickened with bread.

items.raw: 1kg very ripe tomatoes (the riper the better)
1 slice day-old white bread, crusts removed and soaked in 60ml water
items.prep: crusts removed and soaked in 60ml water

items.raw: 4 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, plus extra to serve

steps.text: Core the tomatoes and cut into chunks (no need to peel, the blender handles it).
Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, capsicum, onion, garlic, soaked bread, olive oil, vinegar, and salt in a blender. Blend on high for 2 minutes until completely smooth.
Add cold water to thin to your desired consistency. Some like it like a thick smoothie, others sippable from a glass.
Push the soup through a fine sieve with the back of a ladle for restaurant smoothness (optional but transformative).
Chill for at least 2 hours, preferably 4. Cold gazpacho is the whole point, warm gazpacho is sad tomato water.
Taste and adjust salt and vinegar, chilling dulls flavours.
Ladle into bowls. Top with diced cucumber, capsicum, tomato, and croutons. Drizzle with olive oil and crack pepper over.

notes: In-season tomatoes only. Off-season tomatoes make off-season gazpacho.
Bread soaked in water is the traditional thickener, it gives the soup body without making it heavy.

title: Gnocchi
summary: Light potato gnocchi from baked floury potatoes, tossed in nutty sage butter.

items.raw: 200g 00 flour, plus extra for the bench

steps.text: Bake the potatoes whole at 200°C for 50 minutes, baking, not boiling, keeps the flesh dry, which is essential.
While still hot (handle with a tea towel), peel and pass through a ricer onto the bench. Spread out and cool 5 minutes.

Sprinkle the salt, nutmeg, and most of the flour over the potato. Make a well, add the yolk, and bring together with a bench scraper. Knead briefly, just enough to come together. Overworked gnocchi is gummy.
Cut the dough into 6 pieces. Roll each into a long rope 2cm thick. Cut into 2cm pillows.
For ridges, roll each gnocchi gently down the back of a fork. Lay on a floured tray.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a gentle boil.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the sage leaves and garlic. Cook until the butter foams, turns golden, and smells nutty, the leaves should crisp.
Drop the gnocchi into the boiling water in batches. They're done when they float, about 90 seconds. Lift with a slotted spoon straight into the sage butter.
Toss to coat, add a splash of pasta water, and finish with parmesan and lots of pepper.

notes: Floury potatoes baked dry, never waxy, never boiled. Wet potato = flour bomb = lead pillows.
Knead minimally. Stop the moment the dough comes together.

title: Gnocchi Bake
summary: Shop-bought gnocchi baked straight into a sausage and tomato sauce under mozzarella.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C.
In an oven-safe pan, brown the sausage in oil for 5 minutes. Add onion; cook 5 minutes. Add garlic and chilli; 1 minute.
Stir in tomato paste, then passata, oregano, sugar. Simmer 8 minutes.
Stir in the raw gnocchi, yes, raw. They cook in the sauce.
Tear mozzarella over the top. Drizzle olive oil.
Bake 20 minutes, gnocchi will puff and the cheese will blister.
Optional: 2 minutes under grill for extra char.
Rest 3 minutes. Top with parmesan and torn basil.

notes: Raw gnocchi straight into hot sauce in the oven. No pre-boiling needed.
A one-pan wonder. Weeknight gold.

title: Goulash
summary: Beef braised with jammy onions and sweet Hungarian paprika, brightened with vinegar.

image.credit: Photo: José Antonio Otegui Auzmendi / Pexels

items.raw: 1kg beef chuck or shin, in 3cm cubes
Crusty bread, buttered noodles, or boiled potatoes

steps.text: Brown the beef in the lard over high heat in batches. Don't crowd. Set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onions to the same pot. Cook 20 minutes, yes, twenty, until deep brown and almost jammy. This is where 80% of the flavour lives.
Add the garlic, caraway, and both paprikas. Stir for 30 seconds, paprika scorches fast, don't walk away.
Stir in the tomato paste. Cook 1 minute.
Return the beef. Add the capsicums, stock, and bay leaves. Bring to a bare simmer.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 2 hours, stirring every 30 minutes. The beef should be fork-tender and the sauce thick.
Finish with the vinegar, that brightness lifts the whole pot. Season heavily.
Serve over noodles or with bread, topped with a dollop of sour cream and parsley.

notes: Sweet Hungarian paprika is the right paprika. Smoked alone is too aggressive; sweet alone too mild.
Deep brown onions = deep brown stew. Cheating the onion step makes a pale, lifeless goulash.

title: Greek Chicken Bowl
summary: Oregano and lemon chicken over lemon rice with tzatziki, feta and olives.

items.raw: 2 cups cooked lemon rice (rice + lemon zest + butter + parsley)

steps.text: Marinate chicken 30 minutes.
Heat a heavy pan over high heat. Cook chicken in a single layer 3 minutes a side until deep golden and just cooked.
Whisk tzatziki.
Build each bowl: lemon rice base. Arrange chicken, tomato, cucumber, onion, olives, feta around the edges.
Drizzle tzatziki generously. Scatter pita strips. Lemon wedge.

notes: Lemon rice (zest + butter at the end of cooking) is the surprise upgrade vs plain rice.
Feta crumbled, not sliced. Maximum surface area = maximum flavour.

title: Greek Lamb
summary: Garlic-studded lamb shoulder slow-roasted over potatoes until it pulls apart.

steps.text: Make small slits all over the lamb with a knife. Push a sliver of garlic into each.
Whisk the oil, oregano, cinnamon, salt, pepper, lemon zest, and juice. Rub all over the lamb.
Lay the potatoes, onions, and tomatoes in a deep roasting tray. Sit the lamb on top. Pour the stock and wine around (not over) the lamb. Tuck in the rosemary.
Cover tightly with foil. Bake at 160°C for 3.5 hours.
Uncover and crank to 220°C for 30 minutes, the lamb should burnish, the potatoes should crisp on top.
Rest 15 minutes. The lamb should pull apart with a spoon.
Pile lamb and potatoes onto a platter. Spoon over pan juices. Serve with salad, tzatziki, bread.

notes: Garlic stuffed into the meat is the move. Each bite finds a hit of soft roasted garlic.
Low and slow under foil, then naked and high to finish. Two-temp roast.

title: Greek Salad
summary: Ripe tomato, cucumber, olives and onion under a whole slab of feta and oregano.

items.raw: 4 ripe tomatoes (mix sizes), cut into chunks
1 large cucumber, peeled in stripes and chunked
200g Greek feta, in one thick slab (not crumbled)
4 tbsp extra virgin olive oil (good quality)

steps.text: Salt the tomatoes lightly and rest in a colander for 5 minutes to draw out water, this is the difference between a watery salad and a great one.
In a wide shallow bowl, combine the tomatoes, cucumber, capsicum, red onion, and olives. Toss with the olive oil and vinegar. Season.
Lay the whole slab of feta on top of the salad. Drizzle with extra olive oil. Scatter oregano and dried mint over the cheese.
Crack pepper on top. Don't toss, let people break off pieces of feta as they serve.
Serve with crusty bread to mop up the salad juices.

notes: A slab of feta on top, not crumbled through. The slab thing is non-negotiable in Greece.
No lettuce. A horiatiki has no lettuce. Anything that does is a hotel "Greek-style" salad.

title: Green Papaya Salad
summary: Shredded green papaya pounded with lime, chilli, fish sauce and peanuts.

items.raw: 1 medium green papaya (about 400g flesh), peeled and shredded
6 raw prawns, optional, blanched and chopped
4 bird's eye chillies (adjust to heat tolerance)
3 tbsp roasted peanuts, plus extra for serving

steps.text: In a large mortar (a Thai clay mortar is ideal), pound the garlic and chillies to a paste.
Add the palm sugar. Pound until it dissolves.
Add fish sauce, lime juice, and dried shrimp if using. Mix.
Add the green beans and bruise lightly with the pestle to break the fibres.
Add the tomatoes and prawns. Bruise gently.
Add the shredded papaya. Use a spoon to lift and turn the mixture while bruising lightly with the pestle, you want everything dressed and slightly broken down, not pulverised.
Add 3 tbsp peanuts. Mix once more.
Pile onto plates. Scatter extra peanuts. Serve with sticky rice and cucumber.

notes: Bruise, don't pulverise. Som tum should have crunch.
Green papaya is unripe, find at any Asian grocer. Substitute with green mango or shredded carrot if needed.

title: Grilled Cheese
summary: Cheddar, Gruyère and mozzarella in bread crisped slowly with butter and mayonnaise.

items.item: good white sourdough or country bread
items.raw: 4 slices good white sourdough or country bread
1 tbsp mayonnaise (the secret to the crispiest crust)
items.note: the secret to the crispiest crust

steps.text: Mix the three cheeses in a bowl, the mix is the secret to that perfect pull and flavour. Cheddar for sharpness, Gruyère for nuttiness, mozzarella for stretch.
Spread the outside of 2 slices with mayo, the other 2 with butter. The mayo side gets the lacy crisp; the butter adds flavour.
On the inside of each, pile half the cheese mix. Top with the second slice (mayo and butter outsides).
Heat a non-stick or cast iron pan over medium-low heat (low and slow is the key).
Lay the sandwiches in. Cook 4 minutes a side, pressing gently with a spatula now and then.
The crust should be deep mahogany and crackling, with cheese fully melted and oozing out the edges when you lift it.
Rest 30 seconds, cheese needs to set slightly. Cut diagonally.

notes: Mayo on the outside is not weird. It crisps better than butter alone.
Three-cheese mix elevates a basic grilled cheese into something memorable.

title: Grilled Chicken Salad
summary: Chargrilled lemon and oregano chicken over a crisp salad with feta, olives and avocado.

steps.text: Marinate chicken 20 minutes.
Heat a grill plate to high. Cook chicken 4 minutes a side until char marks form and cooked through. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Whisk dressing.
On a wide platter, arrange lettuce as a base. Top with tomatoes, cucumber, onion, avocado, feta, olives, croutons.
Lay sliced chicken across the top.
Drizzle with dressing at the table.

notes: Dress at the table. Pre-dressed salad goes limp before it hits the plate.
Char marks matter visually and for flavour. Get the grill screaming.

title: Grilled Halloumi
summary: Seared halloumi with watermelon and mint under a warm honey-chilli drizzle.

steps.text: Pat the halloumi completely dry, wet halloumi steams and never browns.
Toss the slices with olive oil, oregano, lemon zest, and pepper.
Warm the honey with chilli flakes, lemon, and oil in a small pan for 1 minute. Set aside.
Heat a heavy pan or grill plate over medium-high heat until very hot.
Lay the halloumi in. Cook 90 seconds per side, deeply golden, no longer. After that point the texture turns rubbery.
Plate over watermelon or tomatoes. Scatter mint and oregano. Drizzle with honey-chilli. Squeeze lemon over.
Serve immediately with warm flatbread.

notes: Halloumi waits for no one. Eat within 5 minutes of leaving the pan or the texture goes squeaky.
Sweet + salty + char = the trinity that makes grilled halloumi great.

title: Grilled Salmon
summary: Lemon and herb salmon cooked skin-side down on the barbecue, finished with herb butter.

steps.text: Pat the salmon dry. Whisk the olive oil, lemon zest and juice, garlic, herbs, salt, and pepper. Brush over the salmon.
Mix the herb butter ingredients into a paste. Roll into a log in cling film and refrigerate.
Heat a BBQ or grill plate to medium-high. Oil the grates well.
Place the salmon skin-side-down. Cook 5–6 minutes without moving, let the skin release on its own when ready.
Flip. Cook 3 more minutes for medium (still slightly translucent in the centre).
Lift onto plates. Top each fillet with a thick slice of the herb butter, it melts over the hot fish.
Serve with lemon and your side of choice.

notes: Oil the grates, not the fish. Oiled fish sticks more.
Salmon is best slightly under, it carries on cooking off the heat.

title: Grilled Steak
summary: A well-salted steak seared hard, rested, and topped with garlic herb butter.

items.raw: 4 rib eye, sirloin, or scotch fillet steaks (250–300g each, 2.5cm thick)

steps.text: Take steaks out of the fridge 30 minutes before. Pat completely dry. Coat lightly with oil. Season HEAVILY with salt and pepper, more than you think.
Mix butter, garlic, herbs, lemon zest into a paste. Refrigerate.
Heat a heavy cast iron pan or grill plate until smoking, really smoking, not warm.
Lay the steaks in. Don't move for 3 minutes (medium-rare on 2.5cm). Flip. Cook another 3 minutes. Use the finger test or thermometer, 52°C is medium-rare.
In the last minute, stand each steak on its fat edge for 30 seconds to render.
Lift onto a warm plate. Top each with a thick slice of herb butter. Rest 8 minutes, non-negotiable.
Slice across the grain. Serve with the resting juices and sides.

notes: Rest the meat. 8 minutes minimum. Cut early and the juices run out onto the board.
Hot pan, dry steak, salt heavily. The Maillard crust is the whole point.

title: Gumbo
summary: A dark roux stew of andouille, chicken and prawns, thickened with okra or filé.

items.raw: 300g okra, sliced (or 1 tsp filé powder added at the end)
items.note: or 1 tsp filé powder added at the end

steps.text: Make the roux, this is the soul of gumbo. In a heavy pot, whisk the oil and flour together over medium-low heat. Stir constantly with a wooden spoon for 30–45 minutes. The colour will go: blonde, peanut butter, copper, chocolate. You want a deep dark chocolate. Do not stop stirring. Do not get distracted. A burnt roux is bin material.
When the roux hits dark chocolate, immediately dump in the onion, capsicum, and celery. They'll cool the roux and stop it cooking further. Sizzle for 5 minutes until the veg soften.
Add the garlic, sausage, Cajun seasoning, thyme, and cayenne. Cook 5 minutes.
Pour in the hot stock gradually, whisking to dissolve the roux. Add the bay leaves and chicken.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce to low and cook uncovered for 60 minutes. The gumbo will thicken and the flavours will deepen.
Add the okra (or, if using filé instead, hold it for the end). Simmer 15 minutes.
Add the prawns in the last 4 minutes, they're done when pink.
Off the heat, stir in 1 tsp filé powder if you skipped the okra. Taste, adjust with salt, more cayenne, or a dash of hot sauce.
Mound a scoop of rice in each bowl and ladle the gumbo around it. Top with spring onion.

notes: Dark roux takes patience. Watching it hit that chocolate colour is the whole skill.
Okra OR filé, never both at once. They both thicken; doubling up makes it slimy.

title: Gyros
summary: Charred marinated pork in warm pita with tzatziki, tomato, onion and hot chips.

items.raw: 800g pork shoulder, in thin strips (or chicken thigh)

steps.text: Combine all the pork marinade ingredients with the meat. Rest 2 hours (or up to overnight).
Whisk the tzatziki ingredients together. Season and refrigerate.
Heat a heavy pan or grill plate over high heat. Cook the pork in batches in a single layer, really let the edges char. About 3 minutes per batch.
Warm the pita briefly over an open flame or in a dry pan.
Build: smear tzatziki on a pita, pile in the pork, add tomato and red onion, drop in a few hot chips, more tzatziki, squeeze of lemon. Roll tight.

notes: Chips inside the wrap. That's the way it's served in Greece. Don't argue.
A vertical rotisserie is the real method but a screaming hot pan with a small batch gives 90% of the result.

title: Gyudon
summary: Thin beef and onion simmered in a sweet dashi and soy sauce over rice with an egg.

items.raw: 300g beef rib eye or sirloin, sliced paper-thin

items.item: generous bowls of steamed short-grain rice
items.raw: 2 generous bowls of steamed short-grain rice
2 eggs (raw or soft-yolked, for topping, Japanese custom)
items.note: raw or soft-yolked, for topping, Japanese custom

steps.text: In a wide pan, combine the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and ginger. Bring to a simmer.
Add the onions. Cook 5 minutes until softening.
Slide the beef into the simmering sauce in a single layer. Cook 2 minutes, it cooks fast and turns from red to grey-brown.
Reduce the sauce slightly until it just clings to the meat, 3–4 more minutes.
Mound rice into deep bowls. Ladle the beef and onions on top, including a few generous spoons of sauce that soaks into the rice.
Top with a raw or soft-cooked egg (crack the raw one right onto the hot beef, it tempers). Scatter pickled ginger, spring onion, and shichimi.

notes: Paper-thin beef cooks in 2 minutes. Get it from a Japanese grocer or freeze and slice it yourself.
Soft yolk over rice is the traditional finish, it makes a sauce of its own.
Raw or soft-cooked egg isn't recommended if you're pregnant, cooking for young children or older people, or have a weakened immune system. Use a hard-boiled egg instead.

title: Halloumi Wrap
summary: Golden seared halloumi rolled with salad, mint and a yoghurt tahini sauce.

steps.text: Pat the halloumi dry. Toss with olive oil, oregano, and lemon zest.
Whisk the yogurt-tahini sauce. Loosen with a splash of cold water until pourable. Taste.
Heat a heavy pan over medium-high heat. Lay the halloumi in. Cook 90 seconds a side, deeply golden, no longer or it goes squeaky and tough.
Warm the flatbreads briefly in a dry pan.
Spread sauce on each. Layer lettuce, cucumber, tomato, red onion, halloumi, mint, and pickled chillies. Dust with sumac.
Roll tight. Serve warm.

notes: Halloumi must hit the pan dry. Wet halloumi steams and never browns.
90 seconds per side. Any longer and the texture turns rubbery.

title: Hawaiian Pizza
summary: Ham and pineapple over tomato and mozzarella, baked until the fruit caramelises.

items.raw: Pinch of salt, sugar, and oregano

items.item: good cooked ham or smoky bacon
items.raw: 200g good cooked ham or smoky bacon, in pieces
200g fresh pineapple, in small chunks (or drained tinned)

steps.text: Heat the oven to 240°C with a stone or tray inside.
Mix the passata with garlic, oil, salt, sugar, oregano.
Spread thin on each base. Dot with mozzarella.
Scatter ham and pineapple over.
Bake 8–10 minutes until the crust is deep golden and the pineapple edges caramelise.
Sprinkle chilli flakes if you like, tear basil over. Slice.

notes: Pineapple on pizza is the great divider. If you're here, you're team yes, own it.
Pat the pineapple dry first. Wet pineapple makes wet pizza.

title: Honey Garlic Chicken
summary: Crisp-skinned thighs basted in the pan with a sticky honey, soy and garlic glaze.

steps.text: Pat chicken dry. Season. Dust both sides lightly with cornflour.
Heat oil in a wide pan over medium-high. Lay the chicken skin-side-down. Cook 7 minutes without moving until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip. Cook 4 more minutes.
Drain excess fat. Reduce heat to medium.
Whisk the sauce ingredients. Pour around the chicken. The sauce bubbles immediately.
Baste the chicken constantly for 3 minutes, the sauce thickens to a glossy syrup that clings to the chicken.
Plate over rice. Drizzle with sauce. Steam veg on the side. Scatter sesame and spring onion.

notes: Cornflour dust gives the skin extra crackle.
Baste in the pan, constant spooning of bubbling sauce makes the glaze coat properly.

title: Hot Dogs
summary: Simmered then charred franks in toasted buns with slow-cooked onions and sauerkraut.

steps.text: Melt the butter for the onions in a pan over medium-low heat. Add the onions and salt. Cook slowly for 20 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown. Stir in the brown sugar for the last 2 minutes.
For the frankfurters: bring a pot of water to a bare simmer (never boil, boiling splits the casing). Slip the franks in for 6 minutes.
Drain and finish on a hot grill plate or in a dry pan with a knob of butter for 2 minutes, rotating, to get char marks.
Butter the inside of the buns and toast on the grill or pan until lightly golden.
Build each: bun, frank, stripe of mustard, pile of caramelised onions, a forkful of sauerkraut, jalapeños, a scatter of fried shallots.

notes: Top-split buns toast better and hold fillings without flopping. Worth the search.
Simmer then sear, boiled hot dogs are sad. Even one minute on the grill makes them.

title: Huevos Rancheros
summary: Fried eggs on charred corn tortillas with black beans and a spiced tomato sauce.

items.raw: 1 jalapeño, finely chopped (deseed for less heat)

steps.text: For the sauce: cook the onion in olive oil 5 minutes. Add the garlic and jalapeño; cook 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, cumin, paprika, chilli powder, oregano, and sugar. Simmer 12 minutes until thick. Season.
Warm the beans in a small pan with a splash of water and a pinch of cumin. Roughly mash.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a non-stick pan. Char the tortillas one at a time directly over the flame or in a dry pan for 30 seconds a side.
In the same pan, fry the eggs sunny-side-up in oil until the whites are set but the yolks runny.
On each plate, lay 2 warm tortillas overlapping. Smear with beans. Spoon plenty of ranchero sauce over the tortillas.
Top each plate with 2 fried eggs.
Scatter avocado, feta, coriander. Drizzle hot sauce. Serve with lime.

notes: Charred corn tortillas, not flour. The corn flavour holds up against the sauce.
Runny yolks are the rule, they mix with the sauce into something better than either alone.

title: Hummus Plate
summary: Silky hummus from peeled, well-cooked chickpeas, served with warm pita and crudités.

items.raw: 250g dried chickpeas, soaked overnight in cold water with 1 tsp baking soda (or 2 × 400g tins)
items.prep: soaked overnight in cold water with 1 tsp baking soda

steps.text: Drain the soaked chickpeas. Cover with fresh water in a pot with the second teaspoon of baking soda. Boil 45–55 minutes until very soft, they should crush between your fingers. (Tinned: drain and simmer with bicarb in fresh water 15 minutes.)
Drain and reserve a cup of the cooking water. While warm, rub the chickpeas in a tea towel to loosen the skins. Lift the chickpeas out, leaving most skins behind. This is the secret to silky hummus.
In a food processor, blend the garlic, lemon juice, and salt for 30 seconds. Let it sit a minute, this mellows the raw garlic.
Add the tahini and cumin. Process until thick and pale.
Add the warm peeled chickpeas. Process 3 minutes, yes, that long. Drizzle in iced water until you have a pillowy, billowing texture. Taste; add more lemon or salt.
Spoon into a wide bowl and swirl with the back of the spoon to create a moat. Pool olive oil in the centre. Dust with paprika and chopped parsley. Scatter toasted pine nuts.
Serve with warm pita and crunchy vegetables.

notes: Baking soda + long cook + peeling = next-level smooth hummus. Worth the effort.
Hummus should be cloud-light, not paste-thick. Iced water is the trick.

title: Italian Meatballs
summary: Browned beef and pork meatballs simmered in a garlicky tomato sauce over spaghetti.

items.raw: 60g panko, soaked in 80ml milk for 5 minutes

steps.text: Combine all meatball ingredients (except olive oil). Mix briefly with hands, overworked meat is rubbery.
Roll into 16 even meatballs.
Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Brown the meatballs in batches for 6 minutes per batch (turning), until well coloured.
Lift out. In the same pan, sauté garlic and chilli flakes for 90 seconds.
Add tomato paste; cook 2 minutes. Add passata, oregano, sugar. Simmer 8 minutes.
Return meatballs to the sauce. Cover and simmer 15 minutes, they finish cooking and the sauce thickens around them. Tear basil over.
Cook pasta. Serve meatballs over pasta with sauce ladled and parmesan grated heavily.

notes: Brown then braise. Sauce-only cooking gives pale, soft meatballs without character.
Pork in the mix is essential, fat is flavour and tenderness.

title: Jambalaya
summary: Creole rice cooked with andouille, chicken and prawns in a spiced tomato base.

items.raw: 2 celery sticks, diced (this is the "holy trinity")

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy Dutch oven. Brown the sausage for 4 minutes. Lift out.
In the same pot, brown the chicken in a single layer for 5 minutes. Lift out.
Add the trinity (onion, capsicum, celery). Cook 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and toast 1 minute. Add the diced tomatoes, Cajun seasoning, thyme, paprika, bay, and cayenne. Simmer 5 minutes.
Tip in the rice and stir to coat in the spiced base.
Return the chicken and sausage with any juices. Pour in the stock. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 22 minutes. Don't lift the lid.
Stir gently. Nestle in the prawns. Cover again and cook 5 more minutes until the prawns are pink and the rice is tender.
Rest 10 minutes off the heat, lid on. Fluff with a fork. Top with spring onion and serve with hot sauce.

notes: This is the "Creole" red version with tomato. Cajun jambalaya is brown, same dish, no tomato.
Don't stir while the rice cooks. Crusty bottom (pegao) is welcomed.

title: Jollof Rice
summary: Rice cooked unstirred in a stewed pepper and tomato base until smoky at the bottom.

items.raw: 2 Scotch bonnet chillies (or 4 bird's eye), deseeded

steps.text: Blitz the capsicums, tomatoes, chillies, and red onion to a smooth puree.
Heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy pot. Cook the diced onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add garlic; cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste, paprika, curry powder, thyme, bay, ginger, and white pepper. Cook 3 minutes, the paste should deepen.
