Pour in the pepper puree. Simmer 15 minutes, stirring often, until darkened and the oil splits from the sauce. This stewing is the soul of jollof.
Add the rinsed rice. Stir to coat in the red sauce.
Add the stock, salt, and sugar. Stir once and don't stir again. Bring to a simmer.
Cover with a lid lined with foil for a tight seal. Reduce heat to lowest and cook 30 minutes.
For the prized party-jollof bottom layer: turn the heat up to medium for the final 5 minutes, listen for crackling. That's the smoky bottom crust forming.
Off the heat, rest 10 minutes, lid on. Fluff with a fork, don't over-stir.
Serve with plantain, chicken, slaw, and a boiled egg if you're feeling Nigerian about it.

notes: The pepper base is the soul. Get it darkened and oily before the rice goes in.
No peeking, no stirring. Once the rice is in, leave it alone.

title: Kare Kare
summary: Tender oxtail in a thick peanut and annatto sauce, served with vegetables and bagoong.

items.raw: 3 tbsp annatto seeds (or 1 tbsp annatto powder)
120g toasted peanut butter (or roasted ground peanuts)
60g toasted rice flour (toast plain rice flour in a dry pan until tan)
items.note: toast plain rice flour in a dry pan until tan

items.raw: 1.2L beef stock (use the oxtail cooking liquid)
1 bunch baby bok choy or pechay

items.item: Chinese long beans or green beans
items.raw: 200g Chinese long beans or green beans, in 5cm lengths

steps.text: Cover the oxtail with cold water in a large pot. Bring to a boil, drain, and rinse, this removes scum and gives a cleaner broth.

Return the oxtail to the pot. Cover with 3 litres fresh water. Add the onions, garlic, bay, peppercorns, and salt. Simmer 2 hours until the meat is falling off the bone. Lift out the oxtail. Strain and reserve the broth.
Steep the annatto seeds in 100ml hot water for 10 minutes. Strain, keep the red liquid.
In a clean wide pan, heat the oil. Cook the onion 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the annatto water and 1.2L of the strained broth. Bring to a simmer.
Whisk in the peanut butter until smooth.
Mix the toasted rice flour with a few tablespoons of cold broth to make a slurry. Whisk in. Simmer 5 minutes, the sauce should be thick enough to coat a spoon.
Add the oxtail back to the sauce. Simmer 10 minutes to meld.
In a separate pan, briefly blanch each vegetable individually, bok choy 1 minute, beans 2 minutes, eggplant 3 minutes. Keep them bright and crisp.
Arrange the oxtail in a wide bowl. Pour the sauce over. Tuck the vegetables in around the edges.
Sauté 4 tbsp bagoong with a little oil, garlic, and a pinch of sugar for 3 minutes. Serve in a small bowl on the side. Rice in another. Each diner mixes their own bite.

notes: Without the bagoong on the side, it isn't kare-kare. The sweet peanut sauce needs the funky salty hit.
Toasted rice flour is the traditional thickener (no cornflour). Toast until tan, not brown.

title: Katsu Curry
summary: Crisp panko cutlets beside a smooth, gently sweet Japanese curry sauce and rice.

items.raw: 2 tbsp curry powder (S&B Japanese is ideal)

steps.text: For the sauce: heat the oil in a heavy pot. Cook the onion and carrot for 12 minutes until soft and starting to caramelise.
Add the garlic, ginger, and apple. Cook 3 minutes.
Sprinkle in the flour, curry powder, and garam masala. Cook 2 minutes, toast the spices.
Whisk in the stock gradually. Add the soy sauce, ketchup, and sugar. Simmer 15 minutes.
Blend the sauce smooth with a stick blender for the classic glossy texture. Season.
Meanwhile, season the chicken and pound to 1.5cm thick. Set up flour, egg, and panko dishes.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, press into panko. Press hard.
Heat 1cm of oil in a wide pan to 170°C. Fry the cutlets 3 minutes a side until deep golden. Drain on a rack.
Slice each cutlet across the grain into 2cm strips, keeping the shape together.
Mound rice on one side of each plate. Spoon plenty of curry sauce alongside (not over the katsu, that's the rule, the crunch must stay). Place the sliced katsu beside the sauce.
Add a small pile of pickles.

notes: Sauce next to katsu, not on top. Crunchy katsu, saucy rice.
Apple in the sauce sounds odd but it's traditional and gives the sweetness.

title: Kebab
summary: Yoghurt-marinated lamb skewers charred on the grill, with flatbread, tzatziki and sumac.

items.raw: 800g lamb shoulder or leg, in 3cm cubes

steps.text: Mix all the lamb marinade ingredients with the meat. Massage in well. Rest at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.

Soak bamboo skewers in water (or use metal). Thread lamb, alternating with onion, capsicum, and a tomato now and then. Pack the lamb tight on its own skewers if you want it more charred, the veg skewer cooks separately.
Brush the vegetable skewers with olive oil and salt.
Heat a BBQ or grill plate to high. Cook the lamb skewers 3 minutes a side for 12 minutes total, turning every few minutes. The edges should char heavily, the inside still pink.
Grill the vegetable skewers for 8 minutes, turning, until soft and charred at the edges.
Rest the lamb 5 minutes on a board.
Warm the pita. Serve with skewers, tzatziki, tahini, raw onion tossed with sumac and parsley, and lemon. Build wraps at the table.

notes: Cook the meat skewers separate from the veg, they need different times.
Aleppo pepper has gentle warmth and fruitiness. Worth seeking out; regular chilli flakes work in a pinch.

title: Korean BBQ Beef
summary: Pear-marinated rib eye seared fast and wrapped at the table in lettuce with ssamjang.

steps.text: Marinate beef 30 minutes.
Heat a heavy pan or grill plate over screaming-high heat.
Cook beef in single-layer batches, 90 seconds per batch. Caramelised edges, tender centres.
Bring everything to the table on a platter: beef, lettuce, ssamjang, garlic, chilli, kimchi, radish, rice, pa muchim.
Each diner builds ssam wraps: lettuce leaf, rice, beef, dot of ssamjang, garlic, chilli. Fold and eat in one bite.

notes: Grated pear is the tenderiser. Korean kitchen secret.
The wrap building is the fun. Don't pre-assemble, let everyone go.

title: Korean Fried Chicken
summary: Double-fried wings, shatteringly crisp, tossed in a sweet and spicy gochujang glaze.

steps.text: Pat the wings completely dry. Toss with salt, pepper, ginger, and rice wine. Rest 10 minutes.
Coat each piece in potato starch, press it on so it sticks. Shake off excess.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 160°C. Fry the wings in 2 batches for 8 minutes each. They'll be pale and only just cooked. Drain on a rack, not paper, paper makes them soggy.
Crank the oil up to 190°C. Fry each batch a second time for 4–5 minutes until deeply golden and properly crisp. This double-fry is the entire point of Korean fried chicken.
While the chicken fries, combine the glaze ingredients in a wide pan and simmer for 3 minutes until sticky and glossy.
Tip the hot wings straight into the glaze. Toss to coat every piece, work quickly, the coating absorbs the glaze immediately.
Pile onto a platter. Scatter with sesame and spring onion. Serve with pickled radish to cut the sweetness.

notes: Potato starch crisps harder than cornflour. Worth tracking down.
Double-fry first to cook through, then to crisp, never one long fry.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
summary: Seared chicken with dried chillies, Sichuan pepper and peanuts in a glossy, tart sauce.

items.raw: 10 dried red chillies (Sichuan or Tianjin), cut in halves
4 spring onions, white parts in 2cm lengths (greens reserved)

steps.text: Marinate the chicken with soy, wine, and cornflour. Rest 15 minutes.
Whisk all sauce ingredients in a small bowl.

Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until it shimmers. Add the dried chillies and Sichuan peppercorns. Toss for 20 seconds, until the chillies darken slightly but don't blacken. Lift them out and reserve. (Or leave them in if you don't mind biting one.)
Add the chicken to the wok in a single layer. Don't move for 90 seconds, let it sear. Then stir-fry 2 minutes until golden and just cooked.
Add the garlic, ginger, and spring onion whites. Toss 30 seconds.
Pour the sauce around the edge of the wok. It will bubble and thicken in 30 seconds. Toss to coat.
Return the chillies and peppercorns. Add the peanuts. Toss for another 20 seconds.
Tip onto a platter. Scatter the reserved spring onion greens. Serve with rice.

notes: Dry-fried, not saucy. Kung pao should be glossy and tossed, not swimming.
The dried chillies are mostly for flavour and aroma, bite at your own risk.

title: Laksa
summary: A rich coconut curry broth with chicken, prawns and tofu puffs over thick noodles.

items.raw: 5 tbsp laksa paste (good Malaysian or Singaporean brand)
400g fresh thick rice noodles (or hokkien noodles)

steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a large pot. Spoon in the laksa paste and 4 tbsp of thick coconut cream from the top of the tin. Fry for 4 minutes, stirring, until the oil splits and the paste turns a deeper red.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk and the chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken and tofu. Simmer 8 minutes. Add the prawns for the final 2 minutes, they're done when they curl.
Stir in the fish sauce and palm sugar. Taste, laksa should be rich, mildly spicy, slightly sweet, salty.
Pour boiling water over the noodles to soften and warm them through. Drain and divide between deep bowls.
Ladle the laksa over the noodles. Top each bowl with bean sprouts, half a boiled egg, herbs, a spoonful of sambal, and a wedge of lime.

notes: Good laksa paste is half the dish. Brands vary wildly, find one you like and stick with it.
The fried tofu puffs soak up the broth like sponges. Don't skip them.

title: Lamb Chops
summary: Rosemary and garlic lamb cutlets seared fast and served under a sharp salsa verde.

steps.text: Combine the lamb with olive oil, garlic, herbs, salt, pepper, and lemon. Massage in. Rest 30 minutes at room temperature.
For the salsa verde: finely chop the herbs, capers, anchovy, and garlic. Stir in the vinegar and olive oil. Don't blend, keep it chunky. Taste; it should be sharp and herbaceous.
Heat a heavy pan or grill plate over high heat until smoking.
Lay the chops in, don't crowd. Cook 2.5 minutes per side for medium-rare on cutlets, 4 minutes on thicker loin chops.
In the last 30 seconds, stand the chops on their fat edge so it renders and crisps.
Rest on a warm plate, loosely covered, for 5 minutes.
Plate with a heavy spoon of salsa verde over each chop.

notes: Rest at room temp before cooking. Cold lamb in a hot pan = tough lamb.
Salsa verde keeps for 3 days. Make double.

title: Lamb Kofta
summary: Spiced lamb shaped around skewers, charred on the grill and wrapped with yoghurt sauce.

items.raw: 1 small onion, grated and squeezed dry

steps.text: Soak 8 bamboo skewers in water for 20 minutes (or use metal).
In a wide bowl, combine all kofta ingredients. Mix with your hands for 2 minutes, overworking gives the kofta their springy texture (opposite of meatballs).
Divide the mince into 8 portions. Around each skewer, shape into a 12cm sausage shape, pressing firmly.
Whisk the yogurt sauce.
Heat a grill plate or BBQ to high. Cook the kofta 3 minutes per side, turn three times for 12 minutes total. The outside should be deeply charred, the inside just pink.
Warm the flatbreads. Build: yogurt sauce, lettuce or salad, kofta off the skewer, sumac, parsley, lemon.

notes: Squeeze water from the grated onion, wet onion makes wet kofta that falls off the skewer.
Mix hard for 2 minutes, this is what gives kofta their bouncy texture.

title: Lamb Tagine
summary: Lamb shoulder braised with ras el hanout and saffron, sweetened with apricots and honey.

items.raw: 1 tsp ras el hanout (or extra cumin + paprika)
Pinch saffron in 2 tbsp hot water

steps.text: In a heavy pot or tagine, brown the lamb in 2 tbsp oil in batches. Set aside.
Add the rest of the oil. Cook onions 10 minutes until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, and all spices. Toast 1 minute.
Return the lamb. Add saffron water and stock. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise on the lowest heat (or in 160°C oven) for 90 minutes.
Add apricots and honey. Continue 30 minutes uncovered until the lamb is fork-tender and the sauce reduces to a thick gloss.
Off the heat, fold in toasted almonds and herbs. Season.
Serve over couscous with flatbread and lemon.

notes: Apricots and honey are key, the sweet-savoury balance is what makes a tagine.
Ras el hanout is a North African spice blend worth tracking down for the right depth.

title: Lasagna
summary: Layers of slow ragù, béchamel and mozzarella, rested so each slice holds.

steps.text: Brown both minces in olive oil over high heat for 6 minutes. Add the onion, carrot, and celery. Cook 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and tomato paste; cook 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half. Add the passata, milk, and bay leaves. Simmer on the lowest heat for 60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and glossy.
Meanwhile, melt the butter for the bechamel. Whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes, don't brown it.
Whisk in the warm milk gradually. Cook 8 minutes, whisking, until thick. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Heat the oven to 190°C. Oil a deep baking dish.
Build: thin layer of ragu on the base, sheets of pasta, layer of ragu, layer of bechamel, scatter of mozzarella and parmesan. Repeat 4 times. Finish with bechamel and a heavy hand of parmesan.
Bake 40 minutes until deeply golden and bubbling at the edges.
Crucial: rest 20 minutes before cutting. This is what makes the layers hold together. Don't skip.

notes: No-boil sheets work if the ragu is wet enough, fresh sheets always slip in raw.
Lasagna improves overnight. Make it a day ahead, reheat covered.

title: Lemon Herb Chicken
summary: Seared, oven-finished chicken with a lemon, wine and butter pan sauce.

steps.text: Mix the marinade. Rub all over the chicken. Rest 20 minutes.
Heat a heavy oven-safe pan over medium-high. Place chicken in (smooth-side down for breasts, skin-side for thighs). Cook 5 minutes until deep golden.
Flip. Transfer the pan to a 200°C oven. Bake 12 minutes (breast) or 15 minutes (thighs) until cooked through.
Lift chicken onto a board. Rest 5 minutes.
For the sauce: place the pan back on the stove. Pour in wine. Scrape the base. Reduce by half.
Add stock and lemon. Simmer 3 minutes. Off the heat, swirl in cold butter. Fold in parsley.
Slice the chicken across the grain. Plate with sauce spooned over and lemon on the side.

notes: Lemon zest in the marinade plus juice in the sauce, both citrus hits.
Cold butter swirled off the heat gives the sauce that restaurant gloss.

title: Lemon Pepper Salmon
summary: Salmon crusted with lemon zest and cracked pepper, with a quick caper butter sauce.

items.raw: 2 tbsp coarse black pepper (use a mortar to crush)

steps.text: Pat salmon dry. Drizzle with olive oil. Salt lightly.
Combine lemon zest, cracked pepper, and granulated garlic. Press heavily onto the flesh side of each fillet.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high. Place salmon skin-side-down. Press flat with a spatula for 30 seconds.
Cook 5 minutes without moving, the skin must be cracker crisp.
Flip. Cook 2 more minutes.
Lift salmon out. In the same pan, melt the butter and add sliced garlic. Sizzle 30 seconds, no colour.
Off the heat, add lemon juice, capers, and parsley.
Spoon sauce over each fillet. Serve with asparagus and lemon.

notes: Coarse pepper, freshly cracked. Pre-ground pepper has lost its flavour.
Skin-side first, pressed flat. The crackling skin is half the appeal.

title: Lentil Soup
summary: Brown lentils simmered with cumin and tomato, finished with spinach and lemon.

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrot, and celery in olive oil for 10 minutes until soft. Add garlic and all spices; cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste; cook 2 minutes.
Add the lentils, stock, tomatoes, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Cook 25–30 minutes until the lentils are tender. Season heavily.
Off the heat, stir in the spinach and lemon juice. The greens wilt in residual heat.
Fish out the bay. Top each bowl with parsley and a dollop of yogurt.

notes: Lemon at the end. The acid lifts the whole soup, lentils need brightness.
A drizzle of good olive oil and a crack of pepper at the table makes it.

title: Lo Mein
summary: Soft egg noodles tossed with chicken, cabbage and a glossy soy and oyster sauce.

items.raw: 300g chicken or pork, sliced thin (or 300g mixed vegetables for veg)

steps.text: Cook the noodles per packet. Drain. Don't rinse, you want the surface starch to grab the sauce.
Whisk all sauce ingredients in a bowl.
Heat the wok over high heat. Add 2 tbsp oil. Stir-fry the chicken 3 minutes. Lift out.
Add the last tbsp oil. Add the garlic and the white parts of the spring onion. Toss 20 seconds.
Add the carrot and cabbage. Stir-fry 90 seconds, they should stay crunchy.
Return the chicken. Add the cooked noodles. Pour the sauce around the edges of the wok.
Toss continuously with two spatulas (or chopsticks) for 90 seconds. Every strand glossy.
Off the heat, fold in the bean sprouts and remaining spring onion. Plate immediately.

notes: Lo mein = "tossed noodles". Chow mein = "fried noodles". Lo mein stays soft and saucy; chow mein gets crispy edges. Different dishes.
Wok hei comes from very high heat. If your stove is mild, work in small batches.

title: Loaded Nachos
summary: Corn chips layered with spiced beef, beans and cheese, baked and piled with cold toppings.

items.raw: 1 cup pico de gallo (or chunky salsa)

steps.text: Brown the mince in oil over high heat for 6 minutes. Add onion; cook 3 minutes. Add garlic and all spices; cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and stock. Simmer 5 minutes until thick. Finish with lime juice. Season.
Heat the oven to 200°C. On a large oven-safe platter or tray lined with paper, spread half the corn chips in a single layer.
Scatter half the beef, half the beans, and half the cheese over.
Top with the rest of the chips, the rest of the beef and beans, and a final heavy layer of cheese.
Bake 10 minutes until the cheese is fully melted and bubbling.
Top with pico de gallo, avocado, sour cream, jalapeños, coriander, and spring onion.
Bring to the table with lime wedges. Eat with your hands.

notes: Two layers, not a pile. Bottom chips with no cheese turn to sad dry chips.
Cold toppings go on AFTER baking. Hot baked, cold dressed.

title: Lobster Roll
summary: Chunks of lobster lightly dressed in mayonnaise, piled into butter-toasted rolls.

items.raw: 2 live lobsters, around 600g each (or 400g cooked picked meat)

steps.text: For live lobsters: chill them in the freezer for 30–60 minutes until they no longer move, as animal welfare guidance recommends. Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to the boil. Plunge the lobsters in head-first. Cover and cook 10 minutes for 600g each.
Lift out and rest in a bowl of ice water for 5 minutes, this stops cooking and makes the shells easier to handle.
Crack the claws and tails. Pull the meat out in large pieces. Pat dry. Cut into 2cm chunks, keep the texture rough.
In a bowl, whisk the mayo, lemon juice, celery, chives, mustard, salt, and pepper. Fold through the lobster, gently, you want chunks not paste.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Butter the outsides of the buns generously and toast them golden brown on both sides.
Line each bun with a leaf of lettuce if using. Pile in the lobster salad. Squeeze of lemon on top.

notes: Maine: chilled with mayo. Connecticut: warm with melted butter. Both legitimate, I prefer Maine for the contrast with the warm buttery bun.
Don't over-dress. The lobster is the star; the mayo is just a binder.

title: Mac and Cheese
summary: Macaroni baked in a three-cheese sauce beneath a crisp paprika crumb.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cook the pasta in well-salted water until just shy of al dente (2 minutes less than packet), it finishes in the oven. Drain.
For the sauce: melt the butter, whisk in the flour, cook 2 minutes for a pale roux.
Whisk in the warm milk gradually. Cook 5 minutes until thick. Add the cream and warm through.
Off the heat, whisk in the mustard, paprika, garlic powder, nutmeg, and cream cheese until smooth.
Gradually whisk in the cheddar and Gruyère in handfuls, don't dump it all at once or it clumps. Off the heat is key.
Season generously. The sauce should taste slightly over-seasoned because the pasta dilutes it.
Stir the drained pasta through the sauce. Tip into a deep baking dish.
Mix the panko, melted butter, parmesan, and paprika. Scatter over the top.
Bake 20–22 minutes until the top is deep golden and the edges are bubbling.
Rest 5 minutes. Serve straight from the dish.

notes: Off-the-heat cheese whisking. Hot sauce + cheese = stringy mess.
Three-cheese mix gives both flavour (cheddar), nuttiness (Gruyère), and silkiness (cream cheese).

title: Mango Curry
summary: Chicken in a coconut and ripe mango sauce with curry leaves, finished with fresh mango.

items.raw: 600g chicken thigh, in pieces (or 500g paneer for vegetarian)
2 ripe mangoes, 1 blitzed to a puree, 1 diced
10 fresh curry leaves (if you can find them)

steps.text: Heat the coconut oil. Cook the onion 8 minutes until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, and green chilli. Cook 1 minute.
Add all the ground spices. Toast 30 seconds.
Add the chicken. Stir to coat. Cook 5 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and mango puree. Add curry leaves and salt. Simmer 12 minutes.
Add the diced mango. Simmer 3 more minutes, just to warm through, you want fresh mango bite, not stewed.
Off the heat, lime juice and coriander.
Serve over rice with naan and raita.

notes: Ripe mangoes only. Underripe mango goes stringy and tart in the wrong way.
Half puree, half chunks. That balance gives sweetness in the sauce and texture in every bite.

title: Mapo Tofu
summary: Silken tofu in a fiery doubanjiang and pork sauce, finished with numbing Sichuan pepper.

items.raw: 3 tbsp doubanjiang (Sichuan broad bean chilli paste)
2 tbsp cornflour mixed with 3 tbsp water
1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground

steps.text: Bring a pot of salted water to a bare simmer. Slip the tofu cubes in for 2 minutes, this firms them up and stops them breaking later. Lift out gently.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the pork. Break it up and stir-fry for 4 minutes until the fat renders and the edges crisp.
Push the pork to the side. Add the doubanjiang and stir for 30 seconds until the oil turns red.
Add the douchi, garlic, ginger, and chilli flakes. Stir 30 seconds.
Pour in the stock. Add soy sauce and sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Slip the tofu in gently. Simmer 5 minutes without stirring, let the tofu absorb the broth.
Pour the cornflour slurry around the edge of the wok in a thin stream. Push gently with the back of a spoon, don't stir, just nudge. The sauce will thicken and grip the tofu.
Scatter the ground Sichuan peppercorns and spring onions over the top.
Serve over steamed rice. Eat while the lip-tingling numbness is fresh.

notes: Silken tofu is fragile. Push, never stir.
Real Sichuan peppercorns at the end. Don't cook them; the tongue-tingling málá fades with heat.

title: Margherita Flatbread
summary: Store-bought flatbread topped with raw tomato sauce and mozzarella, baked hot, with basil.

items.raw: 2 store-bought naan or 2 ready flatbreads (or pizza bases)

items.item: Extra virgin olive oil to finish
items.raw: Extra virgin olive oil to finish

steps.text: Heat the oven to 230°C with a pizza stone or heavy tray inside.
Mix the passata with garlic, olive oil, salt, sugar, and oregano. Don't cook it.
Spread a thin layer of sauce on each flatbread, leaving a 1cm border.
Dot with torn mozzarella.
Slide onto the hot stone. Bake 8–10 minutes until the cheese is melted and starting to colour.
Tear basil over the top. Scatter parmesan. Crack pepper. Drizzle with olive oil.
Slice and serve immediately.

notes: Hot oven is everything. Cold oven = sad flatbread.
Basil goes on AFTER baking, heat destroys it.

title: Margherita Pizza
summary: Blistered crust, raw tomato and torn fior di latte, baked as hot as the oven allows.

items.item: Extra virgin olive oil to finish
items.raw: Extra virgin olive oil to finish

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, and salt in a bowl. Add the water and oil and bring together into a shaggy dough. Tip onto the bench and knead 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place in an oiled bowl, cover, and rise at room temperature for 90 minutes (or in the fridge overnight for better flavour). It should double.
Crush the tomatoes by hand into a bowl. Stir in the garlic, oil, and salt. Don't cook it.
Heat the oven as hot as it will go (250°C / 480°F) with a pizza stone or heavy baking tray inside for at least 30 minutes.
Divide the dough in two. On a floured bench, stretch one ball into a 28cm round using your fingertips, leave a thicker rim. Don't use a rolling pin.
Slide the base onto a piece of baking paper. Spread a thin layer of tomato to within 2cm of the edge. Dot with torn mozzarella.
Slide the pizza (on the paper) onto the hot stone. Bake 6–8 minutes until the crust is blistered and the cheese pools.
Tear basil over the top. Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil. Repeat with the second dough ball.

notes: A hot oven is non-negotiable. If yours only goes to 220°C, give it 10 minutes longer to preheat.
Cold dough is more forgiving. The overnight fridge rest is worth doing.

title: Massaman Curry
summary: Beef chuck and potato slowly braised in a mild, warm-spiced coconut and peanut curry.

steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Spoon in 3 tbsp of the thick coconut cream and the curry paste. Fry, stirring constantly, for 4 minutes until the oil separates and the paste smells aromatic.
Add the beef and stir to coat in the paste. Cook 3 minutes.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk and cream, plus 250ml water. Add the fish sauce, tamarind, palm sugar, cardamom, cinnamon, and bay leaves.
Bring to a gentle simmer, half-cover, and cook on the lowest heat for 60 minutes. Stir every 15 minutes.
Add the potato, onion, and half the peanuts. Continue cooking uncovered for another 25–30 minutes until the beef is fork-tender and the potatoes are soft but holding shape.
Taste, adjust with extra fish sauce, palm sugar, or tamarind. The balance should be slightly sweet, slightly tangy, deeply savoury, not very spicy.
Serve over jasmine rice. Scatter with the remaining peanuts and fried shallots, with lime on the side.

notes: Massaman is the gentle giant of Thai curries, sweet, warm-spiced, almost Persian. Slow heat, no hurry.
Chuck steak is the right cut, it takes the time and rewards you with melting texture.

title: Meatloaf
summary: A tender beef and pork loaf baked free-form under a sweet, tangy ketchup glaze.

items.raw: 1 large onion, finely diced and softened in oil
items.prep: finely diced and softened in oil

steps.text: Soak the panko in the milk for 5 minutes, this panade keeps the loaf moist.
In a wide bowl, combine the cooked onion, garlic, soaked panko, eggs, Worcestershire, mustard, tomato paste, thyme, salt, and pepper. Whisk well.
Add both minces. Mix with your hands just until uniform, don't overwork or the texture turns rubbery.
Heat the oven to 190°C. Line a tray with foil. Form the meat into a 25cm long loaf, freestanding (a tin makes it boil in its own fat).
Whisk the glaze ingredients. Brush half over the loaf.
Bake 30 minutes. Brush with another layer of glaze. Bake 25 more minutes, internal temperature 70°C.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing. Brush with the remaining glaze just before serving.

notes: Free-form, not a loaf tin. Tin meatloaf boils in its own juices.
Cook your onion before mixing, raw onion stays crunchy in baked meatloaf.

title: Mediterranean Platter
summary: A generous board of dips, cheeses, cured meats, pickles and warm pita for sharing.

items.raw: 4 warm pitas, torn or cut into wedges

items.item: Extra virgin olive oil for drizzling
items.raw: Extra virgin olive oil for drizzling

steps.text: On the largest board or platter you own, spoon the spreads in three pools. Use the back of a spoon to swirl each. Drizzle olive oil over.
Dust hummus with sumac and paprika. Dust labneh with za'atar.
Around the spreads, place the cheeses, meats, vegetables, and pickles in groups.
Tuck warm pita and crackers wherever there's space.
Scatter pomegranate, mint, and parsley over the whole thing.
Bring to the table with lemon wedges. Serve immediately, the joy is the variety.

notes: The platter is the recipe. Buy excellent versions of each component, it's an assembly job, not a cooking job.
Pomegranate seeds and fresh herbs scattered last lifts a mostly-bought platter into something special.

title: Minestrone
summary: A thick vegetable, bean and pasta soup built on a parmesan rind, finished with pesto.

items.raw: Large handful baby spinach or shredded kale

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot. If using pancetta, render it for 4 minutes. Add onion, carrot, and celery. Cook 10 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and tomato paste; cook 2 minutes.
Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, parmesan rind, bay, and oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Add the potatoes. Simmer 12 minutes.
Add the zucchini, green beans, and cannellini beans. Simmer 8 minutes.
Add the pasta. Cook per packet (usually 8 minutes), then off the heat fold in the spinach to wilt.
Fish out the parmesan rind and bay. Season heavily.
Ladle into bowls. Drizzle with pesto and grate parmesan over the top.

notes: A parmesan rind in the pot is the move. Save them in the freezer for soups.
Better the next day. Add a splash of stock when reheating to loosen.

title: Miso Soup
summary: A homemade kombu and bonito dashi with miso, silken tofu, wakame and spring onion.

items.raw: 4 tbsp white or red miso paste (or a mix)
4 tbsp dried wakame seaweed (rehydrated in cold water 5 min)

steps.text: Wipe the kombu with a dry cloth (don't wash, the white powder is umami). Soak in 1L cold water for 30 minutes if you can.
Bring slowly to just-below-simmer. The instant tiny bubbles appear at the kombu edges, lift it out (longer = bitter).
Bring to a gentle simmer. Add bonito flakes. Cook 1 minute, then turn off the heat. Let flakes sink, 2 minutes.
Strain through fine mesh. This is dashi.
Return dashi to the pot. Warm to just below a simmer, never boil after this.
In a small bowl, whisk a ladleful of warm dashi into the miso paste until smooth, then pour back into the pot.
Add tofu, drained wakame, and mushrooms. Heat 90 seconds, no more.
Ladle into bowls. Scatter spring onion.

notes: Never boil miso. Boiling destroys the live cultures and the delicate flavour.
Dilute miso in a ladleful before adding to the pot, stops clumping.

title: Moussaka
summary: Grilled eggplant and cinnamon-spiced lamb under a firm, golden béchamel.

steps.text: Salt the eggplant slices and rest on a rack for 30 minutes to draw out moisture. Pat dry.
Brush the eggplant lightly with oil and grill in batches in a hot griddle pan or oven (220°C for 15 min) until softened and lightly charred.
Brown the lamb in olive oil over high heat for 6 minutes. Add the onion and cook 8 minutes. Add garlic and tomato paste; cook 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine, let it reduce by half, then add the tinned tomatoes, cinnamon, allspice, bay, and oregano. Simmer 30 minutes until thick. Season.
For the bechamel: melt butter, whisk in flour, cook 2 minutes. Whisk in warm milk gradually. Cook 8 minutes until thick. Season with nutmeg, salt, pepper.
Off the heat, whisk in the egg yolks and half the cheese. The eggs make moussaka bechamel different from lasagna's, they set firm when baked.
Build in a deep baking dish: a single layer of eggplant, half the lamb, eggplant again, the rest of the lamb, a final layer of eggplant.
Pour the bechamel over the top and smooth flat. Scatter the remaining cheese.
Bake at 180°C for 45 minutes until the top is deep golden brown and set firm.
This is the hard part: rest 30 minutes before cutting. Hot moussaka collapses. The wait is the dish.

notes: Eggplant must be cooked through before assembly, raw eggplant under bechamel stays bitter.
Cinnamon and allspice in the lamb sound wrong but make moussaka taste like moussaka.

title: Mushroom Risotto
summary: Carnaroli cooked with porcini-enriched stock and golden mixed mushrooms.

items.raw: 500g mixed mushrooms (button, chestnut, oyster, shiitake), sliced
20g dried porcini, soaked in 250ml hot water for 20 minutes
items.prep: soaked in 250ml hot water for 20 minutes

items.raw: 1L vegetable stock (or chicken stock), kept warm

steps.text: Sauté the fresh mushrooms in olive oil over high heat with garlic and thyme for 6 minutes until deep golden. Season. Set aside.
Squeeze the porcini dry (reserve the soaking liquid, strain it for grit). Chop the porcini. Add the strained liquid to the warm stock.
In a wide pan, melt the butter with oil. Sweat the onion 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the rice. Toast 2 minutes until the edges look glassy.
Pour in the wine. Stir until absorbed.
Add a ladle of stock. Stir gently until almost absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 16 minutes.
In the last 3 minutes, fold in the cooked mushrooms and chopped porcini.
Off the heat, vigorously beat in the cold butter and parmesan, this is the mantecatura.
Cover and rest 2 minutes. Plate onto warm dishes. Drizzle with truffle oil if using. Scatter parsley.

notes: Dried porcini in the stock is the move. Earthy, deep, transformative.
Off-heat butter and cheese at the end. Hot butter splits, hot cheese clumps.

title: Nasi Goreng
summary: Day-old rice fried hard with shrimp paste and kecap manis, topped with a runny egg.

items.raw: 3 cups cold cooked jasmine rice (day-old is ideal)

steps.text: Break up the cold rice with your fingers so there are no clumps. Cold rice = separate grains = proper fried rice.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until it shimmers. Add the garlic, chillies, and onion. Stir-fry 1 minute.
Add the shrimp paste and break it up, it smells terrible, then transforms.
Tip in the chicken. Stir-fry 3 minutes until just cooked. Add the prawns and toss for another minute.
Add the rice and break it up against the wok with your spatula. Toss constantly for 2 minutes until heated through and dotted with brown crispy bits.
Pour in the kecap manis, soy, and oyster sauce. Toss for another minute, every grain should be coated dark brown.
Pile onto plates. Top each serve with a fried egg (yolk runny). Garnish with cucumber, tomato, prawn crackers, fried shallots, and lime.

notes: Hot wok, fresh ingredients, cold rice. Anyone who fries rice in a cold pan gets mush.
Kecap manis (sweet soy) is non-negotiable, that's what makes it Indonesian.

title: Niçoise Salad
summary: A composed platter of tuna, jammy eggs, potatoes, beans and olives with a sharp dressing.

items.raw: 300g good-quality tuna in olive oil (jarred is best)
1 small red onion or 2 shallots, finely sliced

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, 15 minutes. Lift out (keep the water).
Drop the beans into the same water for 90 seconds, then plunge into iced water to keep them bright green. Drain.
Lower the eggs (fridge-cold) into boiling water for 7 minutes for a jammy yolk. Cool in iced water. Peel and quarter.
Whisk the dressing. Taste, should be sharp.
Halve the potatoes while warm and dress with 2 tbsp of the dressing. Let them soak it up.
On a wide platter, lay down a bed of cos. Arrange everything else in composed groups: dressed potatoes, beans, eggs, broken-up tuna chunks, tomatoes, olives, anchovies, capers, red onion.
Drizzle the remaining dressing across the whole platter. Crack pepper on top.

notes: Composed, not tossed. The visual is the point.
Jarred tuna in olive oil > tinned in water. Worth spending on.

title: Okonomiyaki
summary: A savoury cabbage pancake topped with pork belly, sauce, mayonnaise and bonito.

items.item: thin slices pork belly or streaky bacon
items.raw: 8 thin slices pork belly or streaky bacon

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, and dashi powder. Add the water and eggs, whisk to a smooth batter.
Tip in the cabbage, spring onion, and pickled ginger. Mix gently, you want the cabbage coated in batter but still distinct, not pulverised.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat with the oil. Spoon in half the cabbage mixture and shape into a thick round about 18cm wide.
Lay 4 slices of pork belly across the top, pressing them in lightly.
Cover with a lid. Cook 6 minutes until the bottom is deep golden brown.
Flip carefully, slide onto a plate first, then invert back into the pan, pork-side-down. Cover again. Cook 5 more minutes until the pork is crisp.
Slide onto a plate, pork-side-up. Brush with okonomi sauce in a heavy criss-cross. Zigzag the mayo on top.
Scatter bonito flakes generously, they'll dance from the heat. Finish with aonori.
Repeat with the rest of the mixture for the second pancake.

notes: Lid on for the first side, steams the cabbage through without burning the bottom.
The dancing bonito flakes are showmanship, but they also add a deep umami hit.

title: Omelette
summary: A pale, soft French omelette rolled around its filling while still glossy inside.

steps.text: Crack the eggs into a bowl. Beat with a fork until just combined, no white streaks, but stop before you whip in air. Season lightly.
Heat a 22cm non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Add the butter. Swirl until it foams but doesn't brown.
Pour in the eggs. Immediately start moving them with a rubber spatula: pull the set edges into the centre and tilt the pan so liquid runs to fill the gaps. Do this for 30 seconds.
When the surface is still glossy and just-set (the French call it baveuse, slightly underdone), stop stirring. Add fillings down the centre.
Tilt the pan away from you. Use the spatula to fold the edge closest to you over the fillings. Then roll the omelette toward the far edge of the pan and out onto a plate, seam-side-down.
The omelette should be pale yellow with no brown crust. Soft inside, just barely set outside.
Eat immediately. Omelettes wait for no one.

notes: Pale, not brown. A browned omelette is a frittata that lost its way.
Low heat, butter foaming, constant motion. Get those three right and you can't fail.

title: Osso Buco
summary: Veal shanks braised in white wine and tomato, finished with a sharp gremolata.

items.raw: 4 thick cross-cut veal shanks (about 4cm thick, 300g each)

steps.text: Tie each shank around its circumference with kitchen twine, stops it falling apart in the braise.
Season heavily and dredge in flour.
Heat the oil in a heavy Dutch oven. Brown the shanks 4 minutes a side until deep mahogany. Lift out.
Reduce heat. Melt the butter. Add onion, carrot, and celery. Cook 12 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and tomato paste; cook 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine. Reduce by half. Add the tomatoes, stock, bay, and thyme.
Return the shanks bone-side-up so the marrow stays put. The liquid should come about two-thirds up.
Cover. Braise at 160°C for 2.5 hours until the meat is fall-off-the-bone tender.
Lift the shanks gently. Reduce the sauce on the stove for 5 minutes if it needs body.
Mix the gremolata.
Plate each shank with sauce spooned over. Scatter gremolata heavily. Serve on saffron risotto or polenta.
Don't forget the marrow, scoop it out with a small spoon and spread on bread or stir into the risotto.

notes: The marrow is the prize. Bone-side-up to keep it in the bone during braising.
Gremolata is the foil to the rich braise. Don't skip, it lifts the whole dish.

title: Pad Thai
summary: Rice noodles tossed hot with tamarind, fish sauce, prawns and a crunch of peanuts.

items.raw: 3 tbsp palm sugar (or brown sugar), grated
200g raw prawns, peeled (or firm tofu, cubed)

items.item: Lime wedges and coriander to serve
items.raw: Lime wedges and coriander to serve

steps.text: Soak the noodles in warm water for 20 minutes until pliable but still firm. Drain.
Combine the sauce ingredients in a small bowl. Stir until the sugar dissolves. Taste, it should hit salty, sour, and sweet equally. Adjust with extra tamarind, sugar, or fish sauce.
Heat a wok or large frypan over high heat until smoking. Add 1 tbsp oil and the prawns. Stir-fry 1 minute until just pink. Push to the side.
Add the remaining oil and the garlic. Pour in the eggs and let them set for 10 seconds before breaking them into curds.
Add the drained noodles and the sauce. Toss continuously with tongs for 2 minutes, the noodles should soak up the sauce and turn a glossy amber.
Throw in the spring onions, most of the bean sprouts, and most of the peanuts. Toss for 30 seconds, you want some crunch left.
Tip onto plates. Top with the rest of the sprouts and peanuts, a wedge of lime, coriander, and chilli flakes if you like heat.

notes: High heat, a wide pan, small batches. Cooking for 4 means cooking two pairs.
Tamarind paste varies in strength, start with less and build.

title: Paella
summary: Saffron rice with chicken, chorizo and seafood, left unstirred to form the socarrat.

items.raw: Large pinch of saffron, steeped in 2 tbsp hot water

steps.text: In a wide shallow paella pan or large frypan (no deeper than 5cm), heat the olive oil. Brown the chicken in a single layer for 5 minutes. Lift out.
Add the chorizo. Cook 2 minutes until its red oil runs. Lift out, leaving the oil.
Add the onion and capsicum. Cook 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and smoked paprika; cook 1 minute.
Stir in the blitzed tomato. Cook 5 minutes until darkened and reduced, this is the sofrito, the base of the dish.
Add the rice and stir to coat. Toast 2 minutes.
Pour in the saffron water, then the hot stock. Add salt. Tuck the chicken back in.
Now don't stir. From this point on, no stirring, this lets the bottom develop the crust (socarrat) which is the whole point.
Simmer over medium heat for 15 minutes. The rice should be visible above the stock.
Nestle in the prawns, mussels, peas, and chorizo. Cook another 8 minutes, the prawns should be pink, the shells of the mussels open.
Turn the heat up high for the final 1–2 minutes. Listen, you want to hear gentle crackling from the bottom. That's the socarrat forming. Stop before it burns.
Off the heat, cover with foil and rest 5 minutes. Top with parsley and lemon. Serve straight from the pan.

notes: Bomba rice absorbs liquid without going gluey. Arborio risotto rice is the wrong choice.
The socarrat, the crunchy caramelised crust on the base, is the badge of a good paella. Listen for the crackle.

title: Paneer Butter Masala
summary: Golden paneer in a velvety tomato, cashew and cream sauce scented with fenugreek.

items.raw: 60g cashews, soaked in hot water 15 minutes then blitzed smooth with 100ml water
items.prep: soaked in hot water 15 minutes then blitzed smooth with 100ml water

items.raw: 1 tbsp dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), crumbled

steps.text: Heat the oil and pan-fry the paneer cubes until golden on all sides. Drain.
In a heavy pan, melt the butter with the oil. Cook the onion 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute. Stir in the chilli, coriander, cumin, and turmeric. Toast 30 seconds.
Add the tomato paste, then the blitzed tomato. Simmer 10 minutes until darkened and the oil splits.
Stir in the cashew paste and a splash of water. Simmer 5 minutes.
Blend the sauce smooth with a stick blender for the velvety restaurant texture.
Stir in the cream, garam masala, sugar, and crumbled fenugreek. Slip the paneer in. Simmer 5 minutes, just to warm through and let the flavours marry.
Taste, adjust salt. Finish with a knob of butter off the heat.
Serve with rice or naan, scattered with coriander.

notes: Cashews + cream = the silky luxe sauce. Don't skip the cashews.
Fenugreek (kasuri methi) gives the signature aroma. Find at any Indian grocer.

title: Pastrami Sandwich
summary: Steamed deli pastrami piled high on rye with mustard and dill pickles.

items.raw: 400g good-quality pastrami, sliced thin (from a deli)

items.item: Jewish rye bread or marbled rye
items.raw: 4 slices Jewish rye bread or marbled rye
4 large dill pickles, sliced thin (or kept whole on the side)
items.note: or kept whole on the side

steps.text: Bring the pastrami to room temperature.

Steam the pastrami: set a colander or steamer over simmering water. Drop the pastrami in, cover, and steam 4 minutes until hot and the fat has softened. (Or microwave 30 seconds, purists weep, but it works.)
Meanwhile, toast the rye lightly (just enough to firm up, no browning).
Smear mustard generously on every cut side. Pile the hot pastrami onto two slices, make the mound at least 5cm tall.
Add pickle slices on top of the meat.
Top with the second slice of bread. Press down gently.
Cut on the diagonal. Eat immediately with extra mustard and a whole pickle on the side.

notes: Steam the pastrami. Cold deli pastrami is sad, hot is the whole point of a pastrami on rye.
Mustard not mayo. Mayo on pastrami is a thought crime.

title: Peking Duck
summary: Air-dried, lacquered duck roasted to crackling, rolled in pancakes with hoisin.

items.raw: 12–16 thin pancakes (Chinese steamed pancakes, buy frozen)
6 spring onions, white parts cut into thin strips
items.prep: white parts cut into thin strips

steps.text: A day ahead: rinse the duck and pat very dry. Mix the salt and five-spice and rub inside the cavity. Truss the legs with twine.
Stand the duck on a rack over the sink. Pour 2 litres of boiling water slowly over the skin, it will tighten visibly. Pat dry.
Whisk the honey, soy sauce, wine, and vinegar. Brush all over the skin.
Sit the duck on a rack over a tray, uncovered, in the fridge overnight. The skin must dry out, this is the entire secret to crispiness.
The next day: heat the oven to 200°C. Place the duck breast-side-up on a rack over a roasting tray with a cup of water in the bottom (catches drips, stops smoke).
Roast 90 minutes, basting with the honey mixture every 30 minutes. The skin should be deep mahogany and crackling crisp.
Increase the heat to 220°C for the final 10 minutes if needed for extra crisp.
Rest 15 minutes. Carve the breast and crispy skin in thin slices.
To eat: warm a pancake (steamer or microwave), spread with hoisin, lay on cucumber, spring onion, and a few slices of skin and meat. Roll up.

notes: Dry skin is everything. The overnight uncovered fridge rest is non-negotiable. Anything else makes leathery, not crackling, skin.
Buy the pancakes. Making them from scratch is a separate full project.

title: Penne Arrabbiata
summary: Penne in a sharp, fiery tomato sauce built on garlic and plenty of chilli.

items.raw: 1–2 tsp chilli flakes (depending on heat tolerance)

items.item: passata or 800g tinned San Marzano tomatoes
items.raw: 700g passata or 800g tinned San Marzano tomatoes, crushed
40g grated parmesan or pecorino (optional, Romans purists skip cheese)

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a wide pan over low heat. Add garlic and chilli flakes. Sizzle 90 seconds without colour.
Stir in tomato paste; cook 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, sugar, and salt. Simmer 12 minutes until the sauce darkens and thickens.
While the sauce cooks, boil the pasta in well-salted water until just shy of al dente. Reserve pasta water.
Tip pasta into the sauce with 3 tbsp pasta water. Toss for 60 seconds.
Fold in parsley. Plate. Pecorino if you like, but Romans say no.

notes: Arrabbiata = "angry" in Italian. Don't shy on the chilli.
Roman tradition is no cheese. The sharp tomato and chilli stand alone.

title: Pepperoni Pizza
summary: Spicy pepperoni that curls into crisp cups over tomato and mozzarella.

items.raw: Pinch of salt, sugar, and dried oregano

steps.text: Heat the oven to 240°C with a pizza stone or heavy tray inside.
Mix the passata with garlic, olive oil, salt, sugar, and oregano.
Stretch each base. Spread a thin layer of sauce.
Dot with mozzarella. Lay pepperoni slices over the top.

Slide onto the hot stone. Bake 8–10 minutes until the crust is blistered, the cheese is bubbling, and the pepperoni edges are curled into little crispy cups (that's the prize, buy curl-up pepperoni if possible).
Tear basil over the top. Crack pepper. Drizzle olive oil. Chilli flakes for those who want heat.

notes: Good pepperoni curls into cups when it cooks, holding little pools of orange oil. That's the pizza-cup effect, chase it.
Hot oven, fast bake. Long bake at low heat = sad pizza.

title: Peri Peri Chicken
summary: Spatchcocked chicken roasted in a fiery chilli, garlic and lemon sauce.

items.raw: 1 whole chicken (1.6kg), spatchcocked (backbone removed and flattened)

steps.text: Blitz all peri-peri sauce ingredients to a smooth paste. Reserve half for serving.
Pat the spatchcocked chicken dry. Salt all over. Rub the remaining half of the peri-peri sauce all over, working under the skin where possible. Rest 1 hour (or overnight).
Heat the oven to 200°C with a rack in the middle. Place the chicken skin-side-up on a foil-lined tray.
Roast 40 minutes, basting halfway, until the juices run clear and a thermometer in the thigh reads 75°C. The skin should be deeply burnished, almost black at the edges.
Rest 10 minutes on a board. Cut into pieces.
Drizzle the reserved peri-peri sauce over the chicken before serving. Serve with chips, garlic mayo, salad, and lemon.

notes: Spatchcocking is the key, it cooks the bird evenly and fast, and gives more skin to char.
Half the sauce for marinade, half for finishing. Cooking destroys some heat and brightness, fresh sauce on top adds it back.

title: Pesto Pasta
summary: Fresh basil and pine nut pesto loosened with pasta water and never cooked.

items.item: Extra parmesan and basil to serve
items.raw: Extra parmesan and basil to serve

steps.text: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan over medium-low heat for 3 minutes until just golden. Watch them, they burn the second you turn your back. Cool.
In a food processor, pulse the garlic, pine nuts, and a pinch of salt to a coarse paste. Add the basil and pulse until chopped but not pureed.
Tip into a bowl. Stir in the cheeses, then the olive oil in a stream. The pesto should be loose enough to coat, thick enough to hold its shape on a spoon.
Cook the pasta in well-salted water until al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water before draining.
Tip the hot pasta into a wide bowl. Add the pesto (off the heat, never cook pesto, it kills the basil) and 2 tbsp of pasta water. Toss until each piece is coated.
Add more water if it looks dry. Top with extra parmesan and a few whole basil leaves.

notes: Genoese style: traditionally with thin green beans and waxy potato added to the pasta water. Worth trying.
Pesto darkens fast. Make right before using, or press cling film flat to the surface and refrigerate up to 2 days.

title: Pho
summary: A clear, charred-onion beef broth poured over rice noodles and paper-thin fillet.

items.raw: 300g eye fillet, sliced as thin as possible

steps.text: Blanch the bones and brisket in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain, rinse off the scum, and discard the water, this is the secret to a clean broth.
Char the onion and ginger directly over a gas flame (or under a hot grill) until blackened in patches. The smokiness defines pho.
Dry-toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, coriander seeds, and cardamom in a pan for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Combine the rinsed bones and brisket in a stockpot with the charred aromatics, toasted spices, fish sauce, sugar, and salt. Cover with 4 litres of water.
Bring to a gentle simmer (never a rolling boil, broth must stay clear). Skim any scum off the top for the first 30 minutes.
After 90 minutes, pull the brisket out and rest in cold water for 5 minutes to stop cooking. Slice thin and set aside.
Continue simmering the broth for another 90 minutes. Strain through a fine mesh into a clean pot. Taste and adjust with fish sauce and sugar.
Soak the rice noodles in hot water for 8–10 minutes until pliable. Drain into bowls.
Lay the raw eye fillet over the noodles. Top with sliced onion and the cooked brisket. Pour over the boiling broth, it will cook the raw beef in seconds.
Bring the bowls to the table with a platter of herbs, sprouts, lime, chilli, and the sauces. Each person builds their own.

notes: A clear, deeply flavoured broth is the entire dish. Low and slow, never boil.
Freeze the eye fillet for 30 minutes before slicing, you'll get paper-thin cuts.

title: Picanha
summary: Rump cap grilled fat-side down with rock salt, sliced thin with a sharp tomato vinagrete.

items.raw: 1.2kg whole picanha (rump cap), fat cap on, untrimmed

steps.text: Pat the picanha dry. Don't trim the fat cap, it bastes the meat as it cooks.
Score the fat cap in a crosshatch, 1cm deep. Rub the salt and pepper into both sides, focusing on the fat.
Cut the picanha across the grain into 4cm thick steaks (the traditional churrasco method curls each piece into a C on a skewer).
Skewer each piece in a C-shape if cooking on a grill, with the fat cap on the outside.
Mix all vinagrete ingredients and rest 15 minutes.
Heat a BBQ or grill plate to high. Place the meat fat-side-down first to render. After 6–8 minutes, the fat should be deeply golden and crackling.
Flip and grill the meat sides 2–3 minutes each for medium-rare.
Rest 8 minutes on a board. Slice each piece against the grain into 5mm strips, the fat cap should be on every slice.
Serve immediately with vinagrete, farofa, and beans.

notes: Picanha (rump cap) is one cut, with one fat cap. Get it from a butcher, supermarkets often trim and split it.
Rock salt and high heat. No marinades, no rubs. The cut speaks for itself.

title: Pierogi
summary: Potato and cheese dumplings, boiled then crisped in caramelised onion butter.

items.raw: 1 small onion, finely diced and softened in 1 tbsp butter
items.prep: finely diced and softened in 1 tbsp butter

steps.text: Mix the flour, egg, water, sour cream, and salt into a soft dough. Knead 5 minutes until smooth and elastic. Rest under a bowl for 30 minutes.
Boil the potatoes until tender. Drain and mash smooth. Mix in the cheeses, cooked onion, chives, and seasoning. Cool completely.
For the topping: melt 60g butter in a wide pan. Add the sliced onions and a pinch of salt. Cook 20 minutes over medium-low heat, stirring often, until deeply caramelised.
Roll the dough out 2mm thin on a floured bench. Cut 8cm circles with a glass or cutter.
Spoon a tablespoon of filling onto each circle. Fold in half, press out air, and crimp the edges firmly with your fingers or a fork. Lay on a floured tray.
Bring a big pot of well-salted water to a gentle boil. Drop pierogi in batches. They're done 90 seconds after they float to the surface, about 3 minutes total.
Lift out with a slotted spoon directly into the caramelised onion pan. Toss to coat. Cook 1 minute per side until the edges crisp in the butter.
Serve with sour cream, dill, and pepper.

notes: Boil first, then pan-fry in the onion butter. That double-cook gives the soft-then-crisp texture.
Make a triple batch and freeze raw on trays, fry from frozen, no defrosting.

title: Poke Bowl
summary: Marinated raw tuna over seasoned sushi rice with avocado, edamame and spicy mayonnaise.

items.raw: 400g sashimi-grade tuna or salmon, in 2cm cubes
2 cups warm sushi rice (rinsed, cooked, seasoned with 2 tbsp rice vinegar + 1 tbsp sugar + 1/2 tsp salt)
items.note: rinsed, cooked, seasoned with 2 tbsp rice vinegar + 1 tbsp sugar + 1/2 tsp salt

items.raw: Furikake seasoning (or just sesame + crushed nori)

steps.text: Mix the tuna marinade ingredients. Fold the cubed fish through. Rest 10 minutes.
Whisk the spicy mayo.
Divide warm rice between two deep bowls.
Arrange the marinated fish, avocado, cucumber, carrot, and edamame in colour-blocked sections over the rice.
Drizzle with spicy mayo in a zigzag.
Top with pickled ginger, spring onion greens, and a heavy scatter of furikake.
Eat by mixing your way through, building each bite however you like.

notes: Sashimi-grade fish only. Anything else is sushi roulette.
Warm rice, cold fish, room-temp veg, that thermal contrast is half the appeal.
Uses raw fish. Not recommended during pregnancy or for anyone with a weakened immune system.

title: Pork Adobo
summary: Pork braised in soy, vinegar and garlic, reduced to a glaze and crisped at the edges.

items.raw: 1kg pork belly or pork shoulder, in 3cm cubes

steps.text: Combine pork, soy, vinegar, garlic, bay, peppercorns, sugar, and water in a heavy pot.
Bring to a boil over high heat without stirring. (Filipino kitchen rule, let the vinegar boil off before stirring.)
Reduce to a simmer and cover. Cook 30 minutes.
Uncover and turn the heat to medium-high. Reduce the sauce for 20 minutes, turning the pork occasionally, until the liquid is a glossy syrup and clings to the meat.
Optional but transformative: lift the pork out and crisp in a hot pan with 1 tbsp oil for 3 minutes, those crackling edges are the prize.
Toss in the reduced sauce. Serve over rice. Scatter spring onion and fried garlic.

notes: Don't stir while the vinegar boils. Cuts the sharp acidic edge.
Crisping at the end is the move every Filipino home cook does to the leftovers, do it the first night too.

title: Pork Belly Bao
summary: Soy-braised pork belly in steamed buns with pickled cucumber, hoisin and peanuts.

items.raw: 800g pork belly, skin on, in 4cm pieces
8 bao buns (frozen, from Asian grocer, steam per packet)
items.note: frozen, from Asian grocer, steam per packet

steps.text: Blanch the pork belly: cover in cold water in a pot, bring to a boil, simmer 5 minutes. Drain and rinse, removes scum.
In a heavy pot, combine the pork with both soy sauces, sugar, wine, garlic, ginger, star anise, cinnamon, spring onion whites, and water. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise on the lowest heat for 2 hours, turning the pork once. Then uncover and reduce on medium heat for another 30 minutes, the liquid should be a glossy syrup.
Mix the cucumber with vinegar, sugar, and salt. Rest 15 minutes.
Steam the bao buns per packet (usually 8 minutes from frozen).
Slice the pork belly into 1cm thick pieces.
Open each bao. Smear with hoisin and a dot of sriracha. Lay in 2–3 slices of pork. Top with pickled cucumber, peanuts, coriander, and spring onion.

notes: Slow-braised belly is unctuous and worth the time. No shortcuts.
Steam bao gently, over-steaming makes them slimy.

title: Pork Dumplings
summary: Juicy pork and cabbage dumplings, boiled or pan-fried, with a black vinegar dip.

items.raw: 200g napa cabbage, finely shredded, salted with 1 tsp and squeezed dry
items.prep: finely shredded, salted with 1 tsp and squeezed dry

steps.text: Combine all filling ingredients. Stir vigorously in one direction for 2 minutes.

Fold each dumpling: place a heaped teaspoon of filling in the centre of a wrapper. Wet half the edge with water. Fold in half and pleat (3–5 pleats across the front, pressed against the flat back). Lay flat-bottomed on a floured tray.

To boil: bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Drop in dumplings in batches. Stir gently to stop sticking. When they float, add 1 cup of cold water. When they float again, they're done, about 6 minutes total.

To pan-fry (potsticker style): heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide non-stick pan. Arrange flat-side-down. Cook 2 minutes until golden. Add 100ml water and cover. Steam 5 minutes. Uncover and crisp the bases another minute.
Whisk the dipping sauce.
Serve dumplings hot with sauce, about 6–8 per person.

notes: Fat is flavour. Lean pork mince makes dry dumplings.
Stir in one direction to develop springy texture. Random stirring makes crumbly filling.

title: Pork Fried Rice
summary: Cold rice fried with crisp-edged pork mince, egg and peas in a hot wok.

steps.text: Break up the cold rice with your fingers.
Whisk the sauce ingredients.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over screaming-high heat. Stir-fry the pork until brown and crispy bits form, 5 minutes.
Add another tbsp oil. Pour in eggs. Let them set 5 seconds, then scramble.
Add the last tbsp oil. Add onion and carrot; stir-fry 2 minutes. Add garlic and ginger; toss 30 seconds.
Add the cold rice. Spread it across the wok for 30 seconds to crisp the bottom. Then toss for 2 minutes.
Add the peas. Pour the sauce around the edges. Toss for 60 seconds, every grain glossy brown.
Off the heat, fold in spring onions.

notes: Cold rice, hot wok, fast. Same rules as ever.
Crispy bits of pork are the prize. Don't stir too much during the first cook.

title: Pork Roast
summary: Dry-salted pork roasted high then low for deep crackling, with fennel and rosemary.

items.raw: 2kg pork loin or shoulder, skin on, scored deeply

steps.text: A day ahead: pat the pork dry. Score the skin in deep lines, 5mm deep, every 1cm, through the skin and fat but not the meat. Rub salt heavily into the score lines. Sit on a rack uncovered in the fridge overnight, dry skin is the crackling secret.
The next day: pat any moisture off the skin. Rub the oil into the cuts. Sprinkle with garlic, fennel, rosemary, pepper, and lemon zest.
Heat the oven to 230°C. Place the pork on a rack over a tray. Roast 30 minutes at high heat, this gets the crackling going.
Reduce to 180°C and roast another 1.5–2 hours, depending on size. Internal temperature 65°C in the meat.
If the crackling isn't fully puffed and crisp, crank back to 230°C for 10 more minutes at the end (watch it).
Rest 20 minutes. Cut off the crackling in one sheet first, then slice the meat. Break the crackling into shards.
Plate with roast vegetables, apple sauce, and gravy.

notes: Score deep, salt heavily, dry overnight in the fridge. Three rules. Skipping any one ruins the crackling.
High heat to start, lower heat to cook through. The two-temp roast is the formula.

title: Pork Schnitzel
summary: Thin pork loin crumbed and fried in foaming butter, with lemon and apple sauce.

items.raw: 4 pork loin steaks (about 200g each), pounded to 5mm thin

steps.text: Pound the pork between cling film with a mallet until evenly 5mm thick. Season.
Set up flour, egg-milk, and breadcrumbs. Dredge each schnitzel in flour, dip in egg, then press into breadcrumbs lightly (don't pack the crumbs).
Heat the butter and oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat until the butter foams.
Swim the schnitzel, there should be enough fat to bubble around it. Cook 2 minutes a side, basting with the hot fat for that classic puffed, rippled breadcrumb crust.
Drain on a rack briefly. Serve immediately with lemon, parsley potatoes, and apple sauce on the side.

notes: Pound thin and even. A schnitzel cooks in 4 minutes total.
Basting with the hot fat creates the signature rippled crust.

title: Pork Tacos
summary: Orange-braised pork shoulder fried crisp as carnitas, in charred corn tortillas.

items.raw: Juice of 2 oranges + the squeezed orange halves
3 tbsp lard or neutral oil (for finishing)
12 small corn tortillas, warmed and charred

steps.text: Toss pork chunks with salt, cumin, paprika, oregano, and pepper.
Layer in a heavy pot or Dutch oven with garlic, onion, bay, squeezed orange halves, orange and lime juice, and stock.
Cover and braise at 160°C for 3 hours, until the pork is completely tender.
Lift out the pork. Discard onion, bay, orange halves.
Reduce the braising liquid in a pan until it's a thick glaze.
In a wide pan, heat the lard over high heat. Add the pork chunks and fry, pressing down with a spatula, for 6 minutes, you want crispy charred edges with juicy interiors.
Toss with the reduced glaze to coat.
Char the tortillas. Build each taco: tortilla, carnitas, red onion, coriander, jalapeños, salsa verde, feta, lime squeeze.

notes: Braise then fry, the contrast of crisp edges and tender meat is the entire carnitas point.
Orange juice in the braise is traditional Michoacan. Adds sweetness and acid.

title: Prawn Curry
summary: Prawns simmered briefly in a coconut, tomato and curry leaf sauce.

items.raw: 600g raw prawns, peeled (keep some shells for stock)

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan. Add the onion and cook 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute.
Add turmeric, coriander, cumin, and chilli powder. Toast 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Add the blitzed tomato. Simmer 6 minutes until the oil splits.
Pour in the coconut milk and add curry leaves. Simmer 8 minutes until the sauce darkens and thickens.
Add the prawns. Simmer 3 minutes until just pink and curled.
Off the heat, stir in garam masala, salt, and lime juice.
Serve over rice with coriander, lime, and chilli oil.

notes: Don't overcook prawns. They go rubbery fast, 3 minutes in simmering sauce is plenty.
Goan prawn curry would add tamarind and a kokum berry instead of lime. Try both.

title: Prawn Linguine
summary: Linguine with prawns, cherry tomato, chilli and white wine, lifted by prawn-shell oil.

steps.text: Make quick prawn oil: toast the prawn shells in 2 tbsp olive oil over medium heat for 4 minutes. Strain; discard shells. (Skip if short on time, use plain olive oil.)
Cook the linguine in well-salted water until just shy of al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water; drain.
While pasta cooks, heat the prawn oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli; sizzle 90 seconds, no colour.
Add the tomatoes; press with the back of a spoon to release juice. Cook 4 minutes.
Add the prawns. Toss for 90 seconds. Pour in the wine. Reduce 90 seconds.
Add the drained pasta with a splash of pasta water. Toss for 1 minute.
Off the heat, swirl in the cold butter, lemon zest and juice, and parsley. Crack pepper.
Plate in deep bowls.

notes: No parmesan on seafood pasta. Italian rule.
Prawn-shell oil is the secret. 4 minutes of toasting transforms the dish.

title: Pulled Pork
summary: Spice-rubbed pork shoulder roasted low for hours, shredded and tossed with barbecue sauce.

items.raw: 2.5kg pork shoulder (Boston butt), bone-in if possible
2 tbsp yellow mustard (as binder for the rub)

items.item: apple juice or apple cider vinegar in a spray bottle
items.raw: 250ml apple juice or apple cider vinegar in a spray bottle

items.item: Soft burger buns or slider rolls
items.raw: Soft burger buns or slider rolls

steps.text: Combine the rub ingredients. Pat the pork dry, smear all over with mustard, then coat heavily with the rub. Press it in. Wrap and rest in the fridge overnight if possible.
Heat the oven to 130°C. Place the pork fat-side-up on a rack over a roasting tray.
Roast for 5–6 hours, spraying with apple juice every hour after the first 2. The internal temperature should reach 95°C and a fork should slide in with no resistance.
Pull the tray out, tent with foil, and rest 30 minutes, this is essential.
While the pork rests, combine the BBQ sauce ingredients in a pan. Add a few spoonfuls of the pan juices. Simmer 8 minutes. Strain or leave chunky.
Using two forks (or your hands in gloves), shred the pork. Discard any large fat pieces.
Toss the shreds with enough BBQ sauce to coat, don't drown it. The pork should be glossy, not swimming.
Pile onto buns with coleslaw on top and pickles on the side.

notes: Low and slow is non-negotiable. Anyone who rushes this dries it out.
The bark, that black peppery crust on the outside, is the prize. Don't trim it off.

title: Pumpkin Soup
summary: Roasted pumpkin, carrot and garlic blended with gentle spice and a little cream.

items.raw: 1.5kg pumpkin (butternut or kent), peeled and in chunks

items.item: good olive oil or chilli oil
items.raw: Drizzle of good olive oil or chilli oil

steps.text: Heat oven to 220°C. Toss pumpkin, onion, carrot, and unpeeled garlic with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast on a tray 30 minutes until charred at the edges. This is the soup's soul, don't skip.
Squeeze the roasted garlic out of its skins.
Tip the roasted veg into a pot. Add the spices, stock, and any pan drippings (scrape them off the tray with a splash of stock).
Simmer 10 minutes for flavours to meld.
Blend smooth with a stick blender. Add cream and warm through, don't boil.
Season generously.
Ladle into bowls. Drizzle crème fraîche. Scatter pumpkin seeds, chives, oil. Crusty bread on the side.

notes: Roast the pumpkin first. Boiled pumpkin soup tastes of nothing.
A whole head of roasted garlic, squeezed into the pot, gives the deep sweet base.

title: Quesadillas
summary: Chipotle chicken and melted cheese in crisp, blistered flour tortillas.

items.raw: 400g chicken thigh, diced (or 2 cups cooked, shredded)
1 chipotle in adobo, chopped (or 1 tsp smoked paprika + 1/2 tsp chilli powder)
items.note: or 1 tsp smoked paprika + 1/2 tsp chilli powder

items.item: Butter or oil for the pan
items.raw: Butter or oil for the pan

steps.text: Cook the diced chicken with the onion and capsicum in oil over high heat for 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, chipotle, cumin, salt, and pepper. Cook another 2 minutes until everything is glazed. Take off the heat.
On a flat surface, lay a tortilla. Sprinkle half with cheese, then chicken mixture, then more cheese, then spring onion and coriander. Fold the other half over to make a half-moon.
Heat a dry pan over medium heat. Place the quesadilla in and weigh down lightly with another pan or a spatula. Cook 3 minutes a side until deeply golden and the cheese inside has fully melted.
Slide onto a board. Rest 1 minute (cheese needs to set or it gushes out) then cut into 3 wedges.
Repeat with remaining tortillas. Serve with sour cream, salsa, avocado, and lime.

notes: Dry pan, not oily. Quesadilla skin should be papery and blistered, not greasy.
A 1-minute rest before cutting is the difference between molten cheese and an avalanche.

title: Quiche Lorraine
summary: Crisp blind-baked pastry holding a wobbling custard of bacon and Gruyère.

steps.text: For the pastry: rub the cold butter into the flour and salt until it looks like coarse breadcrumbs. Mix in the yolk and water with a knife until just combined. Press into a disc, wrap, and rest 30 minutes in the fridge.
Roll the pastry to 3mm thick. Line a 23cm tart tin with a removable base. Press into the corners. Trim the overhang. Refrigerate 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Line the pastry with paper and fill with rice or beans. Blind bake 15 minutes, then remove the paper and bake 8 more minutes until pale gold.
While the case bakes, fry the bacon and shallot in a dry pan over medium heat for 6 minutes until the bacon crisps. Drain.
Whisk the eggs, yolks, cream, and milk. Add nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Scatter the bacon, shallot, and most of the Gruyère across the pastry base. Pour in the custard.
Scatter the remaining Gruyère on top.
Reduce the oven to 170°C. Bake 35–40 minutes, the centre should still wobble like jelly when you tap the tin. It sets as it cools.
Rest 20 minutes before slicing. Serve just warm or at room temperature.

notes: A jiggly centre when you pull it out is correct, overbaked quiche turns to scrambled eggs.
Traditional Lorraine has no cheese. Most modern versions include Gruyère; I'm team Gruyère.

title: Ramen
summary: A gentle shiitake and kombu broth seasoned in the bowl, with jammy eggs and pork.

items.item: thin slices roast pork or shredded chicken
items.raw: 4 thin slices roast pork or shredded chicken
Sheet of nori, cut into rectangles

steps.text: Combine all broth ingredients in a pot. Bring to a bare simmer (don't boil, kombu turns bitter) and cook gently for 30 minutes. Strain.
For perfect 7-minute eggs, lower fridge-cold eggs into boiling water, cook 7 minutes exactly, then plunge into iced water. Peel and halve.
Whisk the tare ingredients together in a small bowl. Divide between two deep ramen bowls.
Cook the noodles in well-salted boiling water per packet, usually 2 minutes for fresh, 4 for dried. Drain.
Pour about 400ml hot broth into each bowl and whisk briefly to dissolve the tare. Add the drained noodles, lifting with chopsticks to keep them loose.
Top each bowl with two egg halves, two slices of pork, spring onion greens, sesame, nori, and a drizzle of chilli oil.

notes: The tare-in-the-bowl method is how every ramen shop does it, the broth stays clear and seasoning is precise.
Skip the marbled egg yolk drama; a 7-minute jammy yolk is the goal.

title: Ratatouille
summary: Eggplant, courgette and capsicum browned separately and folded into a rich tomato base.

items.raw: 1 tsp dried herbes de Provence (or thyme + rosemary)

steps.text: Salt the eggplant cubes and rest in a colander 20 minutes. Pat dry, this is what stops it absorbing oil like a sponge.

For the tomato base: warm olive oil in a wide pan over low heat with the garlic for 2 minutes. Add the tomato paste, blitzed tomatoes, herbs, bay, sugar, salt, and pepper. Simmer 15 minutes until thick and rich.
In another pan, brown each vegetable separately over high heat in olive oil. Eggplant 6 minutes, courgette 4 minutes, capsicum 5 minutes, onion 5 minutes. Salt each lightly.
Fold all the cooked vegetables gently into the tomato base. Stir to coat without crushing.
Simmer over low heat for 15 minutes, long enough for flavours to marry but not so long that the veg lose their shape.
Off the heat, tear basil over the top and drizzle with extra olive oil.
Serve warm or at room temperature with crusty bread.

notes: Cook each vegetable separately, then combine. One-pot ratatouille is a mush of everything that tastes the same.
Even better the next day. Make ahead.

title: Reuben Sandwich
summary: Corned beef, sauerkraut and Swiss on rye with Russian dressing, toasted until melting.

items.item: thick slices rye bread or marbled rye
items.raw: 4 thick slices rye bread or marbled rye
300g good corned beef or pastrami, sliced thin

steps.text: Whisk the Russian dressing.
Warm the corned beef briefly in a steamer or dry pan for 2 minutes.
Drain the sauerkraut hard, wet kraut soaks the bread.
Spread butter on the outside of each slice of bread. Spread dressing on the inside.
Build: bread butter-down, Swiss, corned beef, sauerkraut, more dressing, second slice butter-up.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Lay the sandwiches in. Cook 4 minutes a side, pressing gently, until deep golden and the cheese is fully melted.
Rest 1 minute. Cut diagonally.

notes: Squeeze the sauerkraut dry, non-negotiable.
Medium-low heat. High heat burns the bread before the cheese melts.

title: Risotto
summary: Carnaroli stirred with stock and wine, finished all'onda with cold butter and parmesan.

items.raw: 1.2L vegetable stock (or chicken stock), kept warm

steps.text: If making mushroom risotto: sauté the mushrooms in olive oil over high heat with garlic and thyme until deeply golden. Season and set aside.
In a wide heavy pan, melt the butter with the oil over medium heat. Sweat the onion 5 minutes until translucent, don't colour it.
Add the rice. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring, until the edges look glassy.
Pour in the wine and stir until fully absorbed.
Add a ladle of warm stock. Stir gently until almost absorbed before adding the next ladle. Continue for 16–18 minutes, the rice should be al dente with a creamy bind.
Off the heat, stir in the cold butter and the parmesan with vigour, this is the mantecatura, what makes risotto creamy.
Fold through the cooked mushrooms if using. Cover and rest 2 minutes.
Serve onto warm plates. Tap the bottom of each plate, the risotto should spread into a loose wave, not stand up in a pile. That texture is called all'onda.

notes: Don't stir constantly, that's a myth. Stir gently every few minutes; over-stirring makes it gluey.
Cold butter and finely grated cheese at the end. Hot butter splits.

title: Roast Chicken
summary: A whole bird roasted with herb butter under the skin, with a pan gravy from the tray.

steps.text: Bring chicken to room temperature 30 minutes. Pat completely dry, inside and out.
Mix the butter with garlic, chopped herbs, salt, and pepper.
Gently lift the skin over the breast (use a spoon handle). Push half the herb butter under the skin against the flesh. Rub the rest all over the outside.
Stuff the cavity with the lemon halves and thyme sprigs. Tie the legs together with twine.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Sit the onion and carrots in a roasting tray (this is the rack and the gravy base in one). Place the chicken breast-up on top.
Roast 60–70 minutes. Baste once after 30 minutes. Done when juices from the thigh run clear and a thermometer reads 75°C in the thigh.
Lift the chicken onto a board. Tent loosely with foil. Rest 15 minutes, this is non-negotiable.

For gravy: pour pan juices into a small bowl, skim fat. Place the tray over the stove. Whisk in flour; cook 2 minutes. Add wine; reduce. Add stock and reserved juices. Simmer 5 minutes. Strain. Whisk in butter.
Carve and serve with gravy, potatoes, and greens.

notes: Butter under the skin is the move. It bastes from inside the chicken as it cooks.
Rest the bird. 15 minutes minimum. Carve early and the juices run out.

title: Roasted Veggie Bowl
summary: Spiced roast vegetables and crisp chickpeas over quinoa with tahini, feta and pomegranate.

items.raw: 2 cups cooked quinoa or brown rice
1 cup chickpeas (drained, roasted with oil and paprika 20 min at 220°C)
items.note: drained, roasted with oil and paprika 20 min at 220°C

steps.text: Heat oven to 220°C. Toss vegetables with oil and spices. Spread on 2 trays (don't crowd).
Roast 30 minutes, tossing once, until deep golden at the edges.
In a small tray, toss chickpeas with 1 tbsp oil, 1 tsp paprika, salt. Roast 20 minutes alongside the veg.
Whisk tahini dressing, should be pourable but thick.
Build bowls: quinoa on the bottom. Arrange roasted veg, chickpeas, avocado, feta in coloured sections.
Drizzle tahini. Scatter pomegranate, herbs, pumpkin seeds.

notes: Don't crowd the trays. Two trays = roasted veg with char. One crowded tray = steamed veg.
Roasted chickpeas are the crunchy hero. Better than croutons.

title: Rogan Josh
summary: Lamb shoulder braised in yoghurt and Kashmiri chilli until it yields to a fork.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a heavy pot. Add the whole spices (cardamoms, cinnamon, cloves, bay) and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onions. Cook 12 minutes over medium until deep golden.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the ground coriander, Kashmiri chilli, fennel, asafoetida, and ground ginger. Toast 30 seconds.
Add the lamb. Stir to coat and seal, about 5 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat. Whisk the yogurt with a splash of water and stir it in gradually, this stops it splitting.
Return to low heat. Bring to a bare simmer, cover, and cook 90 minutes, stirring every 20 minutes. The lamb should yield to a fork.
Uncover and cook another 15 minutes if the sauce is thin. Season with salt.
Stir in the garam masala off the heat. Rest 10 minutes. Serve with rice and coriander.

notes: Kashmiri chilli for colour and warmth without heat, the dish is aromatic, not fiery.
Whisking the yogurt off the heat then adding gradually is the trick that stops curdling.

title: Saag Paneer
summary: Golden paneer in a vivid, gently spiced spinach sauce enriched with cream.

items.raw: 500g baby spinach (or a mix of spinach and mustard greens)
items.note: or a mix of spinach and mustard greens

steps.text: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds. Plunge into iced water immediately to lock in the colour.
Drain hard, then blitz with the green chillies to a smooth puree.
Fry the paneer cubes in 1 tbsp ghee over medium heat until golden on all sides. Lift out and rest on paper.
In the same pan, add the remaining ghee and cumin seeds. Once they sizzle, add the onion. Cook 8 minutes until golden.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, ground coriander, and turmeric. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in the spinach puree and a splash of water. Simmer 5 minutes, the colour should stay vivid green.
Add the cream and garam masala. Slip the paneer back in and warm through for 2 minutes.
Finish with salt and lemon juice. Serve with rice or naan.
