notes: Blanch and shock the spinach or the dish goes army-green. Vivid green is the prize.
Salt the paneer lightly before frying, bland paneer makes bland saag.

title: Salisbury Steak
summary: Tender beef patties simmered in a browned mushroom and onion gravy, served over mash.

steps.text: Soak the panko in milk for 5 minutes.
Combine the soaked panko, mince, egg, grated onion, Worcestershire, tomato paste, mustard, salt, and pepper. Mix briefly with your hands. Form into 4 oval patties.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Brown the patties 3 minutes a side. Lift out.
In the same pan, melt the butter. Add the mushrooms and cook 8 minutes until deeply browned. Add the onion; cook 5 minutes. Add garlic and thyme; cook 1 minute.
Sprinkle the flour over. Stir 1 minute.
Whisk in the stock. Add Worcestershire and mustard. Simmer 5 minutes until gravy thickens.
Return the patties and any juices. Spoon gravy over each. Simmer 6 minutes until cooked through.
Plate over mash, with peas alongside.

notes: Grated onion (not diced) keeps the patty moist without chunks.
It's a hamburger steak with gravy, embrace the diner vibe.

title: Salmon Nigiri
summary: Slices of cold, sashimi-grade salmon pressed onto hand-shaped vinegared rice.

items.raw: 200g sushi rice, rinsed and cooked as for vegetarian sushi
items.prep: rinsed and cooked as for vegetarian sushi

steps.text: Make seasoned sushi rice. Cool to body temperature.
Pull the salmon out of the fridge. Slice across the grain at a slight angle into pieces 5cm long, 2.5cm wide, 4mm thick. A really sharp knife is essential, wipe with a damp cloth between cuts.
Have a small bowl of water with a splash of rice vinegar nearby (tezu). Dip your hands lightly between each piece.
Take 25g of rice in your dipped hand. Squeeze gently to shape into a 5cm long oblong with rounded edges, firm enough to hold, loose enough to crumble in the mouth.
Place a small dab of wasabi on the centre of each rice oblong.
Drape a slice of salmon over each piece. Press the fish gently onto the rice with two fingers to seal.
Plate immediately. Serve with extra wasabi (don't mix into soy, Japanese custom), soy in a separate dish, and pickled ginger between bites.

notes: Sashimi-grade salmon only. Buy from a Japanese fish shop or reputable source.
Eat by dipping the fish-side (not rice-side) lightly in soy. Soy-soaked rice falls apart.
Uses raw fish. Not recommended during pregnancy or for anyone with a weakened immune system.

title: Salmon Poke
summary: Raw salmon dressed in soy, sesame and honey over sushi rice with avocado and edamame.

items.raw: Spicy mayo (3 tbsp Kewpie + 1 tbsp sriracha)

steps.text: Mix salmon marinade. Fold cubed salmon through. Rest 10 minutes.
Whisk spicy mayo.
Divide warm rice between 2 deep bowls.
Arrange salmon in the centre, then sections of avocado, cucumber, carrot, edamame, cabbage around.
Drizzle spicy mayo. Top with pickled ginger and furikake.

notes: Sashimi-grade only. Don't guess.
Warm rice, cold fish, room-temp veg. The temperature contrast is the dish.
Uses raw fish. Not recommended during pregnancy or for anyone with a weakened immune system.

title: Salmon Teriyaki
summary: Crisp-skinned salmon glazed in the pan with a reduced soy and mirin sauce.

steps.text: Combine the teriyaki ingredients in a small bowl. Stir to dissolve the sugar.
Pat the salmon completely dry. Season very lightly.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high. Place salmon skin-side-down. Press flat for 30 seconds with a spatula. Cook 5 minutes without moving, the skin should be crackling crisp.
Flip. Cook 2 minutes on the flesh side.

Pour the teriyaki sauce around the fillets, it will sizzle and start to reduce immediately. Tilt the pan and spoon the bubbling sauce constantly over the salmon for 90 seconds, until the sauce thickens to a syrup and glazes the fish.
Lift the salmon out. Pour any remaining sauce over the top.
Plate over rice with broccoli. Top with sesame and spring onion.

notes: Skin-side first, pressed flat. That's how you get the cracker-crisp skin.
Glaze in the pan at the end, don't marinate or you'll burn the sugar before the salmon cooks.

title: Samosas
summary: Hand-folded pastries of spiced potato and peas, fried slowly and served with chutneys.

items.raw: 1 tsp ajwain seeds (carom, optional but traditional)
500g floury potatoes, boiled and roughly mashed

steps.text: For the pastry: combine flour, salt, and ajwain. Rub in the ghee until it looks like coarse breadcrumbs. Add the warm water gradually and bring together into a firm dough. Knead 3 minutes. Wrap and rest 30 minutes.
For the filling: heat ghee, add cumin and coriander seeds. When they sizzle, add asafoetida, ginger, and chillies. Cook 30 seconds.
Add peas, ground coriander, garam masala, turmeric, and salt. Cook 3 minutes.
Tip in the mashed potato. Mix well. Add amchur, lemon, and coriander. Taste, it should be punchy. Cool completely.
Divide the dough into 8 balls. Roll each into a 16cm oval. Cut in half across the middle, you have 16 half-moons.
Take one half-moon. Fold one corner over to meet the cut edge, creating a cone. Brush the seam with water and press to seal.
Fill the cone two-thirds full. Pinch the open edge closed, pleating slightly. Press firmly.
Repeat with all the dough. Rest the filled samosas 10 minutes.

Heat oil to 160°C (a piece of dough should sizzle gently). Fry the samosas in batches for 8–10 minutes, turning, until deep golden and crisp all over. Low heat is key, high heat cooks the outside before the inside.
Drain on a rack. Serve hot with chutneys.

notes: Low and slow oil. High heat blisters and burns. Patience gives flaky shells.
Cool the filling. Hot filling steams the pastry from inside and tears it.

title: Satay Skewers
summary: Turmeric and lemongrass chicken skewers charred on the grill, with a coarse peanut sauce.

items.raw: 2 stalks lemongrass, white part only, finely chopped

steps.text: Blitz all marinade ingredients except the chicken into a coarse paste. Coat the chicken thoroughly. Rest at least 2 hours.
Soak 12 bamboo skewers in water for 30 minutes (or use metal). Thread 4–5 pieces of chicken onto each, packed tightly.
For the sauce: pulse the peanuts to a coarse meal, leave texture, not a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry the curry paste for 3 minutes until aromatic and the oil separates.
Add the coconut milk, peanuts, palm sugar, tamarind, fish sauce, and kecap manis. Simmer 8 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens to a dipping consistency. Loosen with water if needed.
Heat a grill plate or BBQ to high. Grill the skewers 3 minutes a side until deeply charred at the edges and just cooked through. Baste with leftover marinade once.
Serve hot with the warm peanut sauce, cucumber, onion, lime, and rice or roti.

notes: Char is the whole point. Get the grill screaming hot before the skewers go on.
Real satay sauce has texture, don't blend the peanuts smooth.

title: Schnitzel
summary: Thin veal escalopes fried in foaming butter until the crumb ripples and puffs.

items.raw: 4 veal escalopes (or pork loin steaks), pounded to 5mm

items.item: Boiled baby potatoes tossed with butter and parsley
items.raw: Boiled baby potatoes tossed with butter and parsley
Lingonberry jam or cranberry sauce (for Wiener style)
Chopped capers and anchovy (for Holstein style, optional)

steps.text: Pound the meat between cling film with a meat mallet until 5mm thin. Season both sides.
Set up three plates: flour, egg, breadcrumbs. Dredge each escalope in flour, dip in egg, then press into breadcrumbs. Don't pack the crumbs hard, they should sit loose to puff up in the pan.
Heat the butter and oil together in a wide heavy pan over medium-high heat until the butter foams.
Swim, don't fry, there should be enough fat for the crumbs to float and crisp. Add a schnitzel. Cook 2 minutes a side.
Tilt the pan and baste the schnitzel with the hot fat as it cooks, this is what makes the breadcrumb crust ripple and puff into that golden wave.
Lift onto a rack to drain. Repeat with the rest, topping up butter and oil as needed.
Serve immediately with lemon, parsley potatoes, and a dollop of jam or capers.

notes: Pound thin and even. A schnitzel should cook in 4 minutes total.
The bubbling, puffing breadcrumb crust comes from basting with hot fat, a real schnitzel-maker move.

title: Seafood Paella
summary: Saffron rice with prawns, mussels, clams and calamari, crisped underneath into socarrat.

items.raw: Large pinch of saffron, steeped in 2 tbsp hot water
300g clams, soaked in cold water 20 minutes

steps.text: In a wide shallow paella pan, heat the olive oil. Cook the onion and capsicum 8 minutes until soft. Add garlic; cook 1 minute.
Stir in both paprikas. Cook 30 seconds.
Add the blitzed tomato. Cook 5 minutes until darkened, this is the sofrito.
Add the rice and stir to coat. Toast 2 minutes.
Pour in the saffron water and hot stock. Add salt. Spread the rice evenly.
No stirring from here on. Simmer over medium heat for 12 minutes, the rice should be visible above the stock.
Nestle in the prawns, calamari, peas, and a few mussels and clams (the rest go on top). Cook 6 minutes.
Add the remaining mussels and clams on top, hinge-down so they open into the rice. Cook 4 more minutes until shells open.
Crank the heat for the final 1–2 minutes to develop the socarrat. Listen for crackling.
Off the heat, cover with foil and rest 5 minutes. Top with parsley. Serve from the pan with lemon.

notes: Discard any mussels or clams that don't open after cooking.
The socarrat (crisp rice on the bottom) is the badge of honour. Listen for the crackle, pull just before burn.

title: Seafood Pasta
summary: Linguine with mussels, clams, prawns and calamari in a garlic, wine and tomato broth.

steps.text: Optional but transformative: make a quick prawn-shell oil. Toast the prawn shells in 2 tbsp olive oil over medium heat for 4 minutes. Strain the oil; discard shells.
Cook the pasta in well-salted water until just shy of al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water; drain.
While the pasta cooks, heat the prawn-shell oil (or olive oil) in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli; sizzle 90 seconds, no colour.
Add the cherry tomatoes. Press with a wooden spoon to release juices. Cook 5 minutes.
Crank the heat. Add the mussels and clams. Pour in the wine. Cover with a lid for 4 minutes, they'll open into the broth.
Add the prawns and calamari. Cook 90 seconds.
Add the drained pasta with a splash of pasta water. Toss for 1 minute to bring it together.
Off the heat, fold in parsley, lemon zest, and juice. Crack pepper.
Plate in deep bowls so the broth has somewhere to go. Discard any unopened shells.

notes: No parmesan on seafood pasta. That's the rule in Italy.
Discard shells that don't open. Add them and you risk food poisoning.

title: Seafood Risotto
summary: Saffron risotto with mussels, clams, prawns and calamari, finished with butter and lemon.

steps.text: Warm the stock with cinnamon, saffron, and lemon peel. Keep hot.
In a wide pan, melt the butter with oil. Sweat onion 5 minutes. Add garlic; 1 minute.
Add the rice. Toast 2 minutes until edges look glassy.
Add wine. Stir until absorbed.
Add stock a ladle at a time, stirring gently, until the rice is 10 minutes in.
At 10 minutes, in another pan, sauté the prawns and calamari quickly in a bit of oil for 90 seconds. Set aside.
In the risotto pan, add the mussels and clams. Stir gently. Cover with a lid for 4 minutes, they'll open and release their juices into the risotto.
Continue adding stock for another 4 minutes until the rice is al dente.
Fold in the prawns and calamari with any juices.
Off the heat, mount with cold butter (no cheese, seafood rule). Fold in parsley and lemon zest. Season.
Rest 2 minutes. Plate, should spread like a wave on the plate.

notes: No parmesan in seafood risotto. Butter and lemon do the finishing.
Discard any unopened shells. Don't risk it.

title: Shakshuka
summary: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and capsicum sauce, finished with feta and herbs.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide ovenproof pan over medium heat. Add the onion and capsicum. Cook 8–10 minutes until soft and starting to caramelise at the edges.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprikas, and chilli flakes. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste and fry for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes, a splash of water, sugar, salt, and pepper. Simmer 10 minutes until thick and glossy.
Make four small wells in the sauce with the back of a spoon. Crack an egg into each. Season the eggs.
Reduce the heat to low and cover the pan loosely with a lid or foil. Cook 6–8 minutes, the whites should be just set but the yolks still runny. Check at 6 and judge.
Off the heat, scatter feta and herbs over the top. Bring the pan to the table with bread for mopping.

notes: A wider pan = thinner sauce = faster egg setting. Adjust cooking time by eye, not clock.
Add a handful of spinach to the sauce before the eggs for extra greens.

title: Shawarma
summary: Warm-spiced roast chicken thighs rolled in flatbread with tahini and pickled turnip.

steps.text: Combine all chicken marinade ingredients in a bowl with the thighs. Rest at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
Heat the oven to 220°C. Lay the thighs flat on a foil-lined tray. Roast 18–20 minutes until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice into thick strips.
Whisk the tahini sauce, start with the tahini and lemon, then drizzle in water while whisking. It will seize then loosen.
Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan.
Spread tahini on each flatbread. Layer in lettuce, tomato, cucumber, the chicken strips, pickled turnips, chillies, and toum if you have it. Roll tight.

notes: A whole spice rack in the marinade is the secret. Don't skimp on the warm spices (cinnamon, cardamom, cloves), they're what makes it shawarma.
For real char, finish under a grill for 2 minutes a side after roasting.

title: Shepherd’s Pie
summary: Lamb mince in a thick, herby gravy under a ridged crust of buttery mash.

items.raw: 1kg floury potatoes (e.g. Sebago), peeled and quartered

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in well-salted water until very tender, 18–20 minutes.
While they cook, brown the lamb in oil over high heat, really let it crust before stirring. Drain off excess fat.
Add the onion, carrot, and celery. Cook 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and flour. Cook 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 1 minute. Add the stock, Worcestershire, thyme, and rosemary. Simmer 15 minutes until thick and glossy.
Stir in the peas and season. Tip into a baking dish.
Drain the potatoes well. Mash with butter and warm milk until smooth. Season generously.
Spoon the mash over the lamb and rough up the surface with a fork, those peaks are where the crisp lives.
Bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until the top is deeply golden and the edges are bubbling.
Rest 5 minutes. Serve straight from the dish.

notes: Shepherd's = lamb. Cottage = beef. Get them mixed up at your peril.
A handful of grated cheddar on top before baking is non-traditional but excellent.

title: Shrimp Alfredo
summary: Fettuccine in a lemony parmesan cream sauce with garlic and chilli prawns.

steps.text: Cook pasta until just shy of al dente. Reserve pasta water; drain.
Pat prawns dry, season. Heat olive oil in a wide pan over high heat. Cook prawns with garlic and chilli flakes 90 seconds a side. Lift out.
In the same pan, melt butter over low heat. Cook garlic 30 seconds.
Add cream. Warm through, don't boil.
Off the heat, whisk in parmesan, nutmeg, lemon zest, pepper.
Tip pasta into sauce with a splash of pasta water. Toss to coat.
Fold in prawns. Plate. Top with parsley and extra parmesan.

notes: No parmesan on seafood pasta is the Italian rule. This is the American rule, parmesan goes in. Different dish, different rules.
Lemon zest is the secret upgrade over standard chicken alfredo.

title: Shrimp Fried Rice
summary: Day-old rice fried hard with prawns, egg and peas, glossed with soy.

items.raw: 4 cups cold cooked jasmine rice (day-old is ideal)

steps.text: Break up the cold rice with your fingers.
Mix the sauce in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over screaming-high heat. Add the prawns; stir-fry 90 seconds until just pink. Lift out.
Add another tbsp oil. Pour in the eggs. Let them set for 5 seconds, then scramble into rough curds. Lift out.
Last tbsp oil. Stir-fry the onion and carrot 2 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger; 30 seconds.
Add the cold rice. Spread across the wok and let sit 30 seconds to crisp. Then toss continuously for 2 minutes.
Return prawns, egg, and add peas. Pour the sauce around the edges. Toss for 60 seconds until every grain is glossy and brown.
Off the heat, fold in spring onions. Plate.

notes: Same rules as chicken fried rice: cold rice, hot wok, fast hands.
Prawns get cooked first then added back at the end, overcooked prawns are rubber.

title: Shrimp Pad Thai
summary: Rice noodles tossed with prawns, tamarind, egg, sprouts and peanuts.

steps.text: Soak the noodles in warm water for 20 minutes. Drain.
Mix the sauce ingredients. Taste, must balance salty, sour, sweet equally.
Heat a wok over high heat until smoking. Add 1 tbsp oil and the prawns. Stir-fry 90 seconds. Push to one side.
Add the second tbsp of oil and the garlic. Pour in the eggs. Let them set 5 seconds, then break into curds.
Add the drained noodles and the sauce. Toss continuously with tongs for 2 minutes, the noodles will soak up the sauce and turn glossy amber.
Throw in the spring onion, most of the sprouts, and most of the peanuts. Toss 30 seconds.
Plate. Top with reserved sprouts, peanuts, lime, coriander, chilli flakes.

notes: Tamarind paste varies in strength. Start with less and build.
High heat, wide wok, fast hands. Pad thai is a 90-second dish once it hits the wok.

title: Shrimp Scampi
summary: Linguine and prawns tossed in garlic, white wine, lemon and butter.

items.raw: 600g raw prawns, peeled and deveined (tails on for looks)

steps.text: Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water until just shy of al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, pat the prawns dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli flakes. Cook 90 seconds, sizzling, golden, not brown. Burnt garlic ruins the dish.
Turn the heat up. Add the prawns in a single layer. Cook 90 seconds a side until pink and curled.
Pour in the wine. Let it bubble for 1 minute to cook out the alcohol.
Add the drained pasta with a splash of pasta water. Toss vigorously.
Off the heat, add the remaining butter, lemon juice, zest, and parsley. Toss until the butter emulsifies into a glossy sauce.
Plate and finish with another scatter of parsley and pepper.

notes: Pasta water makes the sauce silky. Don't skip the reserved mug.
Sliced garlic, not minced, minced burns in this dish.

title: Shrimp Tacos
summary: Quick-charred spiced prawns in corn tortillas with avocado sauce and mango.

items.raw: 4 tbsp Greek yogurt or sour cream

items.item: shredded cabbage tossed with lime juice and salt
items.raw: 2 cups shredded cabbage tossed with lime juice and salt

steps.text: Toss prawns with oil, lime, garlic, and spices. Rest 15 minutes.
Blitz the avocado sauce ingredients until smooth. Loosen with water if needed.
Heat a heavy pan over high heat. Cook the prawns in a single layer for 90 seconds a side until pink and slightly charred.
Char the tortillas in a dry pan or over a flame.
Build: tortilla, cabbage, prawns, mango if using, jalapeños, avocado sauce, hot sauce, lime.

notes: High heat, short cook. Overcooked prawns = rubber.
Mango is the surprise hero, sweet against the smoky prawns.

title: Shrimp Tempura
summary: Prawns in a pale, lacy batter of ice-cold soda water, with a light dashi dipping sauce.

steps.text: Devein the prawns. Make 3 small shallow cuts on the underside of each, then pinch to straighten, stops them curling when fried.
For the dipping sauce: warm dashi, soy, and mirin. Cool slightly. Add daikon and ginger.

For the batter: keep everything ICE COLD until the moment you fry. Sift flour and cornflour. Whisk yolk with soda water and salt. Pour the wet over the dry and stir VERY briefly with chopsticks, lumps are correct. Overmixed batter is dense.
Heat oil to 180°C.
Pat prawns very dry. Dust each in cornflour, shake off, then dip in batter and lower into the hot oil.
Fry in batches for 90 seconds, the batter should puff into lacy white-ish coral, never deep brown.
Drain on a rack briefly.
Serve immediately with tentsuyu and lemon. Tempura waits for no one.

notes: Ice cold + barely mixed + hot oil. Three rules. Cheating any one ruins it.
Light golden, not brown. Tempura is pale and lacy, not crusty.

title: Sisig
summary: Boiled then crisped chopped pork, sharpened with calamansi and served sizzling with egg.

steps.text: Place the pork pieces in a large pot with onion, garlic, bay, peppercorns, and salt. Cover with water. Simmer 45 minutes until tender. Drain and cool.
Once cool, dry the pork hard with paper towel. Chop into very small dice (5mm). Roast on a tray at 220°C for 15 minutes until edges char. Or fry in batches in hot oil until crisp.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over high heat. Add the onion and cook 4 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, chilli, and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Tip in the chopped crisp pork. Toss to coat.
Add the soy sauce, calamansi juice, vinegar, sugar, and pepper. Toss to combine. The pork should be glossy and sizzling.
Off the heat, stir in the mayo, this adds creaminess that ties it together.
Tip onto a screaming-hot cast iron plate. Crack the egg over the top, it cooks on contact.
Top with crushed crackling and bird's eye chilli. Serve immediately with rice and extra calamansi.

notes: Cast iron must be HOT enough that the egg sizzles when it lands. That's the show.
Mayo in sisig is a beloved hack, adds the silky finish that pulls everything together.

title: Sloppy Joes
summary: Beef mince in a tangy, sweet tomato sauce spooned onto toasted buns.

items.item: soft burger buns or kaiser rolls
items.raw: 4 soft burger buns or kaiser rolls

steps.text: Brown the mince in oil over high heat for 6 minutes. Add the onion and capsicum; cook 6 minutes. Add the garlic; cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste; cook 2 minutes.
Add the ketchup, brown sugar, Worcestershire, mustard, vinegar, paprika, chilli powder, salt, and stock.
Simmer 12–15 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce is glossy and clings to the meat. It should be sloppy but not soupy.
Toast the buns butter-side-down in a dry pan.
Spoon a generous pile of mince onto each bun base. Top with pickles, jalapeños, and the bun top.
Serve with coleslaw and lots of napkins.

notes: Real sloppy joes have body, the sauce should coat a spoon, not drip off the bun.
Toasted buns are essential or the whole thing collapses.

title: Smash Burger
summary: Thin beef patties smashed onto a smoking pan for lacy edges, stacked two to a bun.

items.raw: 600g beef mince (80% lean / 20% fat, chuck is ideal)

steps.text: Mix the sauce. Refrigerate.
Divide the mince into 8 loose balls without compressing, don't shape patties yet.
Heat a flat steel skillet or heavy pan over screaming-high heat until smoking. Add the oil.

Slap 4 balls onto the hot surface, spaced apart. Using a sturdy spatula and a second flat object (or another spatula on top), SMASH each ball flat, really lean on it. The patty should be 3mm thin, 12cm wide, with ragged irregular edges.
Salt and pepper the tops. Cook 90 seconds without moving, the bottom develops a hard mahogany crust.
Flip. Lay a slice of cheese on each. Cook 30 seconds more.
While the meat cooks, toast the buttered buns alongside or in another pan.
On each bottom bun: sauce, lettuce, onion, then STACK 2 cheesy patties (the second one with cheese facing up), pickles, top bun.
Eat immediately while the cheese is still molten.

notes: A really hot surface and a really hard smash. The lacy charred edges are the whole point, that's the Maillard.
Double-stack the patties. Single smash patties are dry; doubles stay juicy.

title: Soba Noodles
summary: Chilled buckwheat noodles dipped into a cold dashi and soy tsuyu.

items.raw: 1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips

steps.text: Combine the dashi, soy, mirin, and sugar in a small pan. Bring to a simmer, stir to dissolve the sugar, then take off the heat and chill in the fridge, at least 30 minutes.
Bring a pot of unsalted water to a rolling boil (soba is salty in the dough, don't salt the water). Add the noodles. Cook per packet, usually 4–5 minutes.
Drain and rinse under very cold water, rubbing the noodles between your fingers to remove all the starch. They should feel squeaky clean.
Plate the noodles on a bamboo zaru (or any flat plate), let them drain.
Pour the cold tsuyu into individual dipping bowls. Each diner adds a dot of wasabi and spring onion to their bowl.
Top the noodles with nori strips and sesame.
To eat: pick up a small tangle of noodles with chopsticks, dip the bottom half in the sauce, slurp.

notes: Cold noodles, cold sauce. Soba is summer food in Japan.
Slurp without apology. It cools the noodle and aerates the flavour, both correct.

title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
summary: Spaghetti emulsified with gently sizzled garlic, olive oil, chilli and parsley.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Cook the spaghetti until just shy of al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water.

While pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a wide pan over very low heat. Add the sliced garlic. The garlic should sizzle slowly, not brown for 4 minutes. Aim for pale golden, not dark. Burned garlic ruins the dish.
Add chilli flakes. Toss 30 seconds.
Tip the drained pasta into the pan along with 4 tbsp of pasta water. Toss vigorously for 90 seconds, the starch from the water emulsifies with the oil into a glossy coat.
Off the heat, fold in parsley and parmesan. Add more pasta water if it looks oily/separated.
Plate. Crack pepper.

notes: Garlic golden, not brown. Burned garlic kills the dish.
Pasta water + emulsion. Toss like you mean it.

title: Spaghetti Bolognese
summary: A slow ragù with milk and wine, simmered until glossy and deeply savoury.

items.raw: 500g beef mince (or half beef, half pork)
150g pancetta or streaky bacon, finely chopped

steps.text: Warm the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the pancetta and cook until the fat renders and it starts to crisp, about 5 minutes.
Add the onion, carrot, and celery. Cook gently for 8–10 minutes until soft and sweet, stirring often. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Turn the heat up and add the mince. Break it apart with a wooden spoon and brown well, let it actually colour, don't just grey it. This step is where the flavour lives.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes until darkened. Pour in the wine, scrape the base, and let it reduce by half.

Add the tomatoes, milk, bay leaf, nutmeg, and a good pinch of salt. Bring to a bare simmer, half-cover with a lid, and cook on the lowest heat for 75–90 minutes, stirring every 15 or so. The sauce should be glossy and thick.

Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water until just shy of al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water, drain, and toss the pasta into the sauce with a splash of the water. Cook together for a minute to marry.
Serve in warm bowls topped with grated Parmesan and torn basil.

notes: The milk is not a typo, it tenderises the meat and rounds out the acidity.
Make it the day before if you can. It deepens overnight.

title: Spicy Beef Bowl
summary: Gochujang-glazed beef over rice with crunchy vegetables, kimchi and a jammy egg.

steps.text: Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Brown the mince for 5 minutes, breaking it up. Drain excess fat.
Add garlic and ginger; toss 30 seconds.
Stir in gochujang, soy, sugar, vinegar, sesame oil, chilli. Cook 2 minutes, the sauce thickens and glazes the beef.
Build each bowl: rice, glazed beef, cabbage, carrot, cucumber, half an egg, kimchi alongside.
Top with spring onion, sesame, and chilli oil.

notes: Korean-inspired beef bowl. Sweet, savoury, spicy, glossy.
A soft-boiled egg makes everything better. 7 minutes for a marbled jammy yolk.

title: Spicy Ramen
summary: A miso and gochujang broth over ramen, topped with jammy eggs and sizzled chilli oil.

items.item: portions fresh or dried ramen noodles
items.raw: 2 portions fresh or dried ramen noodles
4 slices roast pork or shredded chicken

steps.text: Heat the oil for the chilli base in a small pan until shimmering. Pour over the gochugaru, Sichuan flakes, garlic, and ginger in a heatproof bowl. It will bubble and smell incredible.
In a pot, combine the stock, shiitake, kombu, spring onion whites, garlic, and ginger. Simmer 20 minutes (don't boil, kombu turns bitter). Strain.
Return broth to the pot. Whisk in miso, soy, gochujang, mirin, and sesame oil.
Cook the noodles in a separate pot per packet. Drain.
Divide the noodles between two deep bowls. Pour the spicy broth over.
Top with two egg halves, pork, blanched bok choy, spring onion, sesame, nori. Spoon plenty of the chilli oil over the top, that's where the dish lives.

notes: Chilli oil over the top, not stirred in. The first bite should hit you with heat.
Soft-boiled egg with marbled yolk is the badge of honour. 7 minutes from fridge-cold.

title: Spicy Sausage Pasta
summary: Rigatoni in a tomato and cream sauce with crisp-edged spicy sausage and chilli.

items.raw: 500g spicy Italian sausage ('nduja or hot Italian), casings removed

steps.text: Brown the sausage in olive oil over high heat for 6 minutes, breaking it into chunks. The fat renders and crisps the edges.
Add onion. Cook 5 minutes.
Add garlic and chilli flakes. Toss 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomato paste; cook 2 minutes. Add wine; reduce 90 seconds.
Add tinned tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes until thick.
Cook pasta in well-salted water until just shy of al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water.
Stir cream into the sauce. Simmer 3 minutes, it goes a beautiful tomato-pink.
Drain pasta straight into the sauce. Toss with a splash of pasta water for 60 seconds.
Plate. Scatter parmesan and torn basil.

notes: Spicy sausage means spicy sausage. Don't use mild and try to add chilli later, the heat from the meat is different.
Pink sauce, also known as vodka sauce style. Cream + tomato = the magic.

title: Spicy Thai Noodles
summary: Rice noodles stir-fried with chilli, tamarind and fish sauce, finished with Thai basil.

items.raw: 1 tbsp sriracha or Thai chilli paste
300g flat rice noodles (or thick egg noodles)
2 bird's eye chillies, sliced (or to taste)
Crushed peanuts, lime wedges, coriander for serving

steps.text: Soak the rice noodles in hot water 8 minutes until pliable. Drain.
Whisk all sauce ingredients.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Cook the protein 2 minutes. Lift out.
Add the garlic and chillies. Sizzle 20 seconds.
Add carrot and capsicum. Stir-fry 90 seconds.
Add the drained noodles. Spread across the wok 30 seconds, then toss.
Pour the sauce around the edges. Toss for 60 seconds, glossy and clinging.
Return the protein. Add spring onions and bean sprouts. Toss 20 seconds.
Off the heat, fold in basil.
Plate. Top with peanuts, coriander, lime.

notes: Adjust heat with the chilli paste and bird's eye. Easy to dial up or down.
Basil at the end. Cooking basil dulls it.

title: Spring Rolls
summary: Fresh rice paper rolls of prawn, herbs and vermicelli with a peanut hoisin dip.

items.raw: 1/2 cup shredded cooked pork or chicken (optional)

items.item: Vietnamese mint or Thai basil if you have it
items.raw: Vietnamese mint or Thai basil if you have it
Garlic chives, in long pieces (optional but classic)
1 tbsp crushed roasted peanuts to garnish

steps.text: Pour boiling water over the vermicelli. Soak 4 minutes until just tender. Drain and rinse under cold water. Snip into shorter strands with scissors.
Set up a rolling station: a wide dish of warm (not hot) water, a damp clean tea towel on a board, and the fillings all arranged.
Dip one rice paper into the warm water for 5 seconds, it should still feel slightly stiff. It will continue softening as you work.
Lay flat on the tea towel. On the bottom third, lay 4 prawn halves cut-side-up in a row. Above them, place a small bundle of noodles, a few lettuce leaves torn small, carrot, cucumber, and herbs.
Fold the bottom over the filling. Fold the sides in. Roll up tightly, the prawns should show through the top.
Whisk the dipping sauce ingredients with the water until smooth. Top with crushed peanuts.
Cover finished rolls with damp paper towel so they don't dry out. Serve fresh, these don't keep.

notes: Warm water (not hot) and dip for 5 seconds only. The wrappers carry on softening on the bench.
Prawns cut-side-up on the bottom = they show pink through the wrapper. Looks better.

title: Stuffed Cabbage
summary: Cabbage leaves rolled around beef, pork and rice, baked slowly in sweet-sour tomato.

items.raw: 1 onion, finely diced and softened in butter
items.prep: finely diced and softened in butter

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Core the cabbage. Submerge whole and boil 4 minutes, then peel off the outer leaves. Continue boiling and peeling until you have 14 large pliable leaves. Trim the thick rib at the base of each leaf flat.
Combine all filling ingredients in a bowl. Mix briefly with your hands, don't overwork.
For the sauce: cook the onion in olive oil 6 minutes. Add garlic, paprika, and bay; cook 1 minute. Add passata, stock, sugar, and vinegar. Simmer 8 minutes. Season.
Lay a cabbage leaf flat. Place 2 tbsp filling at the stem end. Fold the sides over, then roll up tightly like a burrito.
Heat the oven to 170°C. Pour a third of the sauce in the base of a deep baking dish.
Pack the rolls seam-side-down in a single tight layer. Pour the remaining sauce over the top to cover.
Cover with foil and bake 75 minutes. Uncover and bake 15 more minutes.
Serve with a generous dollop of sour cream, dill, and bread.

notes: Trimming the thick stem flat (don't cut through) makes rolling easy. Don't skip.
Better the next day. Make ahead, reheat covered.

title: Stuffed Chicken Breast
summary: Chicken breast filled with spinach, feta and sun-dried tomato, seared then roasted.

items.raw: 200g baby spinach, wilted and chopped (squeeze out water)

steps.text: Mix all the stuffing ingredients.
Cut a deep horizontal pocket into each chicken breast, almost through to the other side.
Spoon a quarter of the stuffing into each pocket. Press the chicken closed. Secure with 2 toothpicks each.
Rub the outside of the chicken with oil, paprika, garlic powder, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Heat an oven-safe pan over medium-high. Sear the chicken 4 minutes a side until golden.
Transfer to a 200°C oven for 14 minutes (75°C internal).
Rest 5 minutes. Pull out toothpicks. Slice across the grain. Plate over roasted potatoes with salad.

notes: Squeeze the spinach dry. Wet spinach makes wet stuffing makes wet chicken.
Toothpicks hold the seal while it sears. Easy to remove.

title: Stuffed Eggplant
summary: Roasted eggplant filled with spiced lamb, topped with feta, yoghurt and pomegranate.

steps.text: Halve the eggplants lengthways. Score the flesh in a deep crosshatch (without cutting through the skin). Brush with oil, salt, and roast cut-side-up at 220°C for 25 minutes until soft and golden.
Scoop out half the flesh from each (leaving a 1cm shell). Chop the scooped flesh.
Brown the lamb in olive oil over high heat 5 minutes. Add onion; cook 5 minutes. Add garlic and all spices; cook 1 minute. Add tomato paste; cook 1 minute.
Add the chopped eggplant flesh and tinned tomato. Simmer 10 minutes. Stir in parsley. Season.
Pile the filling back into the eggplant shells. Top with feta and pine nuts.
Bake at 200°C for 15 minutes until the feta starts to colour.
Top each with a spoon of yogurt, pomegranate, and mint.

notes: Pre-roast the eggplant, half-cooked eggplant under filling stays bitter.
Pomegranate and yogurt on top transforms it, sweet, tangy, fresh against rich filling.

title: Stuffed Mushrooms
summary: Mushroom caps filled with bacon and cream cheese, baked under a buttery parmesan crumb.

items.raw: 20 large button or chestnut mushrooms, stems removed and chopped

steps.text: Heat oven to 200°C. Toss mushroom caps with oil, salt, pepper. Lay gill-side-up on a tray.
Render bacon in a dry pan 5 minutes. Add shallots; 3 minutes. Add chopped mushroom stems; 4 minutes until brown. Add garlic, thyme, chilli; 30 seconds.
Off heat, mix in cream cheese, parmesan, panko, parsley. Season.
Spoon filling into each mushroom cap, mounding.
Top with the buttery panko + parmesan crumb.
Bake 18 minutes until deeply golden and bubbling.
Rest 3 minutes. Serve hot.

notes: Cook the chopped stems back into the filling, waste nothing.
Buttery crumb top is the texture move. Don't skip.

title: Stuffed Peppers
summary: Capsicums filled with spiced mince, rice and feta, baked until soft and golden.

items.raw: 4 large capsicums (red or yellow), tops cut off and seeds removed
items.prep: tops cut off and seeds removed

items.item: Fresh basil or parsley to serve
items.raw: Fresh basil or parsley to serve

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Sit the capsicums upright in a baking dish.
Brown the mince in olive oil over high heat for 5 minutes. Add the onion; cook 5 minutes. Add garlic, cumin, paprika, and oregano; cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and tinned tomatoes. Simmer 8 minutes until thick.
Off the heat, fold in the cooked rice, feta, and parsley. Season heavily.
Spoon the filling into the capsicums, mounding the tops.
Top each with mozzarella and a drizzle of olive oil.
Pour 100ml water around the peppers in the dish (steams them tender).
Bake 40 minutes until the peppers are soft and slumped and the cheese is deep golden.
Rest 5 minutes before serving.

notes: A splash of water in the base of the dish is the trick to peppers that go soft instead of charring on the outside while staying raw within.
Leftover rice works perfectly, even better than freshly cooked.

title: Stuffed Shells
summary: Jumbo pasta shells filled with ricotta and spinach, baked in tomato sauce with mozzarella.

items.raw: 300g baby spinach, wilted and squeezed dry

steps.text: Cook shells in well-salted water until very al dente (per packet minus 2 minutes). Drain, lay on a tray with a touch of oil so they don't stick.
For sauce: warm olive oil and garlic 90 seconds. Add tomato paste, then passata, oregano, sugar. Simmer 12 minutes. Season.
Mix filling ingredients.
Heat oven to 200°C. Spread half the sauce in a baking dish.
Stuff each shell with a heaped spoon of filling. Lay open-side-up in the sauce.
Spoon the rest of the sauce over the shells. Top with mozzarella and parmesan.
Bake 22 minutes until bubbling and the cheese is deep golden.
Tear basil over. Rest 5 minutes.

notes: Under-cook the shells. They finish in the oven.
Squeeze the spinach hard. Wet spinach = wet filling = soggy shells.

title: Sunday Roast
summary: Roast beef with crisp potatoes, Yorkshire puddings and a red wine gravy.

items.raw: 1.5kg floury potatoes, peeled and in chunks
4 tbsp duck fat or beef dripping (or vegetable oil)

steps.text: Take the beef out of the fridge 1 hour before cooking. Pat dry. Rub with oil, mustard, garlic, thyme, salt, pepper.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 8 minutes. Drain and rough up in the colander, fluffy edges = crispy roast potatoes.
Heat the oven to 220°C. Sear the beef in a hot pan all over for 6 minutes until crusted.
Transfer to a roasting tray. Roast 20 minutes at 220°C, then drop to 180°C and roast another 35–40 minutes for medium-rare (50°C internal). Rest 20 minutes, non-negotiable.

While the beef rests: heat the duck fat in a roasting tray at 220°C until smoking. Add the parboiled potatoes carefully, they'll sizzle. Toss to coat. Roast 45 minutes, turning twice, until deep golden and crackling.
For Yorkshires: whisk flour, eggs, milk, salt to a smooth batter. Rest 30 minutes minimum.
Heat a 12-hole muffin tin with 1 tsp dripping in each hole at 220°C until smoking.
Carefully pour batter into each hole (it should sizzle). Bake 20 minutes, don't open the oven or they collapse. Wait for deep golden and risen.
For gravy: use the beef pan. Whisk flour into the fat, cook 2 minutes. Add wine, reduce. Add stock and any resting juices. Simmer 5 minutes. Strain.
Carve the beef across the grain. Plate with potatoes, Yorkshires, greens, gravy, and sauces.

notes: A Sunday roast is a project. Timing is everything, the chart in your head matters more than any single dish.
Cold pan, screaming-hot fat for the Yorkshires. They puff because of the temperature shock.

title: Sushi Rolls
summary: Hand-rolled maki with seasoned rice, salmon, cucumber and avocado.

items.raw: 1 cucumber, cut into long thin batons
200g sashimi-grade salmon, cut into long strips

steps.text: Rinse the rice under cold water until it runs clear, this takes 4 or 5 changes. Drain well.
Combine the rice and water in a saucepan with a tight lid. Bring to a boil, then reduce to the lowest heat and cook 12 minutes. Remove from heat and rest, lid on, for another 10 minutes.

Warm the vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small pan until dissolved. Spread the rice onto a wide tray and fold the vinegar through with a spatula, fanning to cool. Aim for body-warm, glossy, and slightly sticky.
Mix the mayo and sriracha if using.
Place a nori sheet shiny-side-down on a bamboo mat. Wet your hands and spread a thin, even layer of rice over the bottom two-thirds, pressing gently, leave a 2cm strip of bare nori at the top.
Lay a line of cucumber, avocado, and salmon across the rice, about a third up from the bottom. Add a thin streak of spicy mayo.
Lift the edge of the mat closest to you and roll forward, tucking the fillings tight under the rice. Squeeze gently to shape, then unroll the mat and seal the bare nori with a dab of water.
Wet a sharp knife. Cut the roll in half, then each half into three. Wipe the blade between cuts.
Serve with soy, ginger, and wasabi. Scatter sesame seeds on top.

notes: Sashimi-grade fish only for raw. Otherwise use cooked prawn, smoked salmon, or skip the fish for a veg roll.
Don't over-rice the nori. A thin layer rolls cleaner and tastes better.
Uses raw fish. Not recommended during pregnancy or for anyone with a weakened immune system.

title: Swedish Meatballs
summary: Small allspice-scented meatballs in a creamy gravy, with mash and lingonberry jam.

steps.text: Combine meatball ingredients (except oil). Mix briefly. Roll into 24 small meatballs (smaller than Italian).
Heat oil in a wide pan over medium-high. Brown the meatballs 5 minutes, turning, until golden all over. Lift out.
Drain excess fat. Melt the butter. Whisk in flour; cook 2 minutes for a pale roux.
Whisk in stock gradually. Add cream, mustard, Worcestershire. Simmer 4 minutes until smooth and silky.
Return meatballs. Simmer 8 minutes until cooked through.
Plate over mash. Scatter parsley. Spoon lingonberry on the side.

notes: Allspice and nutmeg are what makes them Swedish, not Italian.
Smaller meatballs = more surface area = more sauce per bite.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
summary: Double-fried pork tossed at the last moment in a glossy pineapple and vinegar sauce.

items.raw: 1 tbsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water
1 capsicum (red and green mix), in chunks

steps.text: Toss the pork with soy sauce and wine. Rest 15 minutes.
Whisk the sauce ingredients (except cornflour slurry) in a bowl.
Combine the cornflour and plain flour. Dip each pork piece into beaten egg, then dredge in the flour mixture, pressing hard so it sticks.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 170°C. Fry the pork in batches for 4 minutes until pale gold. Drain on a rack.
Crank the oil up to 190°C. Fry each batch a second time for 1 minute until deep golden and crisp. Drain.
In a wok, heat the oil. Add the garlic and ginger; sizzle 20 seconds.
Add the capsicum and onion. Stir-fry 90 seconds, keep them crunchy.
Pour in the sauce. Bring to a simmer. Stir in the cornflour slurry. Cook 30 seconds until glossy and thick enough to coat.
Add the pineapple and the fried pork. Toss for 30 seconds, coat everything but don't let the pork lose its crispness.
Tip onto a platter. Scatter sesame seeds. Serve immediately with rice.

notes: Double-fry the pork. First fry cooks; second fry crisps.
Toss at the very last second. The sauce makes the pork soggy fast.

title: Tagine
summary: Chicken braised gently with saffron, preserved lemon and green olives.

ingredientGroups.title: Chicken tagine with preserved lemon and olives

items.raw: Pinch of saffron, steeped in 2 tbsp hot water
1 preserved lemon, pulp scraped out, rind sliced

steps.text: In a heavy pot or tagine, brown the chicken in 2 tbsp olive oil over medium-high heat, skin-side first, for 5 minutes a side. Lift out.
Reduce the heat. Add the remaining oil. Cook the onions for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, and all the ground spices. Stir 1 minute.
Pour in the saffron water and stock. Return the chicken with any juices.
Tuck the preserved lemon rind and most of the olives around the chicken.
Cover and simmer on the lowest heat for 60 minutes. The chicken should be fall-off-the-bone tender, the sauce thick.
Lift the lid for the last 10 minutes if the sauce needs reducing.
Off the heat, scatter the remaining olives, coriander, and parsley. Season.
Serve over couscous with flatbread to mop up.

notes: Preserved lemon, find at any Middle Eastern grocer. The rind is what flavours the dish; the pulp can be added or discarded.
A tagine pot (clay with conical lid) is traditional but a heavy Dutch oven works fine.

title: Takoyaki
summary: Octopus batter balls turned in their wells until golden, with sauce and bonito.

steps.text: Whisk all batter ingredients into a thin, smooth liquid, it should be runnier than pancake batter.
Heat a takoyaki pan (cast iron with hemispherical wells) over high heat. Brush every well and the surface generously with oil.
Pour batter to fill each well plus a thin layer over the whole pan. Drop a piece of octopus into each well. Scatter spring onion, ginger, and tenkasu across the entire pan.
Cook 2 minutes, the edges of each well will set.

Using a skewer (or chopstick), cut the connecting batter between wells. Lift the cooked side up and into the well, rotating each ball 90 degrees so the raw batter pours down into the well to form the second half.
Continue turning every 30 seconds for 4 minutes, basting with extra batter, until each ball is round and deep golden all around.
Lift onto a plate, brush with takoyaki sauce, zigzag mayo on top, scatter bonito flakes (watch them dance) and aonori.
Eat immediately, the centre is molten. Take small bites or burn your tongue.

notes: You need a takoyaki pan. There's no real substitute, the wells are the whole technique.
Tenkasu (crispy tempura crumbs) add the irregular crunchy bits inside. Find them at a Japanese grocer or skip.

title: Tandoori Chicken
summary: Yoghurt-marinated chicken roasted hot and charred under the grill.

items.raw: 1.2kg bone-in chicken pieces (legs and thighs), skin removed

steps.text: Score each chicken piece deeply 3 times, this lets the marinade penetrate.
Combine all marinade ingredients into a thick paste. Coat the chicken thoroughly, working it into the cuts. Refrigerate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Heat the oven to 240°C with a rack in the top third. Line a tray with foil and set a rack inside.
Arrange the chicken on the rack with space between pieces. Roast for 25 minutes, turning once halfway, until the edges char and the juices run clear.
For real tandoori char, finish under a grill (broiler) for 2–3 minutes a side until you get blistered black spots. Watch it, it goes from charred to burnt fast.
Rest 5 minutes. Serve with lemon, raw onion rings, mint chutney, and warm bread.

notes: Kashmiri chilli is mild and brings the iconic red colour, not regular chilli powder.
Skinless because the marinade needs to touch the flesh. The yogurt does the tenderising.

title: Tapas Platter
summary: Patatas bravas and garlic prawns with jamón, manchego and olives for the table.

items.raw: 500g waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into 2cm cubes

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the potato cubes with olive oil, smoked paprika, and salt. Roast on a tray for 30 minutes until deeply golden.

For the brava sauce, warm the olive oil in a small pan over low heat. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds. Stir in the tomato paste, paprika, and cayenne. Cook 2 minutes. Add the vinegar and 2 tbsp water. Simmer 2 minutes. Cool and swirl through the aioli.
For the gambas: heat the olive oil in a small heavy pan with the garlic and chilli over low heat. The garlic should sizzle gently for 2 minutes, no colour, just perfume.
Turn the heat to high. Add the prawns. Toss for 90 seconds, splash in the sherry, and pull off the heat. Scatter parsley.

Build the platter: spread the hot potatoes on a board, dollop the brava sauce over them, pile the prawns at one end with the oil drizzled around. Arrange jamón, manchego, olives, quince, peppers, and bread around the edges.
Serve warm, with a glass of sherry or rioja.

notes: Tapas is about variety and pace. Don't try to time everything for one moment, let the platter unfold across the table.
Patatas bravas need to be properly crisp. Don't crowd the roasting tray.

title: Teriyaki Beef Bowl
summary: Thin beef glazed in teriyaki over rice with broccoli, carrot and cucumber.

items.raw: 400g beef sirloin or rump, thinly sliced
1 tsp cornflour mixed with 1 tbsp water

items.item: steamed broccoli or sugar snap peas
items.raw: 1 cup steamed broccoli or sugar snap peas

steps.text: Whisk all sauce ingredients except the cornflour slurry.
Heat oil in a wide pan over high heat. Add the beef in a single layer. Sear 1 minute, then toss for another 90 seconds. Cooked through and lightly caramelised.
Pour the sauce in. Let it bubble for 1 minute, then add the cornflour slurry. Toss for 30 seconds until the sauce thickens and glazes the beef.
Mound rice in each bowl. Top with broccoli, carrot, cucumber, and the glazed beef.
Drizzle any remaining sauce over the top. Scatter sesame, spring onion, and pickled ginger.

notes: Build the bowl, don't mix it. Each component should be distinct visually.
Thin-sliced beef cooks in 2 minutes total. Don't walk away.

title: Teriyaki Chicken Bowl
summary: Crisp-skinned, pan-glazed teriyaki chicken over rice with fresh vegetables and avocado.

steps.text: Pat chicken dry. Season lightly. Heat oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high. Place chicken skin-side-down. Press flat and cook 7 minutes until the skin is crackling crisp. Flip and cook 4 more minutes.
Combine the sauce ingredients in a small bowl.
Drain excess fat from the pan. Pour in the sauce, it will bubble immediately. Baste the chicken constantly with the bubbling sauce for 2 minutes until thick and glossy.
Rest 2 minutes, then slice.
Build each bowl: rice on the bottom, broccoli, carrot, cucumber, avocado around one side, sliced glazed chicken on the other. Top with egg. Drizzle remaining pan sauce.
Scatter sesame, spring onion, pickled ginger.

notes: Skin-side-down longer than you think. That crackling skin is the dish.
Same chicken as Salmon Teriyaki technique, pan-glazed at the end, not marinated.

title: Teriyaki Pork
summary: Seared and roasted pork tenderloin, sliced and glossed in a pan-reduced teriyaki.

steps.text: Whisk the glaze ingredients.
Season the pork. Heat oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Brown the pork tenderloin on all sides, about 6 minutes total.
Transfer to a 200°C oven for 12 minutes (medium, 63°C internal).
Lift the pork to a board. Rest 5 minutes.
Place the pan back on the stove. Pour in the glaze. Bring to a vigorous simmer and reduce 3 minutes until syrupy.
Slice the pork into 1cm rounds. Return briefly to the pan; spoon glaze over each slice.
Plate over rice with steamed veg. Spoon any remaining glaze over. Top with sesame and spring onion.

notes: Tenderloin is the right cut, quick to cook, takes a glaze well.
Sear-roast then glaze in the pan. Don't pre-marinate, sugar burns in the oven.

title: Teriyaki Shrimp Bowl
summary: Quick-glazed teriyaki prawns over rice with broccoli, avocado and cucumber.

items.raw: 1 tsp cornflour mixed with 1 tbsp water

steps.text: Whisk soy, mirin, sake, sugar, ginger, and garlic.
Heat oil in a wide pan over high heat. Add prawns. Cook 90 seconds a side until just pink.
Pour in the sauce. It will bubble immediately. Add the cornflour slurry. Toss for 30 seconds until glossy and clinging.
Build bowls: rice on the bottom, then arrange prawns, broccoli, cucumber, avocado, carrot in sections.
Spoon any remaining glaze over. Scatter pickled ginger, sesame, spring onion.

notes: Quick glaze, quick toss. Overcooked prawns are rubber, fast or never.
Cornflour slurry gives the glaze that restaurant-glossy cling.

title: Teriyaki Tofu
summary: Crisp cornflour-dusted tofu tossed briefly in a glossy teriyaki glaze.

items.raw: 1 tsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water

steps.text: Press the tofu under a weight for 15 minutes wrapped in a tea towel. Dry tofu fries crisp; wet tofu steams sad.
Cube and toss with cornflour to coat lightly.

Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide non-stick pan over medium-high. Fry the tofu in a single layer, untouched, for 3 minutes per side, then turn to a third side for 1 minute. Cubes should be deep golden on at least 3 sides. Lift out.
Whisk the sauce ingredients (minus the slurry).
Pour the sauce into the pan. Bring to a bubble. Add the cornflour slurry and stir 30 seconds until glossy and syrupy.
Return the tofu. Toss for 1 minute to coat in glaze.
Plate over rice with veg. Top with sesame and spring onion.

notes: Press the tofu. Skipping ruins texture.
Toss the tofu in glaze AT THE END, briefly. Cooking it in the sauce too long softens the crust.

title: Thai Basil Chicken
summary: Knife-cut chicken stir-fried with garlic, chilli and holy basil, topped with a crisp egg.

items.raw: 400g chicken thigh, finely chopped (not minced, knife-cut texture is the dish)
items.note: not minced, knife-cut texture is the dish

items.raw: 2 cups Thai holy basil leaves (or sweet Thai basil)
Fried egg per person (sunny-side-up, crispy edges)
Prik nam pla (sliced chilli in fish sauce)

steps.text: In a mortar (or by hand with a knife), bash the garlic and chillies into a coarse paste. This bruising releases their oils.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the garlic-chilli paste and shallots. Stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant (don't brown).
Add the chicken. Press flat against the wok for 1 minute, then break up and stir-fry 2 more minutes until cooked.
Mix the oyster sauce, both soys, fish sauce, and sugar. Pour around the edges of the wok. Toss for 30 seconds.
Add the stock or water. Toss until the sauce reduces and clings, 30 seconds.
Throw in the basil. Toss for 5 seconds, just to wilt.
Plate over rice. Top with a crispy fried egg with runny yolk. Lime and prik nam pla on the side.

notes: Knife-cut chicken, not mince. Bigger texture, more flavour absorption.
Holy basil is the authentic herb. Sweet Thai basil works. Italian basil does not, different flavour entirely.

title: Thai Green Curry
summary: Chicken simmered in coconut milk with a paste fried until fragrant, finished with basil.

items.raw: 3–4 tbsp Thai green curry paste (good quality)

items.item: small Asian eggplant or 8 baby corn
items.raw: 1 small Asian eggplant or 8 baby corn, halved
100g snake beans or green beans, cut into 5cm pieces

steps.text: Open the coconut milk without shaking. Scoop the thick cream off the top, you should have 4–5 tablespoons.

Heat the coconut oil in a heavy pan over medium heat. Add the coconut cream and the curry paste. Fry, stirring constantly, for 3–4 minutes until the oil separates and the paste smells fragrant and toasty.
Add the chicken and stir to coat. Cook 3 minutes.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk and the stock. Add the fish sauce, sugar, and lime leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the eggplant. Simmer 8 minutes, then add the beans and cook another 4 minutes until tender but still bright.
Off the heat, stir in the chilli, basil, and lime juice. Taste, adjust with more fish sauce (salt), sugar (sweet), or lime (sour).
Serve over jasmine rice with extra lime.

notes: Frying the paste in coconut cream is the single most important step. Skip it and you get muddy curry.
Thai basil is different to Italian basil, it has an aniseed note. Substitute with regular basil only if you must.

title: Tikka Masala
summary: Charred yoghurt-marinated chicken finished in a smooth, creamy spiced tomato sauce.

steps.text: Marinate the chicken at least 2 hours.
Heat the oven to 220°C. Lay chicken on a foil-lined tray and roast 12 minutes until edges char. Or sear in a screaming-hot pan in batches. Set aside.
In a heavy pan, melt the ghee. Cook the onion 10 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute. Add the spices; toast 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the passata. Simmer 12 minutes until darkened and glossy.
Blend smooth for the classic restaurant texture (optional).
Stir in the cream, sugar, and fenugreek. Slip the charred chicken in with any juices. Simmer 5 minutes.
Season heavily. Serve with rice and naan, topped with coriander.

notes: Chicken tikka first, then sauce. Cooking raw chicken in the sauce gives you curry-chicken, not tikka masala.
Tikka masala is British-Indian fusion. It belongs on this list, half the country eats it weekly.

title: Tofu Buddha Bowl
summary: Glazed crisp tofu and roasted sweet potato over quinoa with a lemon tahini drizzle.

items.raw: 1 cup cooked quinoa or brown rice

items.item: chopped red cabbage tossed with vinegar and salt
items.raw: 1 cup chopped red cabbage tossed with vinegar and salt

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the sweet potato and broccoli with olive oil, paprika, and salt. Roast 22 minutes, tossing once, until charred at the edges.
Press the tofu (15 minutes under a weight). Toss with cornflour.
Pan-fry tofu in oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes per side, 3 sides, until crisp.
Off the heat, toss the tofu with soy sauce, maple syrup, and sesame oil, the residual heat glazes it.
Whisk the tahini drizzle, should be pourable but thick.
Build each bowl: quinoa on the bottom. Arrange roasted veg, tofu, carrot, cabbage, avocado in coloured wedges.
Drizzle with tahini sauce. Scatter sesame, pumpkin seeds, coriander.

notes: Press the tofu. Wet tofu = sad tofu, always.
Tahini drizzle ties everything together. Don't skip.

title: Tofu Stir Fry
summary: Pressed, cornflour-dusted tofu fried golden and tossed with vegetables in a hoisin glaze.

items.raw: 500g firm or extra-firm tofu, in 2cm cubes
1 tbsp cornflour mixed with 3 tbsp water

steps.text: Press the tofu: wrap in a tea towel, lay flat on a board with a weight on top for 15 minutes. Dry tofu fries crisp; wet tofu steams sad.
Toss the tofu cubes with cornflour to coat lightly.

Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide non-stick pan over medium-high. Fry the tofu in a single layer, untouched, for 3 minutes per side, then turn to a third side for 1 minute. The cubes should be deep golden on at least 3 sides. Lift onto a plate.
Whisk the soy, hoisin, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, and chilli flakes.
Add the last tbsp of oil to the pan. Stir-fry broccoli for 90 seconds. Add capsicum and mushrooms; cook 2 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger; toss 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce mix. Bring to a simmer. Add the cornflour slurry; stir 30 seconds until glossy.
Return the tofu and fold gently. Add spring onions.
Plate over rice. Top with sesame and chilli.

notes: Press the tofu. Skipping this step ruins the texture.
Cornflour dust before frying gives a crackly skin. Don't batter, just dust.

title: Tom Kha Gai
summary: Chicken simmered gently in coconut milk with galangal, lemongrass and lime leaves.

items.raw: 3 stalks lemongrass, bashed and in 5cm pieces

steps.text: In a pot, combine the stock, coconut milk, coconut cream, galangal, lemongrass, lime leaves, and garlic. Simmer gently for 10 minutes, don't boil hard or the coconut splits.
Add the chicken and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms, tomato, and chillies. Simmer 5 more minutes.
Off the heat, stir in fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime juice, always last so the flavours stay vivid.
Taste, should hit creamy, sour, sweet, salty, mildly spicy.
Top with coriander. Serve with rice.

notes: Tom kha = "boiled galangal", galangal not ginger if you can find it; the flavour is brighter and more piney.
Don't boil after the coconut goes in. Gentle simmer keeps the soup silky.

title: Tom Yum Soup
summary: A hot and sour lemongrass and galangal broth with prawns, mushrooms and lime.

items.raw: 3 stalks lemongrass, bashed and cut in 5cm pieces
2 tbsp Thai chilli paste in oil (nam prik pao)
400g raw prawns, peeled (heads on for flavour if possible)
items.note: heads on for flavour if possible

items.raw: 300g mushrooms (oyster, straw, or button), torn or sliced

steps.text: In a pot, combine stock, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, garlic, and chillies. Simmer 10 minutes, extract the aromatic oils.
Stir in the chilli paste. The broth should turn a vivid orange-red.
Add the mushrooms and tomato. Simmer 3 minutes.
Add the prawns. Simmer 90 seconds, until just pink.
Off the heat, stir in the fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime juice. Always last, heat kills the freshness.
Taste: should hit sour, salty, sweet, and spicy in equal measure. Adjust with lime, fish sauce, sugar, or chilli paste.
Ladle into bowls. Top with coriander. Serve hot with rice if you like.

notes: Don't eat the lemongrass or galangal pieces, they're for flavour. Fish them out or push to the side.
Balance over heat. Tom yum should sing on the tongue, not just burn.

title: Tortellini Alfredo
summary: Cheese tortellini in a quick butter, cream and parmesan sauce, ready in minutes.

steps.text: Cook the tortellini in well-salted water per packet, usually 3 minutes. Reserve a mug of pasta water; drain.
While they cook, melt butter in a wide pan over low heat. Add garlic; 30 seconds without colour.
Pour in cream. Warm through but do not boil.
Off the heat, whisk in parmesan gradually. Add nutmeg and pepper.
Tip the drained tortellini in. Toss gently. Splash in pasta water if sauce thickens too much.
Plate. Top with parsley and more parmesan.

notes: Off-heat cheese whisk. Hot cream + cheese = grainy.
15-minute weeknight winner. Fresh stuffed pasta is the move.

title: Tortilla Soup
summary: A spiced tomato and chicken broth with beans and corn, piled with crisp tortilla strips.

items.raw: 6 corn tortillas, cut into thin strips

steps.text: Toss tortilla strips with oil and salt. Bake at 200°C for 8 minutes until crisp. Set aside.
Cook onion and capsicum in oil 8 minutes. Add garlic, jalapeño, all spices, tomato paste. Cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and stock. Simmer 15 minutes.
Take 2 cups of soup out, blend, return, thickens the base.
Add shredded chicken, beans, and corn. Simmer 5 minutes. Finish with lime juice. Season heavily.
Ladle into bowls. Pile high with tortilla strips, then sour cream, avocado, cheese, coriander, jalapeño.

notes: Bake the strips, don't fry. Less mess, same crunch.
Pile toppings high, the contrast is the dish.

title: Tteokbokki
summary: Chewy rice cakes and fish cake simmered in a sticky, sweet and spicy gochujang sauce.

items.item: Sesame oil and sesame seeds to finish
items.raw: Sesame oil and sesame seeds to finish

steps.text: Soak the rice cakes in cold water for 10 minutes if they're refrigerated or dried; skip if fresh.
In a wide shallow pan, combine the stock, gochujang, gochugaru, soy, sugar, corn syrup, and garlic. Whisk to dissolve. Bring to a simmer.
Add the onion. Cook 2 minutes.
Add the rice cakes and fish cake. Simmer 8 minutes, stirring often. The sauce will thicken to a glossy red coat.
In the last 2 minutes, add the spring onions and boiled eggs if using.
Drizzle with sesame oil and scatter sesame seeds. Serve straight from the pan.

notes: Wide pan, not deep. The sauce needs to reduce, not boil like soup.
Sticky-sweet-spicy is the balance. Adjust sugar and gochujang to taste.

title: Tuna Melt
summary: A tangy tuna salad and cheddar toasted slowly in a buttered pan until molten.

items.raw: 2 × 185g tins good tuna in oil, drained
1 tbsp finely chopped pickles or capers
120g grated mature cheddar (or melty white cheese)

steps.text: Flake the tuna roughly in a bowl. Add mayo, celery, pickles, onion, mustard, lemon, chives, salt, and pepper. Mix gently, keep texture.
Spread the tuna mix thickly on 2 slices of bread. Top each with a heavy pile of cheese.
Top with the second slice. Butter the outside of each sandwich on both sides.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Lay the sandwiches in and weigh down lightly with a second pan or plate.
Cook 4 minutes a side, until deep golden and the cheese inside is fully melted into the tuna.
Rest 1 minute. Cut diagonally.

notes: Medium-low and patient. High heat burns the bread before the cheese melts.
Tuna in oil >> tuna in water. The fat carries the flavour.

title: Tuna Poke
summary: Soy and sesame-marinated raw tuna over warm sushi rice with avocado, edamame and cabbage.

items.raw: 1 tsp chilli oil (or pinch of chilli flakes)
2 cups warm sushi rice (rinsed, cooked, seasoned with 2 tbsp rice vinegar + 1 tbsp sugar + 1/2 tsp salt)
items.note: rinsed, cooked, seasoned with 2 tbsp rice vinegar + 1 tbsp sugar + 1/2 tsp salt

steps.text: Whisk the tuna marinade in a bowl. Fold the cubed tuna through. Rest 10 minutes.
Whisk the spicy mayo.
Divide warm rice into 2 deep bowls.
Arrange in coloured sections: tuna in the centre, then avocado, cucumber, edamame, cabbage around it.
Drizzle spicy mayo zigzag. Top with pickled ginger, spring onion greens, and furikake.
Mix at the table.

notes: Sashimi-grade tuna only. Buy from a reputable Japanese or fish shop.
Warm rice, cold fish, room-temp veg. The temperature contrast is the dish.
Uses raw fish. Not recommended during pregnancy or for anyone with a weakened immune system.

title: Turkey Burger
summary: A moist turkey patty with avocado mayonnaise, pickled onion and jalapeño.

items.raw: 700g turkey mince (with thigh fat if possible)
1 small onion, finely grated and squeezed dry

steps.text: Mix patty ingredients (except oil). Form into 4 patties, slightly wider than the bun, with a dimple in the centre (stops puffing).
Mash avocado mayo ingredients.
Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook patties 5 minutes a side until 75°C internal (turkey needs to be cooked through). Lay cheese on in the last minute if using.
Toast buns butter-side-down.
Build: bottom bun, avocado mayo, lettuce, tomato, patty, pickled onion, jalapeño, more avocado mayo, top bun.

notes: Turkey is lean. Grated onion + soaked panko keeps it moist; otherwise it's like eating cardboard.
Dimple the centre. Otherwise turkey patties puff into footballs.

title: Turkish Pide
summary: Boat-shaped flatbreads filled with spiced lamb and cheese, one crowned with a runny egg.

items.raw: Sumac, lemon, and parsley to serve

steps.text: Mix dough ingredients. Knead 8 minutes. Rise 1 hour.
Combine lamb topping ingredients. Mix briefly.
Heat the oven to 240°C with a pizza stone or heavy tray inside.
Divide the dough in 2. Roll each into a long oval, 30cm × 15cm.
Spread half the lamb down the centre of each, leaving a 3cm border. Sprinkle cheeses over the lamb.
Fold the long edges in over the topping, pinching the ends to make a boat shape. Twist or pinch the points sharply.
For one of them, crack an egg into the centre after baking 8 minutes (it cooks in the last few minutes, runny yolk).
Slide onto the hot stone. Bake 10–12 minutes total until the dough is deep golden and the lamb is sizzling.
Brush the crust with melted butter. Dust with sumac. Scatter parsley.
Cut across into 4cm slices. Serve with lemon.

notes: The boat shape isn't just visual, the raised crust catches juices that would otherwise drip away.
Egg in the centre at the end is a classic pide variant. Worth doing.

title: Udon Noodles
summary: Thick, chewy udon in a hot dashi, soy and mirin broth with fish cake and egg.

items.raw: 2 portions fresh udon noodles (frozen is excellent)

items.item: large pieces tempura prawn or thinly sliced beef
items.raw: 2 large pieces tempura prawn or thinly sliced beef (optional)

steps.text: Combine the dashi, soy, mirin, sake, and sugar in a pot. Bring to a simmer for 3 minutes, this is the kake broth. Keep hot.
Cook the udon in a separate pot of unsalted boiling water, fresh udon takes 1–2 minutes, frozen 2–3 minutes. Drain.
Divide the hot noodles into 2 large warm bowls. Pour over the broth, it should just cover.
Top each bowl with sliced fish cake, the egg (split), and any other proteins.
Scatter spring onion and sesame. Sprinkle shichimi for heat.
Eat with chopsticks for noodles and a wide spoon for broth. Slurp.

notes: Fresh udon (especially frozen Japanese udon) is far better than dried. They're thick, chewy, and silky.
A hot bowl is half the experience. Warm them in the oven or with hot water before pouring in the broth.

title: Vegetable Curry
summary: Sweet potato, cauliflower and chickpeas simmered in a spiced coconut sauce.

items.raw: 2 tbsp medium curry powder (or 1 tbsp garam masala + 1 tbsp Kashmiri chilli powder)
items.note: or 1 tbsp garam masala + 1 tbsp Kashmiri chilli powder

steps.text: Heat the oil. Cook onion 8 minutes until golden. Add garlic and ginger; 1 minute.
Add all the spices and tomato paste. Toast 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and stock. Add sweet potato and cauliflower. Simmer 15 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and capsicum. Simmer 8 more minutes until the veg are tender but holding shape.
Off the heat, fold in spinach (it wilts in residual heat) and lime juice. Season.
Top with coriander. Serve with rice or naan.

notes: Adaptable, swap any vegetable in season. Just keep firm veg in early, leafy at the end.
Coconut milk makes it creamy but not heavy. Great vegan curry without trying to be one.

title: Vegetable Lasagna
summary: Roasted eggplant, zucchini, capsicum and mushroom layered with spinach ricotta and tomato.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss eggplant, zucchini, and capsicum with oil and salt. Roast 25 minutes until soft and lightly charred. Cool. Slice capsicums.
Sauté mushrooms in olive oil over high heat 6 minutes until deep brown.
For tomato sauce: cook onion and garlic in oil 8 minutes. Add tomato paste; cook 2 minutes. Add passata, oregano, sugar, salt. Simmer 15 minutes.
For ricotta: mix ricotta with egg, parmesan, chopped wilted spinach, nutmeg, salt, pepper.
Heat the oven to 190°C.
Build: thin sauce on base, sheets, dollops of ricotta, roasted veg, mushrooms, sprinkle of mozzarella, more sauce. Repeat 3 times. Top layer: sheets, sauce, mozzarella, parmesan.
Bake 40 minutes covered with foil for the first 25 minutes, uncovered for the rest. Top should be deep golden.
Rest 20 minutes.

notes: Pre-roast the vegetables. Layering raw veg means watery lasagna.
Ricotta + egg + spinach creates the cohesion this needs without bechamel.

title: Vegetarian Sushi
summary: Maki rolls filled with crisp vegetables, pickled radish and glazed pan-fried tofu.

items.raw: 120g firm tofu, in batons, marinated in soy + mirin + sesame oil 15 minutes then pan-fried golden
items.prep: in batons, marinated in soy + mirin + sesame oil 15 minutes then pan-fried golden

steps.text: Rinse the rice 4–5 times until water runs clear. Drain.
Cook rice with water: bring to boil, reduce to lowest heat, cover, 12 minutes. Rest 10 minutes off the heat.
Warm vinegar, sugar, and salt to dissolve. Spread rice on a tray; fold the vinegar through with a spatula, fanning to cool.
Mix mayo with sriracha.
Place a nori sheet shiny-side-down on a bamboo mat. Wet your hands and spread a thin layer of rice over the bottom two-thirds, leaving a 2cm strip of bare nori at the top.
Lay a line of cucumber, avocado, carrot, tofu, and pickled radish across the rice, about a third up from the bottom. Streak with spicy mayo.
Lift the closest edge of the mat and roll forward, tucking tight. Squeeze gently to shape. Unroll the mat and seal the bare nori with a wet finger.
Wet a sharp knife. Cut the roll in half, then each half into three. Wipe blade between cuts.
Serve with soy, ginger, wasabi. Scatter sesame.

notes: Wet hands, sharp knife, light pressure. Mantra for any sushi roll.
Pickled radish (takuan) gives the umami hit that meat fillings would otherwise.

title: Veggie Burger
summary: Black bean, rice and walnut patties fried crisp and stacked with a tangy burger sauce.

items.raw: 1 × 400g tin black beans, drained and dried well
1 egg (or 1 tbsp flaxmeal + 3 tbsp water for vegan)
items.note: or 1 tbsp flaxmeal + 3 tbsp water for vegan

steps.text: Pat the black beans very dry, wet beans = mushy patties. Roast on a tray at 180°C for 8 minutes to dry further.
In a wide bowl, partially mash the black beans with a fork, leave half whole for texture.
Add rice, carrot, onion, garlic, oats, walnuts, soy, tomato paste, paprika, cumin, oregano, egg, salt, and pepper. Mix well. The mixture should hold together when squeezed.
Form into 4 thick patties. Refrigerate 15 minutes (they hold together better when cold).
Whisk the burger sauce. Toast the buns butter-side-down.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the patties 5 minutes a side until deeply golden and crisp. Lay a slice of cheese on each in the last minute if using.
Build: bottom bun, sauce, lettuce, tomato, patty, onion, pickles, sauce, top bun. Press together.

notes: Drying the beans is the secret. Wet beans make sad veggie burgers that fall apart.
Make a double batch and freeze raw, cook from frozen for an extra 2 minutes per side.

title: Veggie Stir Fry
summary: Crisp vegetables stir-fried in order over high heat, glossed with soy and oyster sauce.

items.raw: 1 tbsp cornflour mixed with 3 tbsp water

steps.text: Have every vegetable prepped and ready by the wok. Stir-frying happens fast.
Mix the soy, oyster, wine, sesame oil, and sugar in one bowl. The cornflour slurry in another.
Heat the wok over high heat until smoking. Add 1 tbsp oil. Toss in the broccoli; stir-fry 2 minutes. Splash in 2 tbsp water to steam through. Tip out.
Add the rest of the oil. Add the garlic, ginger, and chilli. Sizzle 20 seconds.
Add the carrot and capsicum. Toss for 60 seconds.
Add the mushrooms and sugar snaps. Toss 90 seconds.
Return the broccoli. Add the bok choy and spring onion. Toss 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce mix and the cornflour slurry. Toss for 30 seconds until glossy and coating.
Plate over rice. Scatter sesame.

notes: Mise en place is non-negotiable, once the wok is hot, there's no time to chop.
Vegetables in order of cook time: hardest first, softest last.

title: Veggie Tempura
summary: Sweet potato, pumpkin, eggplant and mushrooms in a light, crisp tempura batter.

items.raw: 1 small kabocha or pumpkin, sliced 5mm thick

steps.text: Warm the dipping sauce ingredients (except daikon). Cool. Stir in daikon.
Make the batter exactly as for shrimp tempura, ice cold, barely mixed, lumps OK.
Heat oil to 180°C.
Pat each vegetable dry. Dust in cornflour, shake off, dip in batter, lower into oil.
Fry in batches for 2–3 minutes (sweet potato and pumpkin need longer; mushrooms and beans 90 seconds).
Drain on a rack.
Serve immediately on a platter with the dipping sauce and lemon.

notes: Different vegetables fry for different times. Don't mix sweet potato and beans in the same batch.
A drizzle of grated ginger in the dipping sauce makes it sing.

title: Zucchini Noodles
summary: Salted zucchini ribbons tossed briefly with garlic, cherry tomato, lemon and basil.

steps.text: Spiralise the zucchinis (or use a peeler for ribbons). Toss with the 1 tsp salt and rest in a colander 10 minutes, draws out water, the key to non-soggy zoodles. Squeeze gently with your hands.
Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add garlic and chilli; sizzle 90 seconds without colour.
Add prawns or chicken if using. Cook through.
Add cherry tomatoes. Cook 3 minutes until they start to burst.
Add the zoodles. Toss for 90 SECONDS only, they cook fast and turn to mush after 3 minutes.
Off the heat, add lemon zest, juice, basil, parmesan. Toss.
Plate immediately. Crack pepper.

notes: Salt and drain the zoodles first. Skip this and you get watery soup.
90 seconds in the pan, no more. Zoodles should still have bite.
